r.b: Prevention was my goal more than repair. A year on this and the eleven lines between my brows haven't deepened while everything else about my skin got brighter. Desert climate demands a heavier moisturizer over top but that's normal here. Sunscreen every single morning, obviously.

Hormonal breakouts along my jaw have haunted me since my twenties. Started the 0.3 in March, moved to twice a week, then three times. There was a mild purge around week three, maybe five small spots, then everything calmed. It's mid June and my jawline is clear for the first time in years.

Half the scary reviews describe people using it nightly from day one. Don't do that and you'll likely be fine. My experience was two weeks of very mild dryness, then steadily improving texture and tone over four months. Minus one star because it's a splurge on a grad student budget.

Nose pores were my white whale. Twelve weeks of the 0.5, three to four nights a week, and they're noticeably tighter. Also cut down the oiliness on my forehead somehow. A rice grain amount covers my whole face so the tube lasts longer than you'd think.

Graduating from the 0.5 to the 1.0 after two years took no adjustment period at all. At 58 my skin looks better than it did at 50. The boswellia and bisabolol in the base seem to keep the strong stuff calm.

Took a bare-faced photo before starting because I never trust my own memory. Compared it at week ten and actually gasped. The lines by my mouth are shallower and my whole face looks more even. Used the 0.5 every other night with a ceramide cream on top.

r.t: Solid, once you find your rhythm
r.b: Needed two months of trial and error, every third night, then every other, buffered, unbuffered. Once the routine clicked, so did my skin. Texture is better, breakouts are rare now. Wish the box included honest guidance about the adjustment period instead of me learning from forums.

Honestly didn't expect much from an over the counter tube, but the 0.5 smoothed the horizontal lines on my forehead in about ten weeks. I use it after washing my face, wait twenty minutes, then a plain moisturizer. No purge, just a bit of dryness at the hairline early on.

Torn on this one. My texture is legitimately better and some sun spots faded, but my already dry skin has been thirsty ever since I started, no matter how I buffer. Constantly reapplying moisturizer through the day. If your skin runs dry, think hard before committing.

Someone at work asked if I'd been on vacation. Nope, just five months of this stuff every other night. Texture is smoother, the little bumps on my chin are gone, and my skin catches light differently now. Wear your SPF and start slow, that's the whole trick.

Bought this for myself and now half the tube disappears into my husband's routine. Can't even be mad, his razor bumps improved and my dark spots from a bad sunburn faded noticeably. We alternate nights out of necessity. Ordering two next time.

Everything changed at 54, my skin got thin, dull and crepey almost overnight. My derm suggested starting with the 0.3 twice a week and building up. Six months later I'm on the 0.5 nightly and the crepiness on my cheeks has genuinely improved. It never stung, which surprised me.

Week two was rough, not going to lie. Flakes around my nose, tightness at night. I dropped to every third night with a thick moisturizer on top and by week seven my texture looked airbrushed. The bisabolol in it seems to keep the sting down compared to other retinols I've tried. Pea sized amount, PM only, sunscreen religiously.

Jumped straight into the 1.0 because I'd used prescription strength before. Even so, it demanded respect the first month. Results are excellent, clearer skin and finer texture, but if this is your first retinol please start at 0.3. Knocking off a star for the price per millilitre.

Real retinol, real percentage, real adjustment period. My cheeks flaked for two weeks even at the 0.3 before things settled beautifully. Now at month five my skin looks fresher than it has in years. Four stars only because the initiation was rougher than advertised.

When the man who can't find the butter in the fridge says your skin looks smooth, something is working. Four months on the 0.5, applied to bone dry skin at night. Some flaking in week two, nothing since. My cheeks feel like they did a decade ago.

Love what it does for texture, but in January my dry skin needed a rich cream layered on top or I'd flake around the nose. Works beautifully three nights a week from spring through fall. Just plan your winter routine accordingly.

Old shallow scarring from my teens is finally softening after five months. It's not a magic eraser, the deeper ones are still there, but the overall texture is so much better that people assume I changed my diet or something. Started 0.3, now on 1.0 with no issues.

Three drugstore retinols sat unfinished in my drawer before this. The cream itself is silky, not greasy, and a small squeeze from the tube does my whole face. By month two the crosshatching on my cheeks was visibly finer. It's pricier, but I actually finish the tube, so the math works out.

Bought the 0.5 for fine lines at 34 and it ended up sorting out the constant congestion along my chin as a bonus. Took about six weeks and there was a rough patch around week three, but the payoff was worth it.

Learned the hard way that generous application equals a flaky, red weekend. Once I scaled back to an actual pea for my whole face, smooth sailing and genuinely smoother skin by month two. Four stars because the instructions could be way clearer for first timers.

My skin doctor actually nodded when I told her I moved to this from a stronger prescription I couldn't tolerate. She said pure retinol in a stable tube is a smart middle ground. Five months in, my sun damage looks lighter and my forehead is smoother. No complaints at all.

Contrary to reviews complaining about size, mine stretched five months using it three nights weekly. The results were gradual but definite, softer crow's feet and a more even tone. Only gripe is squeezing out the last two weeks worth takes scissors and determination.

At my age I figured texture was just permanent. Eight weeks with this, three nights a week, and the rough patches on my temples are gone. It spreads easily, sinks in within a couple minutes, and has basically no scent. My wife started using it too, so now we need two tubes.

Retinol and my reactive skin have never gotten along until this one. Whatever the bisabolol and boswellia are doing, it works. I started with the 0.3, twice a week, and I've had zero angry patches in four months. Lines around my eyes look softer and my cheeks aren't blotchy anymore.

Moisturizer, then a pea of the 0.3, then moisturizer again. Doing it that way I've had zero flaking on my dry skin since the second week, and the fine lines between my brows have softened noticeably after two months.

r.t: Cocktail it with your night cream
r.b: Mixing a pea of this into my evening cream was the trick my dry skin needed. Straight application left me tight and itchy, blended it's completely comfortable and still effective. Fine lines around my eyes softened by week nine. Would be five stars if it came with usage tips like that.

r.t: Effective but the tube is small
r.b: It works, no argument there. Forehead lines were softer by week six on the 0.5. But 30 ml at this price when a pea size is all you need still stings compared to drugstore options. Paying for the stability and the elegant base, I suppose.

Fine lines improved, I'll give it that, and my skin tone is more even. But the deep folds around my mouth haven't budged after seven months and that's what I bought it for. Probably unrealistic expectations on my part. Decent product, just know its limits.

Tretinoin made me peel for two years straight and I finally gave up. This is gentler but I'm seeing comparable smoothing without walking around with a red face. The boswellia must be doing some soothing work. Nightly on dry skin, moisturizer after, done.

r.t: Back on it after a break
r.b: Stopped for the summer thinking I didn't need it. Big mistake, my texture crept back by September. Restarted slowly, two nights a week, and within six weeks the smoothness returned. Lesson learned, this is a keeper. Buffering with moisturizer on dry weeks helps a lot.

r.t: Two nights a week is plenty
r.b: Everyone online insists on nightly use like it's a competition. My skin disagreed loudly. At twice a week I still got the smoothing and brightening by month three, minus the drama. Docking a star since even careful use leaves my chin a bit tight the next morning.

This is my third tube of the 1.0 and the crow's feet situation is genuinely better than it was a year ago. Texture is a thick cream that spreads thin. One warning, don't use it the night before a peel appointment. Learned that the hard way.

Patience is the price of admission here. One night a week for the first month felt pointless, but by month three my pores looked tighter and the fine lines under my eyes had softened. No irritation because I never rushed it. The tube keeps the retinol stable too, which I appreciate after a jar product died on me.

Sadly a fail for me. I did everything right, 0.3 strength, once weekly, sandwiched between moisturizer, and still ended up with stinging and a flare that took three weeks to calm. My rosacea-prone skin just can't do real retinol apparently. The cream itself feels nice, hence the second star.
Six weeks of the 0.5 at night did more for the lines around my eyes than a year of expensive peptide creams ever managed.

r.t: Cheek texture smoothed by week eight
r.b: Orange peel texture on my cheeks drove me nuts for years. This is the first thing that actually changed it. Week eight is when I noticed my sunscreen sitting flat instead of settling into every pore. Slight tingle the first few uses, gone now.

Fair warning, I purged for a solid two weeks on the 0.5. Almost quit. Glad I pushed through because month two onward my skin has been the clearest and smoothest it has been in years. Docking a star for the rough start, but that is retinol for you.

Speaking from experience here. Got lazy on a cottage weekend and earned new freckles that took months to fade. The product itself is excellent, my skin is smoother and brighter after four months. But retinol plus sun isn't a joke, so budget for a good SPF too.

r.t: Redness faded once I slowed down
r.b: Man, the first month was rough. Red patches on both cheeks that lasted days. I dropped to once a week and things eventually leveled out, and I do see mild smoothing now at month four. Just wish the gentle formula claims matched my actual experience.

r.t: Night one tingle, week six glow
r.b: First application tingled for about ten minutes and I braced for disaster. Never happened. By week six I had that lit-from-within thing people talk about, and by week twelve the lines around my mouth were softer. I keep the tube next to my toothbrush so I never forget.

After years of assuming retinol was off the table for me, the 0.3 proved otherwise. I buffer it over moisturizer and use it three nights a week. Mild tightness the first two weeks, nothing since, and my skin looks fresher overall. The tube keeps everything stable too, which matters with pure retinol.

r.t: Too much for my reactive skin
r.b: Even the 0.3 twice a week left me flaky around the mouth and slightly raw at the smile lines. I can only manage it once a week now, which means results are crawling. If your skin is reactive, budget months for the adjustment or look at gentler formats.

r.t: Tube beats a jar every time
r.b: Small thing, but I appreciate that this comes in a sealed aluminum tube instead of a jar so the retinol stays potent to the last squeeze. The 0.5 smoothed the bumpy texture on my cheeks in about a month. No fragrance, no sting, just quiet steady results.

You have to earn this one. Slow introduction, rich moisturizer, diligent SPF. Do all that and it repays you with the smoothest skin of your adult life. Skip steps and it will humble you fast. My dry skin needed the sandwich approach for the first month, then adjusted fully.

My derm started me on the 0.3 and moved me up to the 0.5 after two months. Pea sized amount at night, every third night to begin, and by week five the rough patches on my forehead were visibly smoother. Whatever the bisabolol is doing, I never got the angry redness other retinols gave me.

Two years of bakuchiol gave me maybe ten percent of what this gave me in three months. I was scared of real retinol because of my sensitive skin but the 0.3 with its calming bisabolol never flared me up. Smoother texture, fewer clogged pores, softer laugh lines.
Fifteen minutes before I do my makeup for any event, and my base has honestly never applied smoother than it does over this.
Solid mask, visible brightening by morning, but the eye holes sit tight against my eyes and I ended up trimming them bigger with scissors. Minor design gripe on an otherwise excellent product.

Most sheet masks slide around or gap at the nose but this one hugs properly and stays put the full twenty minutes. Loaded with essence without dripping down my neck. Skin looks lit from within for a couple of days after.

Pro tip, there's enough leftover essence in the pouch to do your neck and the backs of your hands. Mask itself sat well on my face, cooled nicely, and the green tea and aloe kept it from tingling. Glow lasted through the next day. My wife started stealing them so now we order more.
Results are lovely, my skin drinks up the essence and looks noticeably fresher. But the per-mask cost makes this a special occasion thing, not a habit. I save them for photos and presentations.
Long haul flights destroy my skin and one of these on landing night puts it back together. Cooling, calming, and the dull grey cast is gone by morning.

r.t: Bought a box for the bridal party
r.b: Handed these out to all five bridesmaids the night before the wedding and every single one asked where to buy them. Radiant, plump, zero irritation on anyone, including the bride with rosacea-prone skin.

Used one the night before corporate headshots. The vitamin C and arbutin serum is generous, almost dripping, and my skin looked lit and even the next morning without extra makeup. It's a splurge per sheet so I save them for occasions, but for occasions they earn it.
So much essence in the packet that it dripped onto my shirt collar before I got it positioned. Wear an old tee and lean back. The glow the next morning earned back the star it almost lost.
One mask a month alongside my regular ZO routine and my tone stays even through summer. The green tea and aloe keep it soothing rather than tingly, which I didn't expect from a brightening mask.

Spent too long at the pool, came home pink, and this mask with its aloe took the heat right out while still brightening. Keep a second one in the fridge for the next weekend. Feels like a mini facial.

My cheeks tingled the whole twenty minutes and stayed flushed for about an hour afterward. The brightness the next day was nice, but my sensitive skin and the vitamin C in this seem to disagree. Patch test first if you are reactive.

Straight from the packet it's a bit slidey and drips onto your collar. Ten minutes in the fridge fixes both problems and makes it gloriously cooling. The brightening effect is real but subtle after one use, more of a freshness than a transformation. Four stars, would be five at a friendlier price per mask.

Used one the morning of my sister's wedding and my skin photographed like I had eight hours of sleep instead of four. Twenty minutes, peel it off, pat in the leftover essence. The vitamin C and arbutin give a real glow, not just wetness.
The brightness is real but for me it fades within a day or two. Lovely as an event prep step, just do not expect one mask to change your skin long term. Four stars for honest, temporary radiance.
At 55 I was skeptical anything this small could matter, but a month of nightly use softened the vertical lines around my mouth enough that my daughter commented on it.

I'm on a plane every Monday and my skin used to fall apart by Thursday. Tossing this in my liquids bag fixed that. The ZCORE peptide and retinol combo kept working through hotel air conditioning and desert dryness. Texture on my chin smoothed out within a month of consistent use.
Week one was flaky, not going to sugarcoat it. Weeks two through four were the glowiest my skin has ever been. Buffer with moisturizer and start with twice a week.

A pea-sized amount covers my whole face, so this little tube went way further than expected. Started twice a week, now every other night. The crepey texture on my cheeks is visibly tighter and I only flaked for the first ten days. Perfect low-risk way to find out if 0.5% retinol suits you.

Don't let the size fool you, this is the real 0.5% formula and it means business. A rice grain amount covers my whole face. The orange peel texture on my cheeks improved within the month it lasted me.

Not a gentle introduction to retinol, this is the strong stuff in a small package. My dry skin needed it buffered over moisturizer and limited to every third night. Results came anyway, just budget adjustment time.

As a tester this did its job, I'm converted and buying the big tube. But gram for gram the mini costs noticeably more, so if you already know you tolerate retinol, skip straight to full size. Results were the same story everyone tells, brief flaking then noticeably smoother texture by week four.

r.t: Keeps my routine on the road
r.b: Half my month is hotels and this little tube means my retinol schedule never breaks. Same 0.5% formula, same results, just a size that survives carry-on rules.

r.t: Too aggressive for a vacation trial
r.b: Testing this on a two week trip was a mistake. My sensitive skin flaked and stung for most of the vacation photos. The formula is clearly effective but sample it at home first, not somewhere you want to look good.
Honestly every strong product should offer a trial format like this, and the retinol itself smoothed the crepey texture at my temples faster than expected.

We're away most summer weekends and my full-size products stay home. This mini means my retinol schedule doesn't take vacations anymore. Same formula, same slow flake-then-smooth arc, and the tube is small enough to forget it's in the bag until you need it.

Works exactly like the full size, which is the point, but even with a conservative amount mine lasted barely three weeks. Fine for a trial or a trip, frustrating as anything else. Price per gram is steep in this format.
Perfect for my two week Europe trip, sailed through security and kept my skin progress going. The ZCORE peptide formula feels identical to the full size my esthetician recommended.

Commitment issues with retinol? This solves them. I flaked lightly around the nose in week two, kept going, and by the time the tube ran out my forehead lines had clearly softened. Now I know the full size is worth it before spending big.

First retinol ever and the initial week was tingly and tight, almost sent it back. Glad I stuck it out because week three onward my skin looked fresher than it has in years. Just wish the tube came with clearer ramp-up instructions for beginners.

r.t: Cap worked loose in my bag
r.b: Product itself is excellent, my texture improved in three weeks of use. One star off because the cap loosened inside my toiletry bag on a flight and I lost a good quarter of the tube to my makeup pouch.

Grabbed the travel size to see if I could handle 0.5% retinol before dropping full-size money. Three weeks was exactly enough to know. Some dryness in week one, then the smoothest cheeks I've had in years. Full size ordered.

It's whipped and plush and sinks in without grease. I was using a separate retinol and moisturizer and this replaced both. Ten weeks in, the rough patches on my chin are gone and my makeup sits better. One jar lasted me just shy of three months.
Nothing flashy, it just works, and three jars in my texture and tone are the best they have been this decade.

r.t: Congestion city for my oily skin
r.b: I know it's marketed as hydrating but nobody warned my oily skin. Within two weeks I had little closed bumps across my forehead. Texture is beautiful and I get why dry skinned people rave, it's just the wrong tool for my face. Gave mine to my mom who loves it.

Post breakout marks used to sit on my cheeks for months. With this, they fade in weeks, I assume the vitamin C plus gentle retinol combo deserves the credit. It's rich but hasn't clogged me once. My skin looks like I drink more water than I actually do.

As a night cream it is lovely, rich without being greasy. But after two full months I can't honestly say the retinol side has done much. If you want visible correction, this is probably too polite. If you want comfort with a hint of ambition, fine.

Took a good ten weeks before I saw the tone improvement everyone talks about. It's a lovely cream from night one though, so the wait isn't painful. Just don't expect the mirror to change in a month. Price feels fair for a three month jar.

Started my retinol journey here on my derm's advice and couldn't have asked for an easier ramp. No purge, no peeling, just gradually fresher looking skin over about eight weeks. Will graduate to something stronger eventually but this earned its spot.

Third jar and my wife and I now share it, which is its own problem. Fine lines around my mouth softened months ago and stayed that way. It smells like nothing, feels like velvet, and hasn't stopped working. We just budget for two jars now.

This flips the usual order, it feels like a rich night cream that happens to carry retinol. My dry skin drinks it up and I still get the gradual smoothing, my cheeks look more even after two months. No peeling, not even around my nose.
Every other retinol has sent my skin into revolt within a week. Four months on this and not one flake, but the texture change is real. Whatever ratio of retinol to ectoin they landed on, it is right.
Minus thirty outside and my face isn't cracking for once. Rich enough for prairie winters but the retinol keeps working on tone underneath. Two birds, one creme.

Furnace season usually leaves my face tight and dull no matter what I layer on. Not this year. My skin stayed soft through the cold snap and I still got the retinol payoff, a slight glow by week six and smoother cheeks by eight. It's earned permanent counter space.

The creme itself is a five. My gripe is putting retinol and vitamin C in an open jar where light and air get at them every night. Give me an airless pump and I'll hand over the fifth star. Scooping with a spatula in the meantime.

Being honest, my deeper lines haven't changed after four months. What did change is everything else, hydration, smoothness, the blotchy patches on my cheeks. If you want heavy lifting on wrinkles go stronger, but as a comfortable nightly driver this earns its spot.
I alternate this with a 1% retinol, using this on recovery nights, and the combination keeps my skin progressing without ever tipping into irritation. Creamy but sinks in within a minute.

I patch tested for a week because retinol usually sets my face on fire. Nothing. Slowly worked up to nightly and my skin is smoother and calmer than it's been in years. Whatever buffering the polyglutamic acid does, it works for reactive skin like mine.
Feels like a plain rich moisturizer going on, no scent, no sting, but the vitamin C and retinol are clearly doing background work because my tone has evened out noticeably since May.

From fall through spring this is wonderful, hydrating with just enough retinol to keep my skin smooth. In July it sits heavy and I switch to something lighter. If you're oily or it's humid where you live, consider it a seasonal product. Docking one star for summer.

r.t: Second half of the jar went off
r.b: By the halfway point the creme had turned noticeably yellow and the texture went thin. Retinol and vitamin C do not belong in a jar, and at this price the packaging feels like a design failure. The first six weeks were genuinely good, which makes it more frustrating.

The polyglutamic acid in this is no joke. I wake up with my face feeling bouncy and soft, and after two months the sun spots on my cheekbones have faded a shade. It smells like nothing, which I appreciate.

Nothing about this cream is dramatic and that's why it works. I've used it nightly since winter, no irritation, and my skin tone has evened out enough that people assume I've had something done. The ectoin keeps it comfortable even after hockey nights in cold rinks.
Sixty-four year old skin finds most retinols too much and most moisturizers too little. This one threads the needle. Softer lines, less crepe on my cheeks, and comfortable every single night.

Gentlest retinol product I have used. The ectoin and polyglutamic acid keep it cushiony, so I get the smoothing benefits with none of the flaking my skin usually stages in protest. I use it straight, no buffering, four nights a week.

Over my usual moisturizer it rolled up into little bits within the hour, every single morning I tried. On bare skin it behaves fine, so it now lives in my gym bag for body use only. Effective sun protection, fussy about what sits under it.

Two league games back to back on turf that radiates heat, and this stays put through all of it. No white streaks in game photos. It layers over my morning moisturizer without pilling as long as I wait a few minutes. Tube number four just arrived.

High altitude sun is brutal and most water resistant sunscreens clog my pores within days. Two months into this one, clear skin and zero burns. It goes on white for a second then disappears on my light-medium skin.

Fragrance-free doesn't mean smell-free, there's a mild lab-lotion scent for a few minutes. That's my only note. Marathon training through June, ninety minute long runs, zero burn and zero eye sting. Rubs in white then vanishes. I'd buy it again without hesitation, just being thorough.

Coaching outdoor practices four days a week since April. One application before warmup lasts the session, even in rain. It doesn't sweat into my eyes when I'm running drills, which retired the drugstore stuff for good. The 9% zinc formula sits comfortably even on humid days.
Four hour rides with sweat pouring and my face is still protected at the end. Sensitive skin here and the zinc base has never caused redness. Slight sheen at first, gone in ten minutes.

Landscaping my sloped yard means full sun every weekend from May on. This goes on my neck, ears, and forearms and outlasts the sweat. No rash, no clogged pores on my back where lotion usually wrecks me. The vitamin E might be why my skin doesn't feel leathery after.

Retired and outdoors most of the day, morning garden then afternoon pickleball. One generous layer at 9am is still working at 2pm unless I've been sweating buckets, in which case I top up. At 67 my skin is thin and fussy, and this neither stings nor sits in my lines.
Three sets in April heat here is a real stress test and it passed. No eye sting at match point, no white streaks in photos afterward.

Once it sets at the trailhead it doesn't make my hands slick, which matters when you're belaying. Full days on south-facing rock and no burn on my neck or ears. Unscented enough that it doesn't attract bugs, or at least no more than usual.
Great for ski days, doesn't fail in wind or sweat. Just know there is a ten minute greasy phase after applying where you don't want to touch anything. Once it sets, it is matte enough.
Cottage season tested it hard, fishing to roofing to dock repairs, and I never burned once all summer.

Bought it for a single hiking trip and it performed, no burn above the treeline. For daily city wear it's too much, thick to spread and my face feels coated. That's my fault more than the product's, but I'd steer everyday users to the lighter EltaMD lines. It suits actual sport.

Grain truck windows don't block much and August fieldwork is brutal. Neck, forearms, face, every morning, and I've stayed burn-free through two harvests now. Doesn't turn gritty with dust the way thicker creams do. My dad's using it too and he's the hardest sell alive.

Protection is beyond question, I stack firewood shirtless in August and stay pale as ever. Just let it set before dressing, it left faint white smears on a black tee when I rushed. Ten minutes and then nothing budges it, sweat included.

Applied at the first tee, reapplied at the turn, finished the round with zero burn on a cloudless August day. It doesn't leave my hands so slick that I can't grip a club, which matters more than people think.

Every Saturday on the board, two hours minimum, often falling in. This is the only SPF where I come home the same shade I left. It spreads easily over damp skin too, which is handy when you're reapplying on a dock. My husband with sensitive skin borrows it constantly.

r.t: Tube empties fast on full body
r.b: For the face it is perfect. For two adults doing yard work and swimming, the standard tube barely lasts two weekends. Wish I had known about the larger size sooner because the per-use cost adds up.

Weekends on Okanagan Lake all summer. It holds through wakeboard sets and towel-offs better than anything we've tried, and the whole boat crew now uses it. Doesn't sting when lake water splashes your face. Only knock is the tube gets slippery to open with wet hands, hence four stars.

Protection is genuinely excellent and it stays put through spin class. On my deeper skin tone there is a faint grey cast for the first while though. I work it in hard and it mostly settles, but photos right after application aren't flattering.

That strip of skin between glove and jacket cuff used to fry every July. Now I do wrists, neck, and face before every ride. It doesn't run when you sweat inside a helmet, which I learned to appreciate in traffic on a 32 degree day. Great stuff.

Trained for a 3k lake swim all July wearing this. Eighty minutes water resistant is accurate in my experience, I reapplied on shore breaks and never burned my shoulders or neck. It rubs in quicker than most water-resistant formulas and doesn't leave my goggles filmy.

In and out of the ocean all afternoon and it held on exactly like the 80 minute water resistance claims. I use it on the kids too, no complaints about stinging, and the tube lives in our beach bag all summer.

r.t: No sting on sweaty trail runs
r.b: Two hour trail runs in July and this has never once migrated into my eyes. That alone puts it ahead of everything else I've tried. Rubs in fully in about a minute and my hairline doesn't break out.

Dawn patrol twice a week and this holds through a two hour session, saltwater and all. Light enough that I can shower after and go straight to work without feeling greasy or stripped. Six tubes in, zero burns.

On the water by 6am, racing till mid-afternoon. This is the first season my face didn't end up with sunglass lines burned in. Holds through splash and sweat, doesn't grease up my grip on the oars. Our whole boat club buys it now.

Kept my arms and legs burn-free through softball season, no complaints there. On my face it clogged me up within a week, small bumps along my jaw. Acne-prone folks might keep this below the neck. It's staying in my bag but only for body use, hence the middle rating.
On the pitch four evenings a week from May onward. Sweat, sun, no burn, no greasy drip. The vitamin E in it seems to keep my skin from feeling stripped after long days outside.

Handles Tucson spring sun without flinching, and I'm outside for work half the day. The tube is just bulky for a pocket, so it stays in the truck and I sometimes skip reapplying. That's on me, but a slimmer format would earn the fifth star. Skin-wise, flawless.

Never thought a hydrator would show up on my forehead first, but that's where I noticed it. The horizontal lines look shallower and the skin feels smooth and dense instead of thin. I'm 61 and use it under a night cream. A month in and I'm impressed.

r.t: Two pumps, full face and neck
r.b: Honestly surprised how far this goes. Two pumps covers my face and neck with a bit left for the backs of my hands. It layers cleanly under moisturizer at night and my skin has that rested look even after bad sleep. Been through two bottles since winter.

There's a faintly tacky finish for the first few minutes, which bugs me when I'm rushing out the door. Once it settles, the hydration is honestly the best I've used, and my vitamin C layers over it without pilling. Minor gripe, strong recommend.

Flight crew here. Recycled cabin air used to leave my face like parchment by day three of a rotation. A pump of this morning and night and I land looking human. It's small enough for my liquids bag too. Genuinely the hardest working thing in my kit.
She asked what I had changed at my last appointment, before I said anything. That is the review. I pat one pump on damp skin morning and night.

I put this on after cleansing and it's gone before I've even capped the pump. No residue, no pilling under my mineral SPF, which is a miracle because everything pills under that stuff. Skin looks bouncy by mid afternoon instead of tight. Combination skin, 34, third bottle.

r.t: My whole routine is this and SPF
r.b: Guys, skincare doesn't have to be complicated. I wash my face, press this in, add sunscreen, done. Coworkers keep saying I look less tired and I sleep the same terrible five hours. The pump gives the same dose every time which my engineer brain appreciates.

r.t: Sat on top of my skin
r.b: The silicone-slip texture never fully absorbed on my oily skin, just formed a film that my SPF then slid around on. I can get comparable hydration from a basic HA serum at a third of the cost. Clearly works for others, didn't suit my skin type.

r.t: Bought it at my facial, no regrets
r.b: Usually I resist the post-facial upsell, but the sample they smoothed on felt different, cool and cushiony, and my skin stayed comfortable through a whole workday. Bought the full size on the way out. Two months later the lines on my cheeks look finer and I stand by the impulse.

Finished Accutane last fall and my skin stayed desert dry for months after. My dermatologist suggested a serious hyaluronic serum and this got mentioned by name. Within ten days the constant tight feeling eased off. It doesn't sting on raw patches either, which nothing else could claim.

Works exactly as promised, my skin drinks it up and fine dehydration lines look softer within a couple weeks. Four stars only because the price makes me wince every single time I reorder. If money were no object this would be a five.

r.t: Under my eyes stopped looking thirsty
r.b: Started dabbing a little under my eyes on a whim and that dry, crinkly look I'd get by 3 pm is gone. Rest of my face loves it too, but the undereye change is what sold my sister on her own bottle.
Foundation used to catch on the dry patches around my nose. One pump of this after cleansing and my base applies like my skin got resurfaced. Slight silky slip to the texture that makeup loves.

r.t: Finally hydration my oily skin tolerates
r.b: Every rich cream breaks me out, so I'd basically given up on hydration. This absorbs like water, zero grease, zero clogged pores in three months of use. My skin is less shiny now too, I think because it stopped overproducing oil to compensate. Who knew.
Exactly two pumps does face and neck, no waste, no guessing. Four months of daily use and the fine lines on my forehead are shallower in raking light. Understated product that earns its keep.

r.t: Absorbs before I finish brushing my teeth
r.b: Colorado winters plus forced air heating destroy my face every year. This is the first hydrator that actually holds the line. Two pumps at night under a basic cream and I wake up without that tight, papery feeling. The five types of hyaluronic acid thing sounded like marketing until I felt the difference.

Love the serum itself, my flaky forehead has been quiet for two months straight. But the pump starts sputtering and spitting air when the bottle gets low, and I know there's product left in there I can't reach. Fix the packaging and I'm a lifer.

Furnace air and minus twenty walks were destroying my face until I added this under my night cream. The five weights of hyaluronic acid aren't marketing fluff, the hydration genuinely lasts through the night.

Crepey cheeks arrived at 58 no matter what I layered on. Three weeks into this and the texture looks smoothed out, almost cushioned. It has a slippery gel feel that spreads a long way, so one pump does my whole face. A friend asked if I'd had something done.

No complaints about performance, my skin drinks it in and stays plump through Chicago winter wind. But the bottle is small and at this price I hesitate every repurchase. Four stars with a wince at checkout.

r.t: Needs a cream buddy in January
r.b: On its own this wasn't enough for a Chicago winter, my cheeks still got flaky by evening. Layered under a proper cream though, it's excellent, and come spring I could wear it solo. Just know it's a hydrating serum, not a heavy moisturizer replacement.

r.t: Wish the big size cost less
r.b: Really beautiful serum. My skin looks plumper and makeup applies smoother, no complaints on performance. I just burn through a bottle in about seven weeks using it morning and night, and reordering that often adds up. I've dropped to nights only to stretch it.
Noticeable bounce in my cheeks by the second week, and the crosshatch lines under my eyes have visibly relaxed. A little goes far, so the price per month is less scary than the sticker suggests.

r.t: The dry patch fix I needed
r.b: Flaky cheeks since my twenties, and this is the first thing that keeps them smooth for a full 24 hours.

After a visit, my daughter left her bottle behind and I borrowed it for a week. Ordered my own before she even asked for hers back. Skin looks dewy instead of dull, and at 66 that's not a small thing. We compare notes on our bottles now.

r.t: Nice, but so is plain HA
r.b: It's a lovely serum, silky, absorbs fast, never broke me out. My issue is I can't honestly say it outperformed the hyaluronic serum I was using at a third of the price. Maybe my oily skin just doesn't need this much hydration help. Three stars for value.

r.t: Little bumps and a lighter wallet
r.b: Two weeks in I developed a crop of tiny closed comedones along my jaw. Stopped using it, they cleared. Tried again a month later to be fair, same result. My acne-prone skin clearly disagrees with something in here, which stings at this price. Texture and pump were lovely, for what it's worth.

Tried it under three different sunscreens and two moisturizers over a month, and every combination balled up into rubbery crumbs by mid-morning. Waited between layers, used less, applied to damp skin, nothing helped. Returned it, disappointed given the hype.

r.t: Hormones dried me out, this helped
r.b: Perimenopause turned my formerly normal skin into a desert almost overnight. This was the first product that made a visible dent. Skin feels supple again, fine dehydration lines around my mouth have softened, and it plays well with the face cream my doctor has me on. Eight months of daily use now.

Nothing dramatic happened for the first month and I nearly wrote it off. Somewhere around week six I realized my skin looked consistently smoother in my shaving mirror. It's subtle, cumulative stuff, not an overnight trick. Knock a star off for the wait, keep it in the routine.

Layering this over my retinol has cut the tight, squeaky feeling to zero. It has a unique cushiony gel texture, almost like a serum and a primer had a baby, and it never stings even on freshly exfoliated skin.

Recommended by my dermatologist after a resurfacing treatment, and it kept the tight, hot feeling manageable through the whole recovery. Still using it a year later on sensitive skin with zero reactions.

The smoothing effect is immediate, my smile lines look softened within minutes of applying. What sold me is that it isn't just an instant trick. Two months in, my skin holds hydration all day instead of going tight by noon.
Repurchased without hesitation, which at this price tells you everything. Firmness along my jaw and under my chin has genuinely improved, and it plays nicely under makeup.

Started this in February with a June wedding as the deadline. By May my jaw and neck looked noticeably tighter in the dress fitting photos. The sodium DNA thing sounded like marketing nonsense but something in here works. Zero irritation the entire time.

Faithful morning and night use since February, and there might be slight firming at my jaw, or I might be talking myself into it. For this money I wanted certainty, not maybe. Texture and layering are faultless, results underwhelming so far.

r.t: Gentle firming my dry skin tolerates
r.b: Most firming products dry me out or tingle. This is the first that does neither. I layer it under my moisturizer every morning and by month three my cheeks had that bounce back when I smiled. Pump gives an exact dose every time, no waste.

No sting, no redness, which for me is rare. Firming is modest so far, twelve weeks in, mostly around my eyes and upper cheeks. I appreciate that it doesn't pill under my mineral sunscreen. Holding a star until I see what six months brings.

One for me, two for my parents. Dad's 68 and even he noticed his neck looked better by March. For myself, it keeps everything taut through long office weeks. The vitamin E in it seems to keep my winter flakiness away too.

I've cycled through a lot of peptide serums and most did nothing. This one showed changes around week ten, mostly along my jawline and the crepey patch on my neck. It's the only step my routine has kept for a full year.
Sits invisibly under moisturizer and SPF with no pilling, no residue, no scent. After about three months the skin along my cheekbones feels denser somehow, like it snaps back quicker.

The firming is real, my before and after photos agree. But this is a serious financial commitment for something you must use consistently for months. If the price were a third lower this would be an easy five.

I'm 61 and no serum reverses gravity, let's be honest, but after four months my cheeks look less deflated and my smile lines don't fold as deep. Goes on light, sinks in fast, plays fine under sunscreen. One pump covers face and neck if you're quick about it.

It absolutely does something. My skin feels springier and the shallow lines on my cheeks softened around week eight. But the price per bottle stings when you use it daily, and I ration pumps toward the end, which probably undercuts the results. Would be five stars at two thirds the cost.

Dramatic overnight changes don't happen at my age, but by month three my cheeks sit a little higher and the marionette area is softer. The sodium DNA and peptide combination seems gimmicky on paper and yet here we are.

Slots into an aggressive routine without adding any irritation. I use it every morning while my retinol handles nights, and the combination has my skin the firmest and calmest it has been in five years.

I've used it faithfully every morning since spring and I honestly can't say my face looks firmer. Hydration is nice and it layers well, but for this money I wanted more than a pleasant texture. Maybe my expectations were the problem. Finishing the bottle, not rebuying.
Between microneedling sessions my clinic suggested this, and the combination has kept my results going far longer than treatments alone used to. Light, watery-cream texture that vanishes in seconds.

Living in Arizona I refuse anything heavy. This absorbs in maybe twenty seconds and my oily skin never protests. Six months in and the loose bit under my chin has firmed up more than I expected. It quietly became the product I'd panic about running out of.

r.t: Camera sees it before you do
r.b: Confession, I was ready to call it a dud until I compared photos from June and September. The improvement along my jawline is obvious in pictures even though the mirror kept me guessing. Strange but true, and I am continuing.

Love how it wears under SPF and my forehead looks smoother after two months. Just wish the bottle were bigger, using it on face and neck like they recommend, I'm through it in six weeks. The last few pumps also sputter and spray sideways.
Skeptics should give it the full three months. That is how long it took me to believe, and now I won't be without it.

Kept sneaking pumps of my wife's bottle until she made me buy my own. Fair enough. My face just looks less tired and saggy, especially around the mouth. Absorbs fast enough that I don't feel like I'm wearing anything.

Purchased for my face and ended up loving it most for my neck. The crepey texture below my chin has smoothed out considerably since spring. One pump covers face and neck if you spread it while skin is slightly damp.

Ten weeks in I can see mild firming along my jaw, and my skin holds moisture better through the day. But temper expectations, this is a slow subtle helper, not a facelift in a pump. I'll finish the bottle and probably repurchase on sale.

r.t: Real results on a long timeline
r.b: You will need patience. Nothing happened for the first eight weeks and I nearly gave up. Somewhere in month three the firmness changes crept in. Four stars because the wait is real, even if the destination is worth it.

Been using it every morning for five months after my wife's derm suggested it for early sagging. Skin feels denser, like it has more spring when I press it. No smell, no residue, no drama. Expensive, yes, but a bottle lasts me nearly three months.

r.t: Jawline is back on the map
r.b: Ten weeks of morning and night use and the softening along my jaw has visibly tightened. Photos from my daughter's graduation confirmed it was not wishful thinking. It is a slow burn product, commit for the full season.

r.t: Stings a little, worth a lot
r.b: For the first month there was a brief tingle on application, maybe thirty seconds, then nothing. That's gone now and what's left is smoother, calmer looking skin and softer lines by my mouth. If your skin is reactive, start slow, but don't let the early sting scare you off.

Jumped to the full strength after a year on lower doses and within six weeks the deep lines across my forehead have visibly shallowed. It is strong, respect the adjustment period, but the results match the strength.

Kept borrowing pumps from my wife's bottle until she made me buy my own. Razor bumps along my jaw have mostly stopped and the creases across my forehead look shallower. Neither of us expected a night cream to become a marriage negotiation, yet here we are.

r.t: Love the cream, prime the pump twice
r.b: Cream itself is elegant, sinks in fast, no smell. My gripe is the airless pump needs a couple of presses after it sits a few days, and I've wasted product shooting past my hand onto the counter. Skin looks fresher after two months, so I forgive it. Mostly.

Ignored the temptation to use it nightly and stuck with every other night from the start. Zero irritation, and by month three my pores looked smaller and my skin caught the light better. Sometimes the slower road gets you there just fine.

The results are legit, softer lines around my eyes and brighter skin overall by month two. What keeps this at four stars is the cost per bottle when you're using it several nights a week. I ration it like fine whisky now, one pump, no waste.

Rare product that treats my adult acne and my early wrinkles at the same time without shredding my face. The PhytoShield antioxidants apparently help with irritation and I believe it, because I've had none.

Deep horizontal forehead lines have been my nemesis since 50. After roughly four months on the 0.5, they're shallower, and in soft light they nearly disappear. My skin also has a general firmness it didn't have before. Slow and steady, but it's genuinely working.

Dry skin here, and even the 0.25 pulled moisture out, so I buffer it between two layers of cream. Done that way it is excellent, forehead texture noticeably smoother since December. Just not a solo act for dry types.

r.t: Red and angry within a week
r.b: Even the lowest strength was too much for me. By day five my cheeks were red, hot, and flaking around my nostrils, and it took two weeks of bland moisturizer to settle things down. I know retinol has an adjustment period but I've tolerated other gentle formulas fine. Not for my reactive skin.

Went too high too fast and paid for it with two weeks of red, flaking, stinging skin. Entirely my error in strength selection, but I also wish the packaging warned more clearly about stepping up gradually. Back on the 0.25 and rebuilding slowly.

Performance wise I've got no notes, smoother skin, brighter tone, easy to use. The bottle just doesn't last long when you're on it four nights a week. I get about nine weeks per pump bottle. A larger size option would push this to five stars for me.

Terrified of retinol after all the horror stories, I started with the 0.25 twice a week. Four months later I'm at three nights weekly with zero peeling. Pores along my nose look tighter and my skin tone is more even. The niacinamide in it probably deserves some credit for keeping the peace.

Texture improved first, around week four my skin stopped feeling gritty under moisturizer. The stubborn tan spots on my cheekbones are taking longer but they're visibly lighter at the three month mark. Arizona sun did the damage, this is undoing it a little at a time. Sunscreen every day, obviously.
Retinol in a pump bottle that never lets air degrade it, take notes everyone else. Dispenses the same dose every night, and after four months my acne scars have softened at the edges.

Well made and it works, my skin tone is more even and the crow's feet are softer after a season of use. There are cheaper retinols that get you most of the way there though, so the value question is fair. The elegant formula is what you pay for.

r.t: My derm nodded at my last visit
r.b: Been on the 1.0 for about a year after working up from lower strengths elsewhere. At my annual skin check my dermatologist actually commented that my sun damage looked lighter. That never happens. It's strong, so respect it, buffer it, and don't use it the night before a peel.

r.t: Best retinol I have rotated through
r.b: Rotated through four brands in three years and this is the one staying on my shelf for good.

Whatever's left on my fingers goes on the backs of my hands, and after five months the sun spots there have faded noticeably. Face results are great too, smoother texture and fewer little bumps, but the hand thing is the bonus nobody told me about.

My chin has had rough, bumpy texture since my twenties. Six weeks of the 0.5 every other night and I keep catching myself touching it because it's actually smooth. Some dryness in week two, nothing a plain moisturizer couldn't handle. 45 years old, wish I'd started sooner.
The progression system is the smart part. Six months on 0.25, then up to 0.5 with barely a dry patch during the switch. My pores along my nose look half their old size. Take the slow road, it works.

Weeks two and three brought flaking around my nose and chin that made makeup impossible. I almost quit. Glad I didn't, because by week five my skin settled and now looks smoother than it has in years. Just plan your adjustment period around any big events.
Weeks two and three were rough, breakouts in places I never break out. It passed, and my skin now looks better than before I started. Knock off a star for the initiation ritual, but stay the course.

Prescription tretinoin gave me results with a side of constant flaking. This gives me maybe 85 percent of the results with none of the misery. Fine lines at my temples softened over about ten weeks on the 0.5. For a daily driver I'll take this trade all day.

Layering this over a hyaluronic serum was the trick for my dry skin. No flaking, no tight mornings, just gradual smoothing that added up to a real difference around month two. The PhytoShield antioxidant angle sounded like fluff but my skin is less blotchy after sun exposure too.

Turning 40 came with enlarged pores and a rough forehead I didn't sign up for. The 0.5 handled both inside of two months. I use it three nights weekly with a simple moisturizer and nothing else fancy.

r.t: Chin breakouts packed up and left
r.b: Hormonal chin breakouts every single month since high school, and at 35 this cream finally broke the cycle. Two months in, my chin cleared, and the dark marks old spots left behind are fading too. There was a mild purge in week one, small price.

r.t: No smell, no grease, no fuss
r.b: Dispenses as a light unscented lotion, sinks in before I finish brushing my teeth, and has steadily polished my skin over three months. The least annoying retinol routine I've ever kept.

Who says you're done improving after 60. I started the 0.25 last spring, moved to 0.5 by fall, and the crepiness on my cheeks has visibly firmed. My daughter noticed before I told her about it, which is the only endorsement I need.

r.t: Cheaper than my medspa peel habit
r.b: Used to book a resurfacing peel every couple of months. Since starting this retinol I've cut that to twice a year and honestly my skin looks better maintained day to day. Do the math on what a year of peels costs and this bottle starts looking like a bargain.

Not bad, not amazing. Three months of consistent use on the 0.25 and I see a mild improvement in smoothness, but the fine lines I bought it for look about the same. Possibly I need to move up a strength. It never irritated me, so credit there.

Never used retinol before this, and the 0.25 with niacinamide in the base seems to have spared me the horror stories. Light lotion texture from the pump, absorbs in seconds, and my skin looked brighter within a month.

Honestly my melasma barely moved after a full twelve weeks of doing all four steps twice a day. My skin feels smoother and the pads keep my pores clear, so it is not a waste, but for this price I expected more fading. Probably better suited to newer, lighter spots than deep hormonal patches.

Honest take, the first twelve weeks showed steady lightening of my sun spots, then everything plateaued. Repurchased once hoping to push further and got maintenance, not improvement. It's gentle and pleasant to use, but for stubborn spots you may eventually need the retinol version or an office treatment.

Glowy is the only word. The glycolic and salicylic pads give a mild tingle, then the brightening serum and Daily Power Defense sit weightless under moisturizer. My melasma band across the forehead is softer edged and my makeup sits better. Repurchasing before I run out.

Not every step earned a permanent spot on my shelf. The pads and the brightening serum evened out my upper cheeks in about two months, and Daily Power Defense feels lovely, but the polish is scratchier than everything else so I demoted it to Sundays. Pricey for the sizes too.

Years of ingrown hairs left dark shadows along my jaw and neck. Eight weeks with this kit and they've faded more than anything else I tried, including a prescription cream. The glycolic step gave a mild tingle at first, nothing serious. Straightforward routine, morning and night, maybe ten minutes total.

r.t: Skeptic converted, tone way more even
r.b: I was skeptical a kit without retinol could shift my hyperpigmentation, but the niacinamide and peptide brightening serum plus the acid pads did the job slowly and steadily. Around week ten the difference in photos was obvious. Pricey, yes, but the bottles have lasted me over three months.
Sun spots on my cheekbones that two IPL sessions could not fully clear finally faded after three months on this kit, and the routine is dead simple to follow.

My doctor okayed this kit while I'm breastfeeding since there's no retinol or hydroquinone in it, and it's the first pigment routine I've been able to use in two years. The niacinamide and peptide steps layer nicely, no sting. The dark band across my forehead has faded a full shade in three months.

r.t: Sun spots lighter by month two
r.b: Decades of sailing left my cheeks freckled with sun damage. I use the glycolic pads at night, the brightening serum morning and evening, and Daily Power Defense before SPF. Two months later my esthetician asked what I had done. At 61 with reactive skin I appreciated that nothing in this kit stung.

Solid results by week nine, the stubborn spot near my temple is half gone and my overall tone is brighter. One star off because the serum bottle is small for the cost and I'll need a second kit to finish the job.

As someone with deep skin who can't risk hydroquinone halos, this kit was the safest option my derm offered. The steps are clearly numbered on the boxes, nothing bleached or ashy, just gradual lifting of the dark marks along my jaw over about ten weeks.

Learned this the hard way. Two months of nice fading, then a beach weekend without diligent reapplication brought half of it back. The kit itself is well designed for oily skin, light textures, no clogging, and the Daily Power Defense layers fine under makeup. Just understand the sunscreen isn't optional, it's the other half of the program.

Eight weeks in and the brown marks left from a bad breakout last winter are maybe seventy percent gone. Four steps sounds like a lot but the whole routine takes five minutes. No sting, no peeling, which is exactly why I picked the non-retinol version.

Bought this after a rough round of hydroquinone left me irritated and rebounding. This kit is slower but so much kinder. The exfoliating pads smell faintly medicinal, the serum is silky and fragrance free, and my mottled forehead has evened out over the summer without a single flaky day.

Results came, just slowly. Nothing visible for the first six weeks, then my post-pimple marks started to lift. Without retinol you have to accept the timeline. The morning serum pump also sputters when it gets low, which wastes product. Still finishing the kit and my tone is clearly brighter.

My dermatologist suggested this kit while I was pregnant because there is no retinol or hydroquinone in any of the four steps. The pads tingle for a few seconds and the brightening serum layers nicely under sunscreen. By week six the patch above my lip was noticeably lighter. The Daily Power Defense is the sleeper hit of the box.

Between the ramp-up schedule, mandatory sunscreen, and planning social events around peel days, this kit runs your life for two months. It works, my pigmentation and rough patches improved more than with anything else I've tried, but casual users should look at the non-retinol version.

r.t: Thirty years of Texas sun, reversing
r.b: Golf four times a week since the nineties, so my forehead was basically a topographic map of sun damage. Six months on this program and even my dermatologist did a double take. The glutathione and vitamin C steps play nice with my oily skin, no greasy feel. Just keep up the SPF or you're throwing money away.

r.t: Sun damage did not stand a chance
r.b: Twelve weeks, one ugly flaky stretch in the middle, and the mottled brown across my forehead is basically gone.

This isn't a wing-it routine. I tried using both retinols in the same week early on and paid for it with a raw jawline. Following the actual ramp-up schedule fixed everything. Brown spots on my temples are clearly fading at month four. Four stars because the included instructions could be clearer about sequencing.

Two problems, one box. The brightening side faded the mask of pigment across my cheeks while the texture repair smoothed a decade of sun damage. Expect three weeks of flaking and tightness. I kept a bland moisturizer nearby and never skipped SPF. Photos at week twelve convinced my sister to buy it too.

r.t: Old cheek scars look sanded down
r.b: Teenage acne left my cheeks bumpy for twenty years. This kit resurfaced them better than the microneedling I paid triple for. The purge in week three was demoralizing but temporary. Texture now feels close to smooth under my fingertips.

Excellent system, stingy sizes. I ran out of the texture repair three weeks before everything else even using a pea at a time. Results on my acne scarring were worth it, but budget for a replacement tube mid-program.

Started this kit in December, which I don't recommend. Between the two retinols and forced-air heating my cheeks cracked, so I paused for a week and restarted at half pace. Now, at week ten, my dark spots are clearly fading and texture is much finer. Time it for spring.

Results are legit, my mottled cheeks are clearing and the rough patch on my chin is gone. But wow does this kit drink moisture. I went through two tubs of my cream in three months. Dry skin folks, price that into the decision. Still recommending it, just with a caveat.

r.t: Texture like glass by month three
r.b: Nothing over the counter ever touched the rough patches on my cheeks. Alternating the 1% retinol brightener and the 0.5% texture repair at night literally resurfaced my skin, and the niacinamide and glutathione step keeps the redness manageable. Started every third night, worked up to most nights.

Melasma showed up with my second pregnancy and parked itself on my upper lip and forehead. Once I was done nursing, my derm gave me the green light for this. The 0.5% retinol eased me in before the 1%, and the niacinamide and vitamin C steps keep the irritation civil. Five months in, the patches are maybe 70% lighter. I cried a little, honestly.

Comparable to the series of light peels I used to get, honestly. The vitamin C morning step brightens fast while the two retinols do the heavy lifting overnight. My brown patches from years of running outside are the lightest they have been. Just know your face will shed for a couple of weeks.

Four stars only because the first month is genuinely hard. I flaked at my hairline, my smile lines stung, and makeup was pointless for two weeks. Once my skin adjusted the payoff was real, brighter, smoother, tighter pores. If you are retinol-naive, this is the deep end of the pool.

Six weeks of breakouts along my jaw before things calmed down, and I've used retinol before. The brightening results were starting to show when I finished the kit, but my skin barrier needed a month of recovery afterward. Sensitive types should think hard before committing to this one.

Gave myself five months before my twenty year reunion and this kit delivered. The sun spots along my hairline went from obvious to barely there, and my skin has this evenness that foundation used to fake. You have to respect the retinol though, buffer it, go slow, wear sunscreen like it's your job.

You earn these results. My whole face peeled through week three and I questioned everything, then it stopped and what came in underneath was smoother and brighter than my skin has looked since my twenties. Follow the ramp-up schedule, don't freelance.

Having failed with gentler routines, I wanted aggressive and got it. Using both the 1% and 0.5% retinols was intense at first, so I began twice a week each. Month one was flaky, month two was even toned, month three people started asking about my skin. Keep the enclosed guide, you will reference it.

r.t: Peeled more than I bargained for
r.b: Even at the slowest ramp-up I peeled around my nose and mouth for the better part of six weeks. Prairie winter probably didn't help. My discoloration did improve, I'll give it that, but I've shelved the 1% tube and just use the milder pieces now. Works, but my skin barrier filed a complaint.

Weeks two and three were rough, flaking around my nose and chin like I had a sunburn, but I buffered the 0.5% retinol with moisturizer and pushed through. By week eight my acne scars and the dullness were dramatically better. This kit does not baby you. Read the guide, go slow, use sunscreen religiously.
Deep smile lines softened, forehead smoothed out, and the whole transformation took about fourteen weeks of following the instructions exactly.

r.t: Finished the whole kit, zero regrets
r.b: Went in expecting to quit halfway like I do with everything. Didn't. The instructions are idiot proof and the results compound, month one is flaking, month two is smoothing, month three people ask if you've been on vacation.

r.t: The whole routine in one box
r.b: Everything coordinates, which is the point. No guessing whether products conflict. The pump on the retinol doses exactly enough and the airless bottles mean nothing oxidizes. Firmer jawline by month two, smoother forehead by month three. My only note is to buy extra moisturizer for the adjustment weeks.

Mixed feelings. The exfoliation steps gave me a nice glow fast, but I could never tolerate the retinol more than twice a week, so my line improvement has been modest at the four month mark. If your skin runs sensitive like mine, maybe start with something milder and graduate to this.

I bought this for my forehead and ended up treating my neck as well. The 1% retinol is no joke, so I started every third night and worked up. By week ten the horizontal neck lines were noticeably shallower and my cheeks had that dense, bouncy feel again. Calgary winter dryness meant extra moisturizer, but at 61 I'll take the trade.

Followed the schedule exactly and still ended up with a raw, weepy patch on my chin at week three that took a prescription cream to calm down. Maybe my skin is the exception, but I couldn't finish the program and the cost stings almost as much as my face did.

Structure is what I was missing. Cleanser, pads, Daily Power Defense in the morning, the 1% retinol at night with clear instructions on frequency. My skin peeled around week three, then settled into the best texture of my forties. The kit format keeps me honest.

Second time buying. My derm actually liked the ingredient list, the glycolic pads plus 1% retinol combination is what she'd build piecemeal anyway. My dry skin needed a buffer cream at first. Deep smile lines are softer and my tone is more uniform. Not cheap, but nothing this effective is.

Yes you will shed. Yes it is worth it. I ramped from one retinol night a week to three, kept the glycolic pads to mornings, and slathered moisturizer in between. Week ten my daughter asked if I had gotten Botox. I hadn't.

The two vertical lines between my brows have been my nemesis since my forties. Three months of this program and they've gone from grooves to faint creases. The order matters, cleanser then pads then the retinol at night, with Daily Power Defense in the morning. Peeling around week two, gone by week four. It's an investment but cheaper than what my injector quotes.

The name is accurate. I made it to week five before persistent redness and stinging around my nose made me stop the retinol entirely. The cleanser and Daily Power Defense are lovely and I still use them, but half this kit sits unused. If your skin leans sensitive, start with their milder program.

Never had a routine beyond bar soap. My wife set me up with this kit and supervised the retinol nights. Three months on, the deep creases by my eyes have relaxed and the sun damage on my forehead is fading. The pads sting after shaving, so I space them out.

There are a lot of steps here and I fumbled the order the first week, which my face didn't appreciate. Once I settled in, the improvement in firmness around my mouth was obvious by week eight. Denver's dry air plus 1% retinol is a lot, so I alternate nights. Docking a star for the learning curve, not the results.

Round two for me. The first kit reset my skin last year and I took a break over the summer. Firmness around my mouth is the biggest change, plus my pores look half their old size thanks to the salicylic step. The routine card taped inside my cabinet door is falling apart from use.

r.t: My barber noticed before I did
r.b: Honestly didn't expect much. My barber asked what changed about six weeks in, and that's when I looked properly. Smoother forehead, tighter jaw, less of that dull grey tone. The pads sting a bit after shaving so I do them at night. Whole kit lasted me about four months.

r.t: Better than my last two lasers
r.b: My last two laser packages cost ten times this kit and did less for my forehead. The retinol is genuinely strong, my nose peeled like after a beach vacation, but the lines softened by month three. Daily Power Defense under sunscreen is a step I now refuse to skip.

r.t: Works hard, so does the dryness
r.b: Four stars because the results are real but the maintenance is constant. My forehead texture improved a lot by month two and the salicylic step keeps my T-zone clear. But if I skip moisturizer even once, I wake up flaky. Ottawa winters made it worse. Keep a thick cream nearby and you'll be fine.

Unforgiving is the word. I flew for work during week four and between plane air and the retinol my cheeks flaked through my foundation in a client meeting. Once I learned to buffer and time applications, results followed. Deep lines improved, skin firmer. Just respect the strength.

r.t: My face waved a white flag
r.b: I know it says aggressive right on the box, that's on me. Two weeks in my cheeks were red, hot, and rough despite going slow. The cleanser and morning antioxidant are lovely and I still use those, but the acid pads plus retinol together were way too much for my reactive skin. Back to my old routine.

At 58 I wanted more than a nice moisturizer. The 1% retinol was intimidating but the kit walks you up gradually, and the glycolic pads keep the flakes moving along. Sixteen weeks later my forehead lines are shallower and my jawline looks more defined in photos. This is a commitment, not a pampering routine.

Even in Florida heat this program never felt heavy. The gel textures absorb fast and the 1% retinol at night did more for my crow's feet in ten weeks than five years of department store creams. Peeling was minimal for me, maybe because I went slow.

r.t: Wish it came in a pump
r.b: Five stars for the formula, minus one for the tube. It's deeply comforting without sitting greasy, and my dehydration lines plumped up within a couple weeks. But squeezing precise amounts out is messy and I always dispense too much. A pump would save product and my white bathroom counter.

Somewhere in my fifties my skin went flat and dull. Six weeks with this at night and the bounce is back. It plays well over my prescription tretinoin and calms the dryness that used to force me to take breaks. Spendy, but I stopped buying two other products because of it.

Ascorbic acid serums always stung my face, so a moisturizer with the gentler THD form of vitamin C was the workaround my derm suggested. Two months later my skin tone looks brighter and more even with zero sting. Getting antioxidants and rich moisture in one step suits my lazy side too.

r.t: Four stars for the price tag
r.b: Performance deserves five. My tight, flaky winter skin is gone and the cream layers beautifully over serums. But at this price for a small tube, I ration it like saffron, and rationing a moisturizer defeats the purpose. Will repurchase on sale only.

Slathering this on over tretinoin has cut my flaking to nearly nothing. It's rich enough to buffer the harshness but never clogs me, and the squalane in it seems to be exactly what my angry barrier wanted. Retinoid users, this is the cushion you're looking for.

Post-menopause my face turned to paper. This is the first moisturizer in three years that keeps me comfortable past lunchtime. The vitamin C in it is the gentle kind, so no tingling, and my sun spots look slightly softer after two months. A tube lasts me about ten weeks.

Post-menopause my face wanted grease, but everything greasy made me look like a disco ball. This lands in the sweet spot, seriously nourishing with a soft, skin-like finish. Fine flaky patches along my hairline cleared in the first week. Been recommending it to my whole book club.

r.t: Finally a cream my skin keeps
r.b: Most moisturizers evaporate off my face within an hour, I swear. This one stays put through a full day outdoors at minus twenty. Rich but it settles soft, and my windburn-prone cheeks haven't cracked once this season. My new non-negotiable from November through March.

Pea-sized amount does my entire face. The THD ascorbate means I get vitamin C benefits without layering a separate serum, which my reactive skin appreciates. Texture is like cold butter that warms and glides. Redness down, glow up, three months running.

Cold bathroom mornings make this tube genuinely hard to squeeze, and warming it under hot water became a ritual. The cream itself is wonderful, dense, calming, and my cheeks have not flared since I started. Minor packaging gripe on an otherwise excellent product.

At 73 my skin got so dry it itched all day, and prescription creams weren't cutting it. Three weeks with this and the itch is gone, the flaking is gone, and my face doesn't feel like paper. My wife uses it now too. We go through a tube about every two months.

Vitamin C, vitamin E, and serious moisture in one step means my evening routine went from twenty minutes to five. Skin feels cushioned, fine lines around my mouth look plumped by morning, and there is zero scent. My only wish is a larger size option.

Retinol wrecked my barrier in January and this cream rebuilt it. The texture is dense but spreads easily, no fragrance, no sting even on the raw spots beside my nose. Within four nights the flaking stopped. I now sandwich it around my retinoid twice a week.

Gorgeous on my dry cheeks, way too much for my forehead and nose, which looked like a glazed donut by 10 am. No breakouts, thankfully, just more richness than combination skin needs in warm months. I now use it on cheeks only and bought something lighter for the middle.

Beautiful texture, wrong skin type. Two weeks in I had small bumps along my hairline and chin that cleared once I stopped. My mother, who is 68 with dry skin, took my tube and adores it. Combination and oily folks should probably look elsewhere.

r.t: Lovely, but summer is pushing it
r.b: Gorgeous in winter, a bit much in July. I get shiny by noon if I wear it during humid weather, so it has become a night-only cream from May to September. Hydration and softness are top tier. Just know this is a genuinely rich formula, not a whipped gel pretending to be one.

Chicago wind destroys my face from November to March and this cream is the only thing that keeps up. It is heavy in the best way, like a duvet for your skin, but never pills under makeup if you give it five minutes. The antioxidants are a bonus, the comfort is the point.
Dry Alberta air used to leave my cheeks scaly by February, and this thick, unscented cream fixed that in under a week.

Thick cream that melts in like a lotion. My winter-parched cheeks drank it up and I stopped waking with tight, itchy skin within the first week. The squalane gives it slip so a small amount covers the whole face and neck. At 67 this has become my non-negotiable night step.

Beautiful cream, but if I apply foundation too soon it slides around like an ice rink. Give it a solid ten minutes to sink in and everything behaves. Skin has been soft and calm since I started, so I've just adjusted my morning timeline. Worth the shuffle.
Necklace lines softened noticeably by the twelve week mark and the cream never once made my touchy neck skin angry.
Twelve weeks in. Jaw to chin area is noticeably tighter, the horizontal lines less so. Absorbs quick, no smell to speak of, never irritated me once. Buying tube number two.

Regular retinol wrecks my neck, that skin is so much thinner, but the 0.2% dose here with the glaucine complex hasn't caused a single flake in four months. Progress is gradual, more firmness than line erasing, but it's real and I can see it.

r.t: Fine, but my face cream ties it
r.b: Five months of faithful nightly use and the improvement is there but modest, maybe twenty percent softer lines. My regular retinol face cream applied to my neck seems to do about the same when I alternate. For a neck-specific product at this price I wanted a clearer win.

r.t: Still waiting on the deeper creases
r.b: Mixed feelings. The fine crinkling improved within two months, which I appreciate, but the two deep creases I actually bought this for haven't changed at all after finishing the entire tube. Texture and application are pleasant. Managing expectations is the theme here.

r.t: Tech neck rescue for a desk worker
r.b: Fifteen years of laptops gave me lines I noticed in every video call. This was my splurge and it earned it. Slight warmth the first few nights, nothing after. Around week eight the lines stopped catching shadows. I now apply it up to my jaw and down to my collarbone every night.

r.t: Zoom calls made me do it
r.b: Staring at my own neck on video calls for two years finally broke me. Three nights a week to start, then nightly, and the crepiness under my chin has visibly tightened. No sting, no peeling, just slow steady improvement. My only note is the tube empties faster than I'd like.

Fair warning, my neck itched like mad the first several nights, enough that I almost quit. It settled by day ten and now I use it nightly with no issue. Two months later the skin looks thicker and less crinkly. Start slow and buffer with moisturizer if you're sensitive like me.

Skeptic here. Neck creams always seemed like a scam, but my derm pushed this because of the tripeptide plus retinol combo, so I committed to one full tube before judging. Verdict at week eleven: the ring lines are softer and my jawline reads firmer in side profile photos. Fine, I was wrong.

A warm tingling the first two weeks made me nervous but it passed. Lines are softer, skin feels denser. One star off because the retinol made my neck sun-sensitive and I learned that the hard way on a hiking trip. SPF on the neck is mandatory with this one.

Docked one star for the dispensing, the tube spits out more than needed once it is half empty and this isn't a cream to waste. Otherwise the firming is real, the smell is barely there, and my chest area (I apply it there too) looks brighter and smoother.

The product works, my neck looks smoother and the deep line across my throat is fainter after three months. My gripe is the amount. Using it neck plus chest as directed, the tube lasted me barely seven weeks, and at this price that math hurts. Four stars, would be five with more product.

Skeptical me bought this after seeing my profile in a wedding photo. Believer me is on tube three. The glaucine complex supposedly works on the area under the chin, and whether that is why or not, my jawline reads sharper. Silky texture, faint pleasant smell, zero irritation.

I've had two horizontal lines across my throat since my forties and nothing budged them until this. The 0.2% retinol is mild enough that I never flaked, and by month three the lines look shallower in daylight. A pea sized amount from the tube covers my whole neck. Pricey, but I've already reordered.

Wanted to love this but even twice a week it left red blotchy patches down the front of my throat. I gave it six weeks of trying, buffering with cream, everything. My face handles 0.5% retinol fine, so I'm surprised. Returning the rest if I can.
