Realistic expectations required. I saw nothing for the first two months, then a gradual smoothing that friends noticed around month four. It works, but the tube is small and the price isn't, so the cost per visible improvement is steep. Buying again anyway because nothing else has worked at all.

Last winter I hid my neck constantly. This year I don't feel like I have to. I smooth it up from chest to jaw every night after my face routine, and the texture change was obvious around week eight. It's cushiony on my dry skin without leaving any residue.

After sixty, my neck aged faster than my face. Four months of nightly use and the crepiness below my jaw has visibly smoothed. It has a light lotion-cream texture that absorbs before I put on pajamas, no sticky collar feeling. I went through one tube in about nine weeks.

Does what it promises, slowly. My tech neck lines from looking down at my phone are shallower and makeup no longer settles into them. Knocked a star off because you really need two or three tubes to see it through, and that adds up fast.

Face retinol on the neck was always a disaster for me, instant redness and peeling. This formula with its 0.2% dose and the tripeptide blend is the compromise that works. Firmer feel in about six weeks, smoother look at three months. A pea-sized strip does my whole neck.

r.t: Bought for mom, kept for me
r.b: Ordered this for my mother's birthday, tried it once from her tube, and immediately bought my own. It sinks in fast, doesn't transfer onto pillowcases, and after about ten weeks the skin between my collarbones looks smoother and less papery. She's 71 and loves it too. Two converts, one review.

For the finer lines it did beautifully within ten weeks. For the two deep creases I've had since my forties, barely a dent after five months. So temper expectations by the age of your lines. Texture and tolerability are excellent, and it layers fine under fragrance-free body lotion.

Those horizontal lines from decades of looking down finally have some competition. The 0.2% retinol is gentle enough for my neck, which flakes if I even glance at my face retinoid, and by week ten the two deepest rings looked shallower. The tube nozzle keeps things tidy. Slow, steady, real.

Fifty-eight, fair skinned, and my neck aged faster than my face. After a full tube the crepey texture has genuinely improved, maybe forty percent smoother to my eye. I take a monthly side profile photo and the difference between January and April convinced my sister to buy her own.

Treated myself in February and by late spring the crepey texture on my throat had tightened up enough that I wore a scoop neckline without a scarf for the first time in years. Use it at night, warm it between your fingers first, and give it a minute to sink in.

Quick surf before work, rinse, reapply, school drop off, office. This keeps up with all of it. The flexible part is what sold me, coverage stays sheer for daily stuff but doubles up fine when I'll be out for hours. No zinc ghost face in photos either.

Second summer on this and I've stopped shopping around. It sits well over moisturizer and under a hat, every single day, lake or office. Only wish is that the tube lasted longer, so four stars, but the repurchase happens anyway.
Eighteen holes twice a week all spring, no burn, no breakouts, and my sunspots haven't darkened, which for me is a first.

Beard guys know the struggle, sunscreen either cakes white at the edge or vanishes there entirely. This works clean into the beard line and the tint softens the demarcation where my shadow starts. Daily since April, no burns on the cheeks above, nothing clogged underneath.

Teacher here, outside for recess duty and June field trips constantly. On at 7 am, one touch-up after lunch, and I've stayed burn free through the sunniest month of the year. It also doesn't sweat into my eyes when I'm refereeing soccer, which my old spray absolutely did.

Bought this for myself and now my sixteen year old daughter takes it every morning because it covers just enough and doesn't break her out. So really I'm reviewing two users. Neither of us has burned all spring, it layers fine over her adapalene and my vitamin C, and I've already ordered a second tube.

Needed something that wouldn't leave beige marks along my hijab line, and this barely transfers once it sets, give it five minutes. The flexible tint evens my skin enough to skip base makeup most days. Mineral SPF 50 that stayed calm on my skin right through Ramadan when everything felt more reactive.

Pea sized squeeze covers my whole face, which makes the small tube less of an issue than reviews suggested. Even tint, no shine by evening, no smell I can detect. Docking a star only because it can pill if applied too soon after moisturizer. Wait five minutes and it behaves.

Ordered in February for a Mexico trip and it's mid June and I haven't skipped a day since. Survived the beach, then regular life, then the first heat wave. The tint has kept pace from my pale winter face to now. Four stars only because the last quarter of the tube is a fight to squeeze out.

On my oily skin the satin finish everyone raves about turns into a slick by 2 pm and starts migrating. Powder helps, but then I've lost the natural look, which was the point. No breakouts and the protection seems solid, so three stars. Probably gorgeous on normal or dry skin.

Climbing outside most weekends now, and chalk plus sweaty sunscreen is usually a horror show. This dries down properly, so I'm not smearing it around adjusting my sunglasses. Held through a full day at the crag with one top-up. No burn, and no breakouts from helmet sweat either.

Really nice texture, and the Medium shade matches me perfectly at 9 am, but by mid afternoon it's gone about half a shade darker. Not orange, just warmer than I'd like. Protection is excellent though, no burn after a full day outside at Spruce Meadows. I set it with powder now and that solves it.

Resisted this for a year because of the price and the influencer noise. Fine, everyone was right. It's the rare SPF 50 that looks like skin, sits nicely under blush, and washes off without an oil cleanser and a prayer. My tan stopped at my jawline this June, exactly as it should.

Same tube handles a sweaty long run and a regular Tuesday, and that range is why it stays. It never does the watery-then-thick separation my old tinted sunscreen managed, and the finish photographs clean, no flashback at my sister's outdoor wedding in June.

Hyperpigmentation along my cheekbones flares every summer, and this is the first June in years it hasn't. Strict daily SPF 50, the 12% zinc plus their antioxidant, and the tint camouflages what's left while it fades. My derm tracks it with photos and even she commented. Worth every dollar to me.

Darker skin and mineral sunscreen have a rough history, so expectations were low. The Deep shade disappears into my skin within a minute and stays gone, no grey film in daylight or photos. I cycle and play pickup soccer in it, sweat and all. First zinc sunscreen I've ever finished and rebought.

Zinc sunscreens usually turn me ashy within the hour. This one comes in a Deep shade that genuinely matches, and even where it wears thin there's no grey because the 12% zinc oxide is tinted properly. I run outdoors four mornings a week and it hasn't budged. Telling every brown skinned friend I have.

Ran this through a full Nashville spring: kids' baseball tournaments, a pontoon weekend, and every backyard cookout in between. Zero burns, and I'm a guy who burned at his own wedding. Tint is subtle enough that nobody clocks it. Grabbing a backup tube before summer proper.

Decent sunscreen, but the marketing had me expecting more from the tint. My rosacea flush still shows through even with a second layer, so I add concealer anyway, which defeats the one-step promise. As pure SPF 50 it performs fine and doesn't sting. Just know what you're getting.

Coverage sits right at the just-enough line, evens things out but won't hide an actual blemish. For grocery runs, school pickup, and patio lunches, perfect. Anything requiring polish still gets concealer. Four stars as a sunscreen-makeup hybrid, five as pure sunscreen, so I'm splitting the difference.

Sheer on the first pass, but you can tap a second layer over redness or spots and it builds without going cakey. That flexibility is the whole selling point for me. Four stars because the shade lineup is short and I sit between two of them from winter to summer.

Just opened tube three since Christmas, which tells you most of it. For the record: no clinging to flaky patches on my dry skin, no chalky cast, and a one-step finished look for work, even in March when my face was at its worst.

Stopped carrying concealer for daytime. The tint evens out my post acne marks just enough that I look rested instead of covered, and it's still a proper 12% zinc SPF 50 underneath. Smooths in with fingertips, sets in a couple of minutes, barely transfers onto my glasses.

Matched perfectly in the mirror and looked lovely for exactly two hours. Then it oxidized orange on me, badly enough that a coworker asked if I'd tried a new bronzer. Applied less, switched moisturizers underneath, same ending every time. No burn, so the protection works, but I can't wear orange to the office.

Wore this through four straight weekends of tennis in direct sun and never burned. It's tinted mineral with 12% zinc oxide but goes on like a light makeup, not a paste. Sweat didn't lift it and it never ran into my eyes. Reapplied once mid-match and that was it. My combination skin stayed comfortable until evening.

Working outdoor retail through spring, on my feet in full sun five days a week. Everyone at the garden centre has the seasonal farmer tan and my face has stayed even since I started this in March. Light cream, a bit of colour, five minutes in the morning and the odd top-up at break.

Genuinely never thought I'd finish a tube of sunscreen, let alone buy three. My skin reacts to most chemical filters with itching and little bumps, and this zinc formula has caused exactly nothing in four months. The flexible tint claim is real too, it seems to blur into whatever my skin is doing that day.

Culled my whole routine when I got pregnant and this made the shortlist both my OB and my derm cleared, zinc based, no chemical filters. Melasma is what scares me most and so far nothing new despite a sunny spring. The tint also handles the general puffiness situation. Staying on the list postpartum.

Real estate agent, so I'm in photos and sun constantly. Mineral SPFs usually flash back white in listing pictures and this one doesn't, no ghost face even under flash. Clients see me up close all day and it holds. Reapplies over itself between showings without going patchy.

Austin patio season is a sunscreen stress test and this passed. On at 8 am, outside for lunch meetings, and my face isn't pink at dinner. Rubs in within thirty seconds, no white residue along my beard line. Already on tube number two.

Logging a hundred kilometres a week on the trails since the thaw, and this has been on my face for every ride. Doesn't run when I sweat and doesn't feel like a mask under helmet straps. Docked one star for a bit of shine along the strap line by the end of long rides.

After about a month of daily wear my baseline redness is noticeably calmer, which I credit to the niacinamide. The tint neutralizes the flush I do have, so most days it's this plus brow gel and I'm out the door. No stinging even mid flare, which almost never happens with sunscreen and my rosacea.

Most sunscreens light my face on fire. This one, with the niacinamide and pure mineral filters, is completely calm on my reactive cheeks and the tint tones down my permanent flush. I use Fair and it adapts to my pale-but-pink complexion better than custom-mixed foundation did.

Currently three months into tretinoin, so my skin is pink and touchy most mornings. This goes on without any burn and the tint takes the pink down to normal. It has become the bridge that lets me keep the retinoid going. Soft cream texture, absorbs in a minute, no pilling over moisturizer.

r.t: Tan works on South Asian skin
r.b: Hard to find a mineral SPF that doesn't make South Asian skin look grey. Tan disappears into my complexion completely, and even my mother, the toughest critic alive, asked what I was using. Light coverage, real SPF 50, no scent. It's expensive, I know, and I keep buying it anyway.

Finally stopped wearing foundation to the office because the tint in this evens me out enough on its own. One squeeze from the tube covers my whole face, works in with fingers in under a minute, and there's no white cast at all. Been on it since January and my skin honestly looks better.

Walking out the door used to be simple until this met my ceramide moisturizer. Unless I wait a full ten minutes between layers it rolls up in little beige crumbs at my hairline. Timed right, it's lovely and holds through wind off the lake. My mornings just don't always have ten spare minutes.

Tucson UV is unforgiving and this kept my face burn free through a whole spring of hikes. Slight shine shows up around hour six on my combination skin, and a tissue press fixes it. Shade selection could be broader, mine works but it was the only one that did. Otherwise genuinely impressive.

My dermatologist told me to be religious about mineral SPF after IPL and pointed me to this one specifically. Three weeks post treatment, zero irritation, no stinging on the treated spots, and the tint hid the lingering redness at work. The niacinamide seems to settle things down too. Pricey, but I'm not gambling my IPL results on a drugstore SPF.

Protection and tint are lovely for the first few hours, then it starts collecting in my smile lines and under eye creases. I'm 58, texture is a fact of life, but my cheaper tinted SPF didn't do this. Blotting helps a little. I'll finish the tube for outdoor days only.

Brought one tube to Cuba for March break for my whole face-burning family. Three faces every morning and after swims, nobody burned, nobody whined about stinging eyes in the pool, and there was still product left at the end of the week. It has replaced the four bottles we used to pack.

Palest person in every room, and Fair actually matches instead of leaving me pink or grey. It's a cream from a squeeze tube, spreads thin, and dries to a satin finish that doesn't glow like a disco ball. Sensitive skin, no reaction after two months of daily wear.

Snow bounces sun back at you harder than people think, and I've come home pink from snowshoeing plenty of times. Not with this. Two applications across a five hour day and my face was fine. It does feel slightly rich going on, hence four stars, but that fades within ten minutes.

Layers over my morning vitamin C serum without pilling, which is what got half my old sunscreens donated. I use a nickel sized amount, press it in rather than rub, and get an even veil of tint that lasts the workday. Two months in, zero complaints.

On my combination skin the luminous finish tips into shine by mid-afternoon, so I set my T-zone with powder. Otherwise it wears beautifully, never pills over my vitamin C serum, and one tube lasted me nearly three months of daily use.

Twelve hour shifts, then a ride home in afternoon sun. It's still sitting decently at hour ten, which shocked me, just slightly shiny through the T zone. Doesn't aggravate the mask zone on my chin either. Four stars because I'd love a bigger size for the price.

r.t: Ski week, desk week, same tube
r.b: Used it on a Colorado ski week and back home at my desk by a sunny window, and it earns its keep in both. Doesn't crack or ball up in cold dry air like some mineral creams. Goggles barely smudged it. Reapplying over the existing layer works without pilling.

Costs more per month than my gym membership if I use the proper amount, and with SPF you have to. That is the only reason for four stars. Performance is excellent, elegant tint, no flashback in photos, no irritation around my laser-treated areas.

Kept using it right through winter because my dry skin likes the texture more than most moisturizing sunscreens. December sun here is weak but the wind isn't, and this adds a comfortable layer that doesn't flake over dry patches. Tint keeps me looking alive under office lighting.

Replaced both my primer and my SPF step. Foundation glides on smoother over this than over my old silicone primer, oddly. On its own the tint runs a bit sheer for my taste, hence four stars, but as a base layer it has a permanent spot. Dry skin, no flaking, faint pleasant nothing of a scent.

Formulation nerd take: 12% zinc oxide for the SPF, niacinamide for barrier support, an antioxidant on top. That's a sensible stack, and my sensitive skin agrees, three months of daily wear with less blotchiness than my baseline. Soft flexible cream, no chalk, faint mineral smell that vanishes.

Skin tint and SPF in one step cut my morning routine in half. Tan shade warms up perfectly on my medium-deep skin without oxidizing orange by afternoon. Dewy but not greasy finish. I have repurchased twice since spring.

People quit sunscreen in October and I used to be people. Wearing this daily through fall because it's one easy step with a bit of tint, and my summer colour faded evenly instead of going patchy. Sits well under a light BB cream when I want more. No breakouts, no shine.

Wanted to love this, but after about ten days I had a line of small breakouts along my jaw exactly where I'd been applying. Stopped, skin cleared, tried again two weeks later, same result. Frustrating, because the finish and tint were the nicest I've tried. It just doesn't agree with my acne prone skin.

Most tinted mineral SPFs pull pink on me. The Medium here leans neutral warm and settles into my skin instead of sitting on top. Daily wear since midsummer with no irritation. Only wish is a half shade between Medium and Tan for August when I've caught some colour, so four stars.

Neither Fair nor Medium quite matches me, one goes slightly pink and the other slightly warm, so I mix them, which means buying two tubes of a not-cheap sunscreen. The formula itself deserves full marks, comfortable, protective, and pretty. The shade range needs to grow.

Sixty plus dollars for a smallish tube stings, no way around that. But it's the first SPF 50 that doesn't leave my dry skin chalky by noon, and the light coverage means I skip tinted moisturizer entirely. One tube lasts me about ten weeks of daily use, which made the math easier to accept. Five stars at a friendlier price.

Good sunscreen, terrible roommate for my wardrobe. Every white collar and crew neck I own has a faint beige halo now, even when I let it set for ten minutes. My partner uses the same tube with zero transfer, so maybe it's my skin chemistry. The sun protection itself has been flawless.

Look, if a mineral sunscreen can survive August in Miami it can survive anywhere, and this one does. Oily skin, dripping humidity, and it stays comfortable instead of turning into a grease slick. A powder pass at lunch and I'm done. The Tan shade melts into my olive undertone with no weirdness.

Smoke plus sun is rough on skin out here in August. This covers the sun half, and the antioxidant angle made me feel better about the rest, they use something called LIPOCHROMAN that's supposed to help with environmental stress. Can't measure that, but my face was less blotchy this fire season than last.

August at the lake usually leaves me with sunglass lines by Labour Day. This year, nothing, even tone right through. I'm 55 with mature skin and it doesn't emphasize dryness or catch on the rough patches on my cheeks. Comes off completely with my usual cleansing balm at night.

Works well overall. SPF 50, nice satin finish, quick to spread. My quibbles: the cap collects product and gets gunky, and the first squeeze after a few days apart comes out thin until you knead the tube. Neither is a dealbreaker. Skin has been clear and burn free all summer.

Colorado sun at 8000 feet is unforgiving and this kept me protected through a summer of trail runs. It looks like skin, feels like a light lotion, and doesn't migrate into my eyes when I sweat. The 12% zinc gives me confidence a chemical formula never did.

First squeeze after a few days off comes out thin and a bit orange until the rest catches up, so knead the tube first. I learned that the messy way on a white shirt. Once mixed, the product itself is genuinely good, wears long and looks natural. Packaging costs it two stars from me.

Been wearing it every day for about six weeks and the sun spots on my cheeks look softer, partly the tint, partly that they're finally not getting hit with more prairie sun. Taking one star off because I need two squeezes to do face and neck, and the tube empties quickly at that rate.

Forty minutes each way on the bike in July humidity and this stays put. I expected a zinc sunscreen to slide into my eyes and sting, and it just doesn't. Faint mineral smell that fades fast. The tube rides in my jersey pocket for a top-up at lunch.

Wore this daily on a Broken Group Islands trip, reapplied at lunch, and came home without a hint of burn. It held up to salt spray and sweat better than any mineral SPF I have used. The Flex tint evened out my redness too. Zero stinging around the eyes.

Product deserves five, packaging gets three, so four it is. The flip cap cracked halfway through my first tube and it's been riding around in a zip bag since. What's inside is excellent, wears all day through yard work, tint looks natural, no sting around the eyes when I sweat.

Coach field hockey all summer. I reapply at halftime straight over the sweaty first layer and it melds in rather than balling up, which puts it ahead of everything else I've tried. SPF 50, water resistant, and my nose, the family sunburn zone, hasn't peeled once this season.

Spent most of June in the garden and my usual hat plus this kept my 61 year old face completely unburned. It doesn't sweat off into my eyes while I'm weeding, which was my old problem. The slight tint evens my age spots enough for errands afterward without another product.

Eighteen weeks of marathon training, most of it in midday sun, and this is the only sunscreen that survived the long runs. Doesn't drip, doesn't sting the eyes at mile 16, and rinses off with a regular cleanser after. The tube lives in my running vest for anything over two hours.

Days on the water with sun bouncing off the lake will cook your face twice. This goes on at dawn, again at lunch, done. Doesn't gunk up my sunglasses, doesn't wash off with spray, and the tube lives in the tackle box without leaking in the heat.

Every Sunday I'm at an outdoor market stall for six hours, so I burn through sunscreen fast, and this runs roughly double the monthly cost of my old standby. Performance is honestly better, nicer finish, no sting, but for a face-and-neck-every-day person the tube is small. Keeping it for weekends only.

Three cottage weekends so far this season, docks and boats and zero shade, and my face came through unburned every time. Goes on like a light lotion with a bit of colour, dries down quick, doesn't leave the towels orange. My wife and I now share one tube, which is its own problem.

June here is a furnace and most sunscreens are soup by 10 am. This held on better than any mineral formula I've tried, though my oily skin still wanted a powder pass at noon. No burns and no clogged pores after a month. One star off for the shine, but it has earned its spot.

Since my melasma flares with the slightest UV, I need a mineral SPF I'll actually wear every single day. This is it. Light coverage evens my tone enough to skip makeup, the zinc keeps my patches from darkening, and the antioxidant angle sold my dermatologist on it too.

Took it out on the boat three weekends running. Salt spray, wind, sweat, and it didn't streak or go patchy the way my old chemical sunscreen did. The tint is sheer but enough that I skip makeup on the water. No burn through any of it.

Chinook winds strip my face raw, and most SPFs layered on top make it worse. Not this one. It goes over a basic moisturizer without stinging the chapped bits and adds a bit of a buffer against the wind itself. Two tubes down since late winter. Not switching.

Medium blends into my olive skin like a skin tint, not a sunscreen. No white cast, no gray undertone, and enough coverage that I skip foundation on work-from-home days. The squeeze tube travels well and a chickpea-sized amount covers my face. My new daily default.

Post-shave redness used to decide whether I bothered with sunscreen, since most formulas lit my neck on fire. This goes on cool and calm, and the niacinamide in it seems to help with the irritation, judging by six weeks of better behaved skin. Subtle tint, nothing that reads as makeup.

At 67 I've decided makeup is optional but sunscreen isn't, and this splits the difference beautifully. The tint softens age spots and redness without settling into every line the way my foundation did. Worn daily since February. My daughter borrowed it once and ordered her own that same night.

Expecting light-medium coverage from the reviews, I found it barely tints at all over my acne marks, and the Deep shade leans slightly red on my skin. Sun protection seems solid and it never broke me out, but as a tinted product it underdelivers. I finished the tube as hand sunscreen.

Never wore sunscreen daily in my life because everything felt like grease or paste. My wife smoothed this on my face before a hike and I forgot about it within five minutes, which was the whole battle. Now it's part of the post-shave routine. The slight tint even covers razor irritation.

Contact lens wearer with eyes that water if sunscreen so much as thinks about migrating. This stays put, no sting even on trail runs. Four stars instead of five because the tube gets hard to squeeze near the end and I know there's paid-for product trapped in there.

Everything stings my face lately, some weeks even water. This didn't, not once, not even the day after I overdid my retinol. Zinc based with niacinamide, so my derm cleared it for my reactive phase, and the sheer tint means no makeup layered on top. Relief, honestly.

Packed it for a March ski trip and it pulled double duty, SPF for the glare off the snow and a barrier against wind. The tint hid my goggle-line redness at dinner. It does need a thorough rub-in along the hairline, but the finish rewards the effort.

Upgraded from a drugstore tinted SPF and the difference showed inside a week. No more separating into oily patches by mid afternoon, no more clay smell, just a good skin day in a tube. Only gripe is the size for the price, so four stars, but I did already reorder.

Over-exfoliated badly in May, my whole face was red, tight and stinging at everything including water. Stripped my routine down to a gentle cleanser and this cream only. Fourteen days later my skin behaved like nothing ever happened. That's the whole review.

Made the mistake of wearing it under makeup exactly once, greasy by ten and my foundation slid right off. As a night barrier cream though, it is superb. Flaking from my exfoliation program calmed within two nights. Rich, unscented, effective, just not a day cream by any stretch.

Before my peel series my dermatologist told me to have this ready, and now I understand why. It sat gently on freshly peeled skin when even my usual sensitive-skin moisturizer stung. Between procedures I use it as a weekly overnight mask. My skin drinks it and wakes up calm.

A jar this size looks small for the price but I just scraped the bottom after five months of nightly use. A little spreads far once it warms up. Four stars because I'd still prefer a tube for hygiene, dipping fingers into my recovery cream feels wrong.

When they say rich they mean it. This is a proper dense cream that stays put all night. My skin was so dehydrated from prairie wind that lighter lotions vanished in an hour. This one is still there at 6 am doing its job.

Every single moisturizer I tried last year stung on application, even the ones marketed for sensitive skin. This one goes on like silence. No burn, no redness, no fragrance, nothing but relief. Petrolatum and oatmeal, nothing fancy, exactly why it works.

After a brutal week at Lake Louise my cheeks were raw and peeling. Slathered this on morning and night and within four days everything had calmed down. The colloidal oatmeal really does something, you can feel the itch quiet down within minutes of applying.

Prescription steroid creams kept my flare-prone patches under control but never comfortable. This does the comfort part. The colloidal oatmeal takes the itch down fast and the glycerin keeps everything flexible instead of waxy. I use it on my face and the backs of my hands. Genuinely soothing.

Come November when the furnace kicks on, my skin turns to paper. This is the only thing that keeps up. It's genuinely heavy, takes a minute to massage in, and I wouldn't wear it out the door, but overnight it's unbeatable. Wish they sold a double size.

Minus 35 with windchill and my face doesn't crack anymore. I'm 58 and my skin has thinned enough that winter used to mean months of tight, itchy misery. A pea-sized scoop morning and night ended that. The jar isn't glamorous but the cream inside is.

Swapped plain petroleum jelly for this as my winter slugging layer and the difference is real. Same occlusive seal but with shea and oatmeal doing actual work underneath. I wake up plump and calm instead of just greasy.

r.t: Bought for my wife, kept for me
r.b: Her post-procedure jar ended up on my side of the counter after one desperate chinook-wind week. Heavy texture, melts on contact with warm skin, no scent at all. My razor burn and winter scale both cleared up. We now own two jars with our names on the lids.

Quebec winters chap my face on the walk to the metro. A thin layer of this at night and my cheeks stopped cracking for the first winter in years. It smells like nothing, feels like a heavy salve for ten minutes, then settles. One jar lasted the whole season.

There's a noticeable soothing effect about ten minutes after application, like the sting just switches off. I've dealt with reactive skin my whole life and most rich creams break me out or burn. This does neither. It's thick, so warm it between your fingers first.

Applied a thick layer over damp skin before bed on the advice of my derm's nurse. Woke up and the flakes that had been hanging around my cheeks for two weeks were simply gone. Now it's my recovery cream whenever I push my retinol too hard.
Windburn, retinol flakes, post-flight face, this jar quietly fixes all of it overnight, every single time.

Gave me two weeks of clogged pores along my jawline before I connected the dots. My cheeks loved it but everywhere else revolted. This is genuinely a heavy occlusive barrier cream for dry or compromised skin, and my half-oily face wasn't the right audience. Now I use it on my hands, where it's actually great.

Sandwiching my tretinoin between layers of this cut my irritation to basically zero without dulling the results. My derm suggested the technique and this specific cream because of the oatmeal and glycerin combo. Six months in and my retinization phase is a distant memory.

No actives, no acids, no drama. Just a dense cushion of a cream that fixed the flaking around my nose from my tretinoin nights. A jar sounds unhygienic but the cream is so thick a fingertip barely dents it. Small amount, big payoff.

Recommended by my medi-spa after a chemical peel, and it carried me through the whole flaky, tight, weird week. No sting even on freshly peeled skin, which shocked me. Kept a thin layer on around the clock for five days.

Scooping a petrolatum-based cream out of a jar with wet bathroom hands isn't ideal, and I wish ZO offered a tube. The cream itself is a four-alarm dryness fix that saved my skin through an accutane course. Just keep a little spatula nearby and it earns its spot.

Two weeks of clogged pores along my cheeks and jaw despite using the thinnest layer possible. My skin skews oily and this is simply too occlusive for it. My mother uses my leftover jar happily, so it is a mismatch rather than a bad product, but oily and acne-prone folks beware.

Used this for the week following my microneedling session per the clinic's instructions. Skin stayed comfortable and I healed faster than my first session where I'd used something lighter. It did leave my pillowcase a bit slick, hence four stars, but for recovery purposes it's excellent.

Surprisingly breathable for something this occlusive. My skin never feels smothered, just sealed. I dock one star because in summer humidity it's more than I need, so it hibernates in my cabinet from June to September.

My clinic sent me home with this after a laser treatment and it kept the raw stage comfortable without a single reaction. It is basically a sophisticated barrier ointment, petrolatum and shea doing the heavy lifting with zero fragrance. Too heavy for daily wear on my combination skin, perfect for repair weeks.
No perfume, no essential oils, no drama. Just a dense cream that ends dry patches and stays out of the way. I've repurchased twice and it's the one product I never experiment with replacing.

Let me save you the experiment: this under makeup is a slip and slide. It's clearly built for nighttime barrier repair, and used that way it's effective. But I bought it hoping for an all-day cream and that it is not. My t-zone shone like a mirror by 10 am.

Flare season used to mean burning cheeks by evening. A pea of this pressed over my moisturizer locks everything down and the oatmeal keeps the reactivity quiet. It is occlusive, no question, so I keep it to nights, and my skin has been calmer this spring than any year I can remember.

The patches on my jaw and neck flare every spring and hydrocortisone was becoming a habit. This keeps them quiet enough that I barely reached for the steroid cream this year. It's essentially a barrier bandage in cream form. Zero fragrance, which my skin appreciates.

When my ZO retinol program hit peak flake, this cream was the life raft. Thick, almost balm-like, with that colloidal oatmeal calm that settles stinging within minutes. I scoop a little with a spatula, warm it in my palms, and press it on at night. By morning the tight feeling is gone.
My monthly chin eruption is now one polite pimple instead of a constellation, which after fifteen years feels like a scheduling miracle.

r.t: One step needs a light hand
r.b: Love three quarters of this kit. The cleanser and calming components are gentle and the redness improvement is real. The salicylic step is the strong one, daily use left my cheeks tight so I dialed it back to every other day and everything balanced out. Would be five stars if the box warned sensitive types up front.

Working ICU shifts in a mask wrecked my chin and cheeks. Six weeks on this system and the mask breakouts cleared while the constant irritation redness faded. The pads fit in my scrub pocket for mid-shift touch-ups. This kit understands stressed skin.

Thirty-four years old and still breaking out, until this kit. The cleanser plus salicylic pads combination stopped new pimples within a month, and the Daily Power Defense keeps my skin from feeling stripped. Texas humidity used to mean a greasy face by nine a.m. Not anymore.

Clear skin has a subscription cost now, because when I stretched out the pads to save money my congestion crept back. The system genuinely works, oil down, redness down, but replacing components adds up fast. Four stars for results, minus one for my wallet.

The Rozatrol step is the hero here. My cheeks used to flush red by mid afternoon, especially after coffee. Eight weeks in and the baseline redness has dropped enough that I stopped smoothing it out in photos. Breakouts along my chin also quieted down. Wish I'd found this two years ago.

Zero clue what I was doing before this. The numbered steps and the included guide made it foolproof, and within six weeks the blackheads on my nose and the shine through my T-zone both backed off. My girlfriend keeps borrowing the pads. Buy your own, Sarah.

Three of the four products are excellent as is. The 2% salicylic pads run too strong for my reactive skin when used daily, so I keep them to twice a week and the system still works. Redness improved, breakouts rare now. Wish ZO let you tailor the strength at checkout.

Nobody makes products for people who have rosacea and acne at the same time, except apparently ZO. The Rozatrol step soothes while the 2% salicylic keeps my chin clear, and neither fights the other. Twelve weeks in, my cheeks are the calmest they have been since my twenties.

I was juggling a random drugstore cleanser, a toner that stung, and a spot treatment that bleached my pillowcases. This system replaced all of it. The 2% salicylic step keeps my breakouts down to maybe one a month, and my skin doesn't feel stripped after cleansing. Simpler and it works better. Done shopping around.

r.t: Middle of the road for me
r.b: Helped the oil, did little for the redness, which was my main reason for buying. After three full months my flushing is maybe ten percent better while a basic azelaic acid cream I used before did more. The pads and cleanser are good enough that I will finish them.

Photos don't lie, my before and after at eight weeks shows visibly less flush across my nose and cheeks. Rozatrol is the star for me. The pads were too strong daily at first, so I built up from three times a week. The kit format takes the guesswork out.

r.t: Effective once you survive week one
r.b: Drying at the start, no way around it. My cheeks felt tight and I nearly quit, then eased to every other day and everything balanced out. Two months later my skin is clear and the redness across my nose is halved. Start slower than the instructions suggest.

Thirty four years old and still fighting oil like a teenager, until this. Morning routine takes five minutes, the Daily Power Defense feels light, and by month two the constant shine and clogged pores on my nose were mostly memories. Genuinely the first kit I've finished and rebought.

Twenty years of blotting papers and my forehead is finally matte by default. The salicylic pads morning and night cleared the little congestion bumps, and Rozatrol dialed my redness down enough that people stopped asking if I was hot. Took about five weeks to hit stride.

r.t: Tamed the oil, not the bumps
r.b: Two months in, my forehead shine is way down but the small closed comedones along my jaw haven't budged much. Maybe I need more time, maybe I need something stronger. It's a decent maintenance system, just not the deep-clearing fix I hoped for at this price.

Other oil-control routines left my face squeaky and flaky, which just made it produce more oil. This kit controls shine without the desert feeling, I think because the Daily Power Defense step adds back what the acids take. Ten weeks in, clearer and calmer.

Neck scars hide from nobody, so I was diligent with this from the two week mark after my thyroidectomy. Eight months later, the line sits flush with my skin and matches its colour so well that new acquaintances don't notice it. Diligence plus this gel, that's the formula.

r.t: New scars yes, old ones shrug
r.b: The gel itself is easy to love, dries clean, no scent, never irritated the skin around it. My fresh knee scar responded beautifully. The ten year old one on my elbow barely budged after three months, so keep expectations realistic on older marks.
Sixteen weeks of twice-daily use on my tummy tuck incision and it is a flat, pale line instead of the rope I was bracing for.

Playground meets eyebrow, seven stitches, one devastated mom. Our pediatrician said silicone gel once it closed, and this was what the clinic pharmacy carried. Four months on, you have to know where to look to find it. It dries fast enough that she doesn't fuss about it either.

Both ACL portal scars plus the long incision got the twice daily treatment starting a month after surgery. A year later they're thin silvery threads I have to point out at the beach. Never irritated my eczema-prone skin, and one tube stretched further than I expected.

Recovering from a breast reduction, my anchor scars were dark and raised. I've been massaging this in twice daily since month two and the difference at month five is significant, especially where the incisions were thinnest. The dimethicone base feels slippery going on but sets to nothing.

Two months in and my shoulder scar is maybe ten percent less red. I apply morning and night without fail. Maybe my skin is stubborn, but at this price I hoped for more visible change by now. Will finish the tube and update.

Our son split his forehead open on a coffee table. Once the stitches came out we applied this every morning and before bed. Kid-tolerable, no burning, dries fast so he stopped fussing. Eight months later you have to hunt to find the mark.

Six inches of knee replacement scar, and I started this gel at week three post-op with my surgeon's okay. Five months of twice daily use later, it's flat, pale, and the itching stopped almost immediately, which was the part driving me crazy. My physio kept commenting on how clean it healed.

Decent results if you commit to the full twelve weeks. My thyroid surgery scar is smoother and less pink, but the gel feels slightly tacky for a few minutes, which was annoying under a collared shirt in summer. Set time was a non-issue in winter.

Used this twice a day on my shoulder surgery incision for three months. It forms a light flexible film, no smell, no sting. My surgeon commented at the follow-up that the scar was healing flatter than expected. One tube covered the whole course.

Crashed my bike in June and had ugly road rash scarring down my forearm. Applied this once everything had fully closed. The bulbine and centella combo seems to calm the redness quicker than the plain silicone sheets I used on an older scar, and it is far less fussy than sheets.

Using it on a raised scar from a mole removal that was about eight months old when I started. Four months of consistent application softened and flattened it maybe halfway, then progress seemed to stall. Newer scars likely respond better. It's fine, just slower than I hoped.

r.t: Works but the tube is tiny
r.b: Works as promised on my appendectomy scar, noticeably flatter and lighter by month three. Docking a star because the little tube goes quickly if you are covering anything bigger than a small incision, and the price adds up over a full scar protocol.

On the advice of my OB I went with this one because it had centella on top of the silicone base. Applied morning and night starting at week four postpartum. The scar went from angry red to a thin pale line in about ten weeks, and it never stuck to my waistband.

Mohs surgery left a divot and a red line beside my nose. My derm handed me a sample of this and I bought the full tube. It sat well under sunscreen every morning, which mattered since the area could not see sun. Five months later people can't tell.

Working on a shoulder surgery scar and the results are coming along, flatter and lighter at month three. Just know that clothing rubs it off before it fully sets, so I apply it and then stand around like a scarecrow for a few minutes. Minor hassle, decent payoff.

After my mole removal in March I started this on my dermatologist's advice. Twice a day, a thin layer of the silicone gel over the spot on my shoulder. It dries invisible in about a minute. By week six the raised pink line had flattened and faded to almost nothing. Genuinely impressed.

Skin gets thinner every year and this is the first moisturizer that makes mine feel padded again. No fragrance issues, no clogged pores, and my foundation stopped settling into the lines around my mouth after roughly two months.

Heavy night creams usually ball up under my foundation so I expected to keep this for PM only. Nope. Wait twenty minutes in the morning and makeup goes over it beautifully, no pilling. The glycation angle sold me, the smoothness kept me. Four months in and my laugh lines have softened.

r.t: Three months before I believed it
r.b: I'll be honest, at week four I was drafting a refund email in my head because nothing was happening, then somewhere around week ten I caught my reflection in a store window and my jawline looked different, so I checked old photos and yeah, it's doing something, it just takes ages and you have to keep the faith and keep pumping.
At 62 I've tried more creams than I can count. This one earned its shelf spot in a month. Firmer jawline, fewer dry flakes, and it plays nicely under my morning sunscreen on days I use it AM too.

Dense, almost balm like, yet it never suffocates my skin. Sixty-six years old, on my third bottle, and the crepiness on my cheeks has visibly relaxed. The airless pump means nothing dries out or goes off. It just works.

This replaced a much-hyped night cream that cost nearly the same and did half as much. Three months in, the deep smile lines are shallower and my skin bounces back when I press it. My derm mentioned the 18 percent Proxylane concentration is unusually high and I believe it.

Didn't tell a soul I'd switched creams. Six weeks later my esthetician asked what I'd changed because my skin felt bouncier. That's the review, honestly. It's rich, unscented as far as I can tell, and one pump handles my whole face with a little left over.

r.t: Nice but wants a serum underneath
r.b: On its own it's a very good moisturizer, plush and calming, but I only saw real firming once I layered it over my vitamin C. As a standalone I'd call the results modest. As a top layer it earns its keep. Priced like a final boss though.

Solid moisturizer with a slow payoff. The first month I only noticed hydration. Somewhere in month two the elasticity changes crept in. Knock a star for the price, which I can't pretend is comfortable, but I did repurchase.

r.t: A single pump covers face and neck
r.b: You need exactly one pump for face and neck, so a tube lasts me close to three months. I apply it as my last PM step. The texture reminds me of thick pastry cream but it absorbs, and my neck is visibly less crepey since Christmas.

Perimenopause turned my skin to paper practically overnight. This is the first moisturizer since then that feels like it's rebuilding something rather than just sitting on top. Elasticity is noticeably better after three months, that snap back when I press my cheek. Expensive, yes. Effective, also yes.

Broke me out along my chin and jaw within ten days, little clogged bumps I never get otherwise. My skin leans combination so maybe this is truly meant for properly dry, mature skin. Texture and pump were lovely, results weren't, and my clinic doesn't take returns.

Three months of nightly use. Hydration is superb and my skin looks healthier overall, but the firming is subtle, more a general improvement than a visible lift. If you go in expecting comfort first and structure second, you'll be happy.

Menopause wrecked my skin barrier and everything stung. This didn't. Thick, cushiony, faint pleasant scent that disappears fast. By week eight the slackness around my mouth improved enough that my sister asked what I changed.

Nice cream, but heavy for my combination skin in July. I moved it to nights only and cut back to half a pump on the T-zone. Used that way it is excellent, my cheeks look fuller and the flavonoid blend seems to keep redness down.

Repurchased without hesitation. I'm 58, retired, outdoors a lot, and this has kept my skin from going leathery through an Alberta summer and winter both. Firmer along the jaw, softer everywhere. It costs a lot and I no longer care.

Rich without being heavy, which is rare. I use it at night over my retinol and my barrier stopped complaining within a week. The glycyrrhetinic acid must be doing something because the usual winter retinol redness never showed up.

Genuinely torn. Where it doesn't sting, my skin looks great, plumper and calmer. But anywhere near my orbital bone it burns for a minute or two, so I've had to leave a wide margin, which is annoying on a cream this expensive. No idea which ingredient is the culprit.

Quietly luxurious packaging, no scraping a jar, no oxidized top layer, the airless pump delivers the same cream on day one and day seventy. The formula firmed the area under my chin over about ten weeks. A splurge, but I stretched it to eleven weeks of nightly use.

r.t: Cheeks look plumper by week six
r.b: At 63 my cheeks had that deflated look no serum fixed. This cream, with the 18% Proxylane, actually filled things out a bit by week six. It's thick coming out of the airless pump but melts in within a minute. My evening routine is now two steps because this does so much.

Good but the price genuinely stings for the size. Performance-wise I have no complaints, softer neck, calmer skin, plays well over my vitamin C at night. I just wait for my clinic's points events to restock.

Fifty eight, postmenopausal, and my skin drinks this up. It is a dense cream but it melts in as you massage, no greasy film by the time I finish my hair. After about six weeks my cheeks looked plumper and the crepey texture along my jaw softened. The airless pump keeps it fresh to the last dose.

Honestly shocked. I've tried five or six premium creams for the fine crosshatching on my cheeks and this is the only one that changed it. Took about ten weeks of nightly use. There's a slight functional smell, nothing perfumey, and a little goes a very long way.

Expensive for the size, so I keep it to mornings only. Used that way one unit lasted about three months and the under-eye area does look fresher and less crinkly. Would be five stars at a friendlier price.

r.t: Concealer went from need to option
r.b: Concealer was mandatory for me until about week eight of this. Dark circles are softer, the skin under my eyes looks tighter, and most days I now skip it entirely. One gentle press with the cool applicator and it's absorbed before I finish brushing my teeth.

At 58 I wasn't expecting much from an eye serum but by week nine my crow's feet catch less shadow and concealer stopped creasing into them. It's featherweight, absorbs instantly, and hasn't irritated my eyes once, and I wear contacts.

Twelve weeks to see real change, and I mean real. The fan of fine lines at my outer corners is softer, and concealer no longer cracks there. The growth factor and neuropeptide combo apparently needs patience, so give it a full season.

It works, my eye area looks smoother and my husband asked if I'd been sleeping better. But the applicator pushes out more than two eyes need and you can't put it back. I've started dotting the extra on my lip lines. Waste bugs me at this price.

Four months in and the lines under my eyes are maybe thirty percent softer. I like the metal applicator and the serum never migrates into my eyes at the gym. Progress is real but gradual, plan accordingly.

Does real work on my fine lines and the applicator is delightfully cold, but on my dry skin it's not enough alone. I have to seal it with an eye cream at night or I wake up tight. Fine in summer, dicey in January. Results are legit though.

Crepey lids were my main concern and this is the first eye product to make a dent. I use it AM and PM, a rice grain per eye. Around week ten the skin looked smoother and my eyeshadow stopped creasing so badly.

Two months of morning and night use and the puffiness I've had since my thirties is visibly reduced by breakfast. The metal tip feels amazing on groggy eyes. A rice grain amount per eye is honestly enough, so the tube is lasting longer than I feared.

Every eye cream I'd tried either made my eyes water or gave me milia. This did neither. Three months in, the crepe under my eyes is smoothing out and the cooling wand takes down my morning puff fast. Genuinely relieved to have found it.
My daughter put me onto this. The bags I've carried for a decade have deflated noticeably and the crepey texture on my lids feels firmer. Takes months, not weeks, so stick with it.
Gentle enough for my reactive eye area, which has rejected almost every eye product with actives. No stinging, no redness, just a cool glide and a slightly tightened feeling as it dries.

The skin around my eyes usually cracks and flakes once the furnace kicks in. Not this year. The hyaluronic acid keeps that whole area comfortable and the lines at the corners look shallower than last winter. Small tube, but three months later I'm only halfway through.

r.t: Cold metal tip is the point
r.b: I keep this in the fridge so the metal tip turns ice cold, absolute bliss on allergy season eyes. Beyond the gimmick, the hyaluronic base hydrates well and my dark circles read less purple after a couple of months.

Love the cooling applicator, less sure the results justify the cost against my old drugstore caffeine gel. Puffiness control is better here, I'll give it that, and the texture is more elegant. Lines haven't changed much at week nine though.

Half a win for me. The morning swelling under my eyes is dramatically better within minutes of applying, but my dark circles haven't budged after three months. If your main issue is puff, buy it today. If it's pigment, manage expectations.

It stung whenever I got it too close to my lower lashes, and my eyes water easily so that was often. Kept lower on the orbital bone it was fine, but results were mild for me after two months. The cold tip was the highlight.

I work brutal hours and it showed around my eyes. Eight weeks with this and the hollows look less bruised and the fine lines under my lashes have softened. Massaging it in with the cool tip became the best ten seconds of my morning.

Morning puffiness is basically gone since I started this. I'm a 51 year old man with zero routine beyond sunscreen, so the fact that I kept using it says a lot. The gel sets quickly and doesn't sting, and a tiny bead from the applicator covers the whole area.

Dark circles run in my family and nothing topical ever helped. This did not erase them, but paired with better sleep they are visibly lighter and the hollow area looks plumper. Sixteen weeks of consistent use. I'll repurchase.

The cooling tip is pleasant and it hydrates well, I'll give it that. But after a full tube my lines and circles look basically the same in photos. Maybe I needed the stronger stuff. It didn't irritate anything, it just didn't move the needle for me.

r.t: That cooling tip earns its keep
r.b: That metal tip is cold in the best way. I sweep it from inner corner outward every morning and the de-puffing is immediate, before the actual serum even kicks in. Three months later the etched lines under my eyes have softened noticeably.
A little goes far, thankfully, because the unit is small for the money. Results are legit, less puffiness within days and smoother texture by month two. Just wish ZO sized it more generously.

Saw myself in my brother's wedding album and bought this the same night. Five months later my under eyes look brighter and less hollow, and the little lines when I smile don't stack up like they used to. Metal tip stays cold somehow, even in a warm bathroom.

With lotion I always ended up with sunscreen inside my gardening gloves and grit stuck to my face. Now I brush this on at the potting bench, hands stay dry, and I top up my neck when I remember, which is actually often because it's so easy. Lovely soft brush too.

Shaved head, and creams leave me looking polished like a bowling ball. This mattifies while it protects, and reapplying at the turn takes ten seconds without a mirror. Cap twists shut so it doesn't snow powder into my bag. Genuinely can't fault it.

Teaching means two outdoor recesses whether I remember sunscreen or not. This lives in my desk drawer and takes thirty seconds with no mirror. My rosacea-adjacent cheeks tolerate the minerals fine, no burning, no bumps. The brush is softer than my actual makeup brushes.

Prime the brush before judging it. Day one I thought mine was broken, then suddenly powder for days. Now it is my favourite step. Matte but not flat, and my sensitive skin has never once reacted to it.

Cabin altitude UV is real and I'm at a window every working day. This fits in my uniform pocket, passes security, and doesn't wreck my landing-ready makeup. I've converted half my crew. Someone always asks what I'm brushing on during the descent.

Afternoon reapplication used to mean choosing between protection and my makeup. This brushes over everything, knocks down shine, and nobody can tell. I swirl it on before walking to lunch meetings. The Medium shade matches my olive skin better than expected.

r.t: Hands and chest, remembered at last
r.b: The backs of my hands aged faster than my face until I started brushing this on them whenever I did my face. Chest too. Six months later new spots have simply stopped appearing. At 61 that's all I ask. The powder never looks chalky over crepey skin either.

Handy but pricey per gram, and the refill cartridges exist so use them. As a between-reapplications layer over my morning lotion SPF it is brilliant. As your only sunscreen I suspect most people underapply.

Be honest with yourself about coverage, powder alone won't replace a proper morning layer of cream SPF. As a top-up it's brilliant and it's the only reason I hit reapplication targets. Docked a star because the shade range jumps from Fair to Medium with nothing between.

My three-year-old screams at sunscreen lotion but thinks the brush is a makeup game. Four seconds a cheek, done. We use it on her part and ears too. Pediatrician shrugged and said zinc and titanium are exactly what she'd pick for a kid this reactive.

Almost every mineral SPF turns me violet-grey. The Deep shade here reads warm and true, even in daylight. I brush it over moisturizer for the office and over a bare face for weekend cricket. Took a week to trust it, and the second one is already ordered.

Reapplying sunscreen over makeup was the gap in my routine for years, especially living in Arizona. This closes it. Twist, shake, buff on. The brush is soft, the powder finely milled, and I've had zero flashback in photos.

Snow bounces UV at you all day and nobody is rubbing in cream at minus ten. I brush this over my face on the chairlift, one glove off, twenty seconds. No burned nose all season for the first time in a decade. Powder doesn't freeze or clump in the cold either.

Finally, a top-up that survives my toddler-chasing life. It lives in the stroller cup holder. Brush on both our faces before the park, done. My dermatologist confirmed the mineral filters are fine for her too.
Matte finish, zero flashback, and it sets my tinted moisturizer better than my old finishing powder did. Two products in one as far as I am concerned. The Tan shade suits olive undertones nicely.

Hard to trust the coverage, honestly. With a cream I know how much I applied. With this brush I'm guessing, and I still caught some colour on my nose in June wearing it alone. Fine for touch-ups over real sunscreen, not as a standalone.

Every application leaves a fine dust ring on the sink and I've learned not to load the brush over dark clothing. Protection-wise I trust it, my face didn't burn during fall hikes. But between the mess and guessing whether I've used enough, I reach for it less than I expected to.

On my dehydrated skin this reads powdery within an hour, settling into every fine line on my forehead. Over a rich moisturizer it's better, but then it clumps a little on application. I still use it on my hairline and ears where dryness doesn't show. Depends entirely on your skin type.

On summer two with it and the protection is proven, no burns despite coaching soccer four evenings a week. My gripe is cleaning, the brush head isn't removable on mine and after months of sweaty sideline use I wish I could wash it properly. Formula is faultless.

r.t: No white cast on deep skin
r.b: No white cast on my deep skin tone, which almost never happens with zinc oxide and titanium dioxide at these percentages. I use the Deep shade and it warms my complexion slightly rather than greying it out. Impressed enough to buy one for my mother.

Wish the lock was more secure. Mine twisted open in my gym bag and dusted everything in SPF powder, which is a very expensive way to protect a duffel. Product itself is lovely, fine texture, no scent, no breakouts.

Mine shed fine white bristles onto my face from day one and the powder went on gritty rather than smooth. Possibly a defective unit, but at this price I expected quality control. The concept is great and the SPF held up the one weekend I persisted. Support offered a replacement, still deciding.

Passed it around the boat one hot Saturday and now everyone on the crew owns one. Wind and spray don't budge it, and there's no slippery hands on the lines like with lotion. I do a generous four passes per area since powder needs volume to work.

Sweat plus cream sunscreen used to mean burning eyes by kilometer three. Powder minerals stay where I put them. I do a thorough base at home and brush more on at the halfway viewpoint. Sensitive skin, sensitive eyes, zero complaints in four months of weekly long runs.

Liquid SPF slides off my oily skin by mid-morning. This mattifies like a setting powder while topping up protection, so I actually use it three times a day. Pores look smaller after, not clogged. Been telling every oily-skinned friend I have.

Love the convenience, hate how quickly I hit the bottom of the cartridge with twice-daily use. It's mattifying, easy, and my makeup stays intact. Just budget for replacements because you will go through it faster than a tube. Otherwise no complaints at all.

r.t: One in the car, one at work
r.b: Keep one in my car and one at my desk. Reapplication finally happens because it needs no mirror and makes no mess. It goes right over foundation without disturbing it and knocks the shine down at the same time. Genuinely changed my sun habits.

Perfect over makeup in Hawaii humidity where creams just slide. My only issue is applying in trade winds, half a swirl blows away before it lands. I load the brush indoors now. Tan shade is a genuine match for golden skin, no grey film.

Three days outdoors at a music festival, brushing this on every couple hours over sweat and dust. Came home the same color I left. Friends using spray cans got crispy. The Tan shade doubled as light bronzer, which I didn't expect and now rely on.

Great concept, but you have to work for even coverage. I do three passes in circular motions or I end up with stripes of protection, which defeats the purpose. Once you build the habit it is excellent, hence four stars instead of three.

Photographed three outdoor weddings this June and this saved my face every time. You can't stop to rub in lotion mid-ceremony, but you can absolutely swirl powder on between shots. Zero disruption to what little makeup I wear. Bristles are still perfect after heavy use.

My part line burned every single summer until this. Two passes of the powder and it's covered without greasing up my hair. I keep it in the beach bag and do my face at the same time. The 22.5% zinc plus titanium combo is the real deal, not a gimmick.

Lives in my truck year round and the powder hasn't melted or caked, which no cream sunscreen ever managed in Phoenix heat. I hit my face, neck, and driving arm at red lights. Only wish there were a window showing how much is left, I've been caught empty twice.

Golf season essential. I brush it over my face, ears, and part line at the turn and it takes thirty seconds, no greasy hands on my grips. The zinc and titanium formula has kept me burn-free through two full summers. Medium shade blends into my tan perfectly.

Nothing protects this conveniently, and nothing empties this fast either. Six weeks per cartridge for me using it on face, neck, and hands. I've accepted the cost like a phone bill. Powder itself is silky, invisible on my ruddy skin, and hasn't once made me break out.

Took me three weeks to justify the price and one week of prairie sun to justify the repurchase. It goes on clean over my beard shadow, no white flecks. Four stars because the cap could seal tighter, there's always a little dust when I open it.

My dermatologist said melasma management fails at reapplication, so she suggested a powder. Every day at two I brush it on over whatever is left of my morning SPF. A year later my upper lip patch is visibly lighter. It's the habit, but the habit only happens because this is effortless.

Perfect for my job doing site inspections. I can't rewash my face and reapply lotion sunscreen at noon, but I can absolutely swipe this on in the truck. No burn since I started, even through July on scaffolding.

Cream sunscreens smear onto my hijab at the hairline every single time. Powder doesn't transfer, full stop. I do my face and the exposed line at my forehead and everything stays clean. Also love that I can reapply in the car without touching my face with my hands.

This is bottle number four. At 61 I'm not chasing miracles, I just want my skin to hold its ground, and it has. The airless pump dispenses the same neat amount every time and there's barely any scent. It's the one product I won't cut when I trim my routine.

At my age I judge products by whether things get worse slower, and by that measure this earns its keep. Elasticity along my jaw feels maintained rather than sliding. Light texture, the faintest botanical scent that vanishes fast, no residue under makeup. Pricey, but it's my one splurge.

Pilling is my dealbreaker and this passes. One pump in the morning, wait thirty seconds, mineral SPF right over top, nothing balls up. After six weeks my tone looks more even, which I'd guess is the niacinamide doing quiet work. Wish the bottle were bigger for the money.

Realistic expectations required. Nothing happened for the first ten weeks and I nearly quit. Somewhere in month three my skin started looking firmer at the cheekbones and the texture evened out. It works, it just takes ages, and at this price that patience feels expensive.
Light, almost watery texture that I doubted could do anything. Three months later the crepiness on my cheeks has visibly improved and my esthetician asked what I added. This is the only change.

My cheeks had that deflated look that crept in after menopause, and by week eight of using this every morning the bounce is honestly back. One pump covers everything, it sinks in before I've finished my coffee, and my foundation goes on smoother too. Expensive, yes, but I've stopped resenting the price.

Love the serum, mildly annoyed at the packaging. The airless pump worked flawlessly until the last fifth, then started coughing out half doses and I had to unscrew it and scrape. Results wise, smoother texture by week five and my smile lines catch less light. Would still repurchase.
One pump covers face and neck if you press rather than rub. I have finished a full bottle and started the second, mainly because the firmness along my neck is the best it has looked in years.

r.t: Smells like nothing, works like something
r.b: Fragrance-free skincare that actually performs is rare. The serum itself is silky, almost watery, and layers under anything. Around week seven I noticed my nasolabial area looked less shadowed in photos. Dry Colorado air hasn't bothered my skin since I added it.

Bought it for general firmness, kept it for my forehead. The horizontal lines haven't vanished but they've softened enough that I stopped thinking about them. AM and PM, one pump each, and a bottle lasts me about ten weeks. No breakouts on my combination skin either.

Started this after a microneedling series on my clinic's advice. Zero sting on freshly treated skin, which shocked me, and the redness settled faster than after my first two sessions without it. The TriHex peptide blend is apparently the point and I'm a convert.

Pleasant to use, results are quiet and cumulative rather than dramatic. My tone looks more even and the texture finer after four months. If you want overnight wow, this isn't that. If you want your skin slightly better every month, it is.

I used to layer a peptide serum and a niacinamide serum every night. This one bottle does both jobs better. Texture is a light milky fluid that disappears in about ten seconds, no tackiness, nothing to pill. Two months in my skin just looks denser, if that makes sense.

r.t: Nice glow, jury's out on firmness
r.b: Two bottles in, the brightness is undeniable, my skin looks awake even on no-sleep weeks, which I credit to the niacinamide. Firmness is harder to call. Maybe slightly? I keep buying it for the glow and treating any lifting as a bonus.

Week ten and my jawline looks tighter in photos, which is the only place I trust my own judgment. Texture is light, almost lotion-like, with a slight fresh scent that fades in seconds. Layers under moisturizer without a trace.

r.t: Skeptic to twice a day user
r.b: Peptides always struck me as marketing. My wife handed me this when my usual whatever ran out, and eight weeks later I asked her to order me my own. Skin looks less tired, feels thicker somehow. I don't fully understand it and I no longer care.

Honestly I bought this expecting nothing because peptide serums have burned me before. Four months later the laxity along my cheeks has visibly slowed, and my esthetician commented on it before I said a word. I use it at night on retinol off-days and it hasn't once irritated me.

As a first layer it's perfect, silky and instantly absorbed, and everything on top glides. The actual firming is real but modest, more of a gentle nudge than a lift. Four stars because I'd want a touch more payoff for over two hundred dollars.
Fragrance is subtle and gone in a minute, which matters to me. One pump after shaving each morning. Skin looks less tired, and razor irritation calmed down as a bonus I did not expect.

Went home from my Morpheus8 appointment with this and my healing skin absolutely drank it up. No stinging even on day two, which surprised me. I kept using it afterward and the firmness gains seem to be holding longer than they did last round. Converted.

Three months of faithful morning and night use and honestly not much to report beyond nice hydration. My skin is 63 years old so maybe expectations should be modest, but for this price I expected the peptides to show me something.

r.t: Four months in, still just fine
r.b: Can't say much has changed after six weeks. It feels nice going on, absorbs quick, doesn't bug my skin, but for this kind of money I expected some visible movement by now. I'll finish the bottle since everyone insists it's a slow burner. Reserving judgment.

My injector sells this and I assumed it was an upsell. Wrong. Between filler appointments my skin holds its bounce longer, and the fine crinkles on my cheeks have smoothed since spring. One pump AM and PM, the airless bottle lasted just under three months.

Patience required. Weeks one through six I saw nothing and nearly quit. Weeks eight through twelve the elasticity changes showed up, subtle but real. It is a marathon product with a sprint price, so budget accordingly.

Everyone talks about faces but my neck was the giveaway. I run a second pump from chin to collarbone every night and the crepey texture has genuinely improved since spring. Takes discipline, and results needed a solid three months, but it's the first thing that's ever touched my neck.

Using it on face and neck like they suggest, I emptied the bottle in under two months. The product is genuinely good, my skin is more resilient and glowy, but the cost per week stings. Face only from now on, sadly.

Paired with tretinoin nightly, zero irritation, which no other active serum has managed for me. The niacinamide in it probably helps. Six months in, my skin is the most resilient it has been in my forties.

Silky is the right word, it glides on and vanishes, then makeup goes over it five minutes later without pilling. I noticed firmer cheeks around week nine, and my week sixteen photos convinced my skeptical husband to start it too.

Disappointed, honestly. I used every drop over nine weeks, morning and night, took before and after photos, and the difference is barely there. No irritation, credit where due, but at this price I needed more than barely there. Back to my old routine.

Firmer? Maybe slightly. Smoother? Yes, definitely. I docked a star because at this price I want to be certain what I'm paying for, and after ten weeks the changes are subtle enough that I keep second-guessing my mirror.

Started this in February with an October wedding in mind, wanting my melasma patches under control for photos. By June my makeup artist at the trial asked what I'd been doing because she barely needed concealer. Consistent morning use, always followed by SPF 50. So relieved.

Stings a little on my cheeks for the first thirty seconds, every single morning, even after months of use. Not enough to quit, because the brightening results are real, but sensitive skin folks should patch test first.

Sun anxiety used to rule my beach months since my skin spots easily. Layering this under my mineral sunscreen has honestly changed that, no new dark patches all last summer and the old ones kept fading. The antioxidant story sounded like marketing until I saw my own before and after.

Half a dropper each morning covers face and neck, so the bottle stretches further than the price suggests. My tone is the most even it has been in years and the dark marks from a bad desert summer are basically gone.

Bumpy forehead texture I'd had for years smoothed out somewhere around month two, which I didn't even buy this for. Tone is more even as well. The scent is genuinely odd, somewhere between broth and pencil shavings, and it lingers a minute longer than I'd like. Results keep me loyal anyway.

Two rounds of chemical peels barely touched the brown patch on my left cheek. Six months of this every morning did more than both combined, I'd guess it's 70 percent lighter now. Wildly annoyed I didn't start here. Keep it in the box away from light and it lasts fine.

Vitamin C serums and I have a bad history, three different brands, three breakouts. This one has been on my face daily for five months without a single clogged pore. The texture is basically water. My acne marks from last winter have faded to almost nothing.

Borrowed my sister's C E Ferulic for a month and loved the glow but hated the film it left on my T-zone. Phloretin CF gives me the same brightness with a weightless, almost watery feel. Three drops in the morning, sunscreen after. My skin tone has evened out noticeably since January.

Oily skin approved. Every vitamin C serum before this one either pilled or broke me out. This is basically water-weight, sinks in fast, and my overall tone looks brighter since January. The 2 percent phloretin is apparently the discolouration workhorse and I believe it.

Under sunscreen this disappears completely, no pilling, no greasy layer, which matters when you're oily like me. Tone is brighter after three months and a few small spots faded. One star off because the bottle is small for the cost and I go through it in about ten weeks.

C E Ferulic broke me out along my hairline, which nobody warned me about. This version is formulated for us combo and oily folks and the difference was immediate. Same brand quality, same brightening, zero congestion. A year in and I'm on my fourth bottle.

Every application burned for a solid five minutes and after two weeks I had red blotchy patches on both cheeks. I know my sensitive skin is the outlier here since my partner uses the same bottle with zero issues. Returned to my gentler vitamin C derivative. Disappointed given the hype.

Between transit dust and downtown exhaust my skin used to look grey by Friday. This goes on under sunscreen every morning and my face has kept its brightness ever since. It smells a bit savoury for the first minute, I won't pretend otherwise, but it vanishes fast and the glow is worth it.

Six weeks passed before I saw anything and I nearly quit at four. Glad I didn't, because months two and three brought the even tone everyone raves about. It's an investment in patience as much as money. Docked a star for the dropper dribbling down the bottle neck.

r.t: A decade of C, this wins
r.b: Been using vitamin C serums for a decade and this is the one I keep returning to. The ferulic acid stabilizes it properly, my bottle never turned that scary dark brown, and my skin reads brighter within days whenever I restart after a lapse.

Turned noticeably darker by month three even stored in my cabinet, and the last quarter of the bottle smelled sharper and did less. When fresh it brightened well. For this money I expect the formula to survive a Canadian winter indoors.

Brightness, yes, absolutely. Texture, moderately. The stubborn spot on my cheekbone, only partially. Four months of daily use and I'd call it a solid performer that doesn't quite reach miracle territory the price implies. I'll repurchase, but during a sale.

Routine is simple. Cleanse, three drops of this, wait a bit, SPF. That's it, that's the whole thing, and my skin has never been more even. The phloretin and ferulic supposedly boost the vitamin C and I believe it because cheaper C serums never did this for my oily skin.

Overall brightness improved within two months, I'll happily grant that. But the actual dark spots I bought it for look exactly the same after seven months of faithful morning use. For this price I expected movement on both fronts. It's a nice serum that didn't finish the job.

Dries down in seconds flat, which matters when you get ready in fifteen minutes. Skin looks brighter and the rough texture on my forehead improved by month two. The scent is odd for the first ten seconds, then gone.

Left my dermatologist's office with a tiny sample vial and used it for a week. That was enough to notice the brightness difference on my dull winter skin. Bought the full bottle same month. Six months later the dark spot on my temple is half as visible.

Mottled patches on my cheekbones have softened around the edges after three months, used under my tinted SPF every morning. Not a miracle, melasma never fully leaves, but this is the best topical progress I've had outside prescription options.

Coming off medication left my cheeks covered in red and brown marks. My derm suggested a vitamin C with ferulic for the discoloration, and this one is made for breakout-prone skin. Eight weeks in, the older marks are basically gone and the newer ones are halfway there. No clogging whatsoever.

Winced hard at checkout, not going to sugarcoat it. But my discoloration from an old sunburn faded more in three months than in the two years prior, so here I'm buying bottle number two. Would be five stars at a friendlier price. My oily skin loves how weightless it feels.

Effective but that scent takes getting used to, somewhere between hot dog water and pennies. It vanishes fast, thankfully. Marks faded, skin brighter, all the good stuff happened. Just breathe through your mouth for the first minute.
