Nothing dramatic to report except my skin just looks awake now. That grey, tired cast lifted somewhere around week five and friends keep saying I look rested. I use four drops on damp skin every morning. The dropper takes some practice but you get the hang of it.

Leftover hyperpigmentation from years of maskne finally met its match. This played nicely with the acids I already use at night, no conflicts, no purging. Spots along my chin faded over about ten weeks. It does smell faintly like hot dog water for thirty seconds. You adjust.

Post-breakout marks were my whole reason for buying, and by week eight the stubborn ones along my jaw were noticeably lighter. Layers cleanly under moisturizer with no pilling. Will repurchase despite the hit to my wallet.

Sunspots I have carried for years faded noticeably over one summer of daily use, which nothing else had touched. Four drops on dry skin every morning before SPF. The serum stayed a pale amber for the full four months it took me to finish the bottle, stored in a dark cabinet.

Oily forehead, flaky cheeks, and this serum somehow suits both. It sinks in within a minute with no residue, and after two months it seems to have smoothed the rough spots along my jaw. The 10 percent L-ascorbic is enough for results without the sting stronger serums gave me.

Florida heat killed my first bottle, it went amber-dark in two months sitting on a sunny counter. Lesson learned, the second one lives in a drawer and stayed pale to the last drop. Results are real, brighter skin and softer sun damage. Just treat it like the fragile antioxidant it is.

r.t: Vitamin C my oily skin tolerates
r.b: Switched from C E Ferulic because it felt too rich for my oily T-zone, and Phloretin CF fixed everything. Dries down in seconds, no residue under sunscreen, and the post-acne marks on my chin faded within about seven weeks.

Don't let the thin, watery feel fool you into thinking it's weak. Three months of daily use faded the sun damage on my forehead and my skin stopped producing quite so much shine by noon. It layers under everything without pilling. Pricey but I ration it well.

Dropper is messy and the bottle rim gets sticky and stained amber over time. The serum itself performs, clearer tone and fewer clogged pores, and it plays fine with the salicylic elsewhere in my routine. Function five stars, form three.
As a scrub in the shower it is perfect, the steam softens everything first and the beads feel cushioned instead of scratchy. My forehead bumps cleared up over about a month of twice-weekly use.

Congestion along my chin had been building for months. Twice a week with this, left on for five minutes as a mask then massaged off, and it's cleared almost completely. The clay doesn't leave me tight afterward either.

Smoothest my skin has felt in years, full stop. Once weekly, ten minutes, rinse with a washcloth. The lactic and glycolic do the chemical work while the beads handle the physical side, and neither overdoes it.

Physical scrubs usually leave my sensitive skin blotchy for hours, but these jojoba beads are round and soft, no micro-scratches. I use it Sundays only and my texture stays smooth all week. The tube is nearly done and I've already ordered another.

Blackheads on my nose finally look smaller after about six weekly uses. I leave it on the full ten minutes, then work the beads over the congested spots. Nothing else in years of trying has made a visible dent there.

Better as a scrub than a mask for me. The clay is too mild to pull much from my very oily skin, but as a two-minute scrub the acid and bead combo outperforms anything else I own. Buying again for that use alone.

Ten minutes, rinse, done, and my texture problems retreat for the week. It even calmed a brewing breakout on my chin once, I assume the clay pulled it out early. The tube format is far more hygienic than a jar of clay.

Works well as a weekly reset, my nose looks cleaner and skin feels polished. But rinsing the clay plus beads combination takes forever, they end up everywhere, in my beard, on the counter, down the drain board. Effective, just messy.

Tingles for the first minute, maybe ninety seconds, then it settles like a normal clay mask. Rinses off easily without scrubbing your face raw. My skin looks polished and slightly glowy for a couple of days after each use.

Lovely results but drying if you get greedy with contact time. Ten minutes means ten minutes. I left it on while doomscrolling and paid with flaky patches. Used correctly it delivers smoother texture and smaller-looking pores.

Hockey helmet plus sweat equals a forehead full of clogged pores. This became my post-rink routine and the difference showed inside two weeks. The little beads scrub without scratching and the glycolic gives a next-day glow.

r.t: Learned my lesson the hard way
r.b: Overdid it and paid for it, a week of tight red cheeks from doubling up with my retinol nights. Partly my fault, but the label could warn more clearly about combining actives. Used alone and sparingly it is decent.

Dual duty, quick scrub on rushed weeks or a proper clay mask when I have time. The glycolic gives a gentle tingle for the first minute, nothing alarming. My skin feels smooth afterward without that stripped clay tightness.

Once a week is plenty. I got ambitious and used it three times in one week and my cheeks let me know. Respected as a weekly treatment it is excellent, and one tube has lasted me five months and counting.

Sunday night ritual now. Ten minutes as a mask while I tidy the kitchen, then I massage it with wet fingers for thirty seconds so the jojoba beads polish everything off before rinsing. Skin looks freshly facialed every Monday morning.

r.t: A clay mask that doesn't strip
r.b: Clay masks usually leave me tight and flaky for two days. This one has enough slip, and the kaolin and bentonite are balanced so my cheeks stay comfortable. I use it Thursdays before date night because the smoothness under makeup is unreal.

Ordering my third tube says more than any paragraph could. Dry, crinkly undereyes at 49 have steadily improved, and the vitamin C in it seems to have brightened the brownish shadow I always had. Consistent nightly use, that's the whole secret.

Rice grain amounts, seriously, anything more just wastes it. Used that way the tube outlasted my guilt about the price. Firmness along my lower lid improved somewhere in month three and has held since.

Running a retinol on the rest of my face, I needed an eye cream that wouldn't pile irritation on top. This slots in perfectly, calms the orbital area, and delivers its own firming on the side. Eight months in, my eye area finally matches the progress everywhere else.
Pricey, and you feel it at repurchase time every three months. It works, my under-eye area is smoother and makeup behaves, so I keep paying. I just wish SkinMedica sold a larger tube at better value.

Decades of driving into prairie sun gave me deep squint lines, and this is the first eye cream that changed how they look. Softer by week five, noticeably by week ten. A rice grain amount does both eyes. At 63 I'm not expecting miracles, just this steady honest progress.
Crow's feet softened around week eight, and by month four even my unsentimental teenager noticed. Morning and night, ring finger, gentle pats. The tube looks tiny but mine lasted fourteen weeks.

r.t: The bags packed lighter these days
r.b: Undereye bags were my inheritance from years of night shifts. This didn't erase them but they sit flatter and the skin over them looks smoother and less shadowed. Somewhere around week six people stopped asking if I was tired. Tube lasted me almost four months.

Does what it claims, my undereyes look smoother and the fine etching under my lower lashes has softened over two months. Then the reorder page loads and I need a moment of silence. Great product, tough price. Four stars is my compromise.

Month by month the crepe texture under my eyes keeps improving, and I'm now four months in. It's a rich cream but a tiny amount spreads fine once warmed between my ring fingers. My before photo genuinely startled me last week, in a good way.

Tiny tube, three months of twice-daily use and still going. That math helped me forgive the sticker shock. Lines at the outer corners look finer and the whole area reads less tired even on bad sleep weeks.

r.t: Good, but is it that good
r.b: Not sure it beats my old peptide eye cream at a third of the cost. There is improvement, the firmness especially, but the gap between good and this price is where my fourth star lives. Trying one more tube before deciding.

Wake-up puffiness used to hang around until noon. With this on at night, I look normal by the time I've had my coffee. Wasn't even the main thing I bought it for, the firming, which is also happening slowly. Little tube, keeps surprising me.

r.t: Stays exactly where you put it
r.b: Thick but it stays exactly where you pat it, never migrating into my eyes overnight, which ended my relationship with three other eye creams. No sting, no scent worth mentioning, and my morning puffiness settles faster than it used to.

r.t: Warm it up or it drags
r.b: Straight out of the tube it's dense and drags across delicate skin, so warm it on your finger first. Once I figured that out, no complaints. Fine lines look softened after seven weeks and my concealer stopped settling into them. Learning curve, then smooth sailing.

r.t: Zero sting on my sensitive eyes
r.b: Everything makes my eyes water, retinol eye creams especially. This one I can bring right up to the lash line with no burning, no redness. Three months in, the skin at my outer corners looks thicker and less lined. Sensitive-eyed people, this one's safe.

Slow and steady improvement, nothing dramatic week to week, but my three month photos show smoother texture and lighter circles. Four stars because the pace demands faith, and faith is expensive at this price point.

Nearly returned it at week four with nothing to show. Glad I waited it out, because weeks eight through twelve brought real softening at my crow's feet. It rewards the patient and punishes the restless. Four stars because that wait tested me.

Concealer sits better over this than anything I've tried, no creasing by 3 pm anymore. It is a thick cream but it absorbs fully if you pat it in and wait a minute. Two months in, the crinkles when I smile look softer.

r.t: Fine, but my drugstore one tied
r.b: Solid eye cream that hydrates well and never irritated me. After twelve weeks though, I compared photos and honestly can't see much my old caffeine eye gel wasn't doing for a fifth of the price. Growth factors were the pitch, ho-hum was my result. Your mileage may vary.

Gave me milia after about five weeks, little white bumps under both eyes that took ages to clear. My derm said the formula may be too occlusive for my skin. Nothing against the results others get, but my skin voted no.

An esthetician I trust put me on this after I complained about crepey under-eyes at 52. She was right. The growth factor blend needs about ten weeks to show off, but the change in texture is obvious even in magnifying mirrors, my personal enemy.
Under-eye brightening that actually shows up in photos. By week six the brown tinge under my eyes had lifted enough that I skip concealer on weekends. The cream is rich but a tiny dab does both eyes.

Dark circles run in my family, so my expectations were on the floor. Ten weeks of nightly use later, the hollows look brighter and the skin there is firmer, which I think reflects light better. Not gone, improved. That's more than anything else has managed in twenty years.

Fine lines at 47, and this is the first eye cream where I noticed the difference before my husband did. Softer, brighter, smoother by week nine. Pairs fine with my retinol as long as I keep them to opposite ends of the day.

My 16 year old actually uses this without reminders after his dermatologist suggested a salicylic wash, which tells you the texture is satisfying. His skin has visibly improved and now I steal it a few times a week myself. Split between two people, a tube still lasted two months.

r.t: Morning wake-up call for oily skin
r.b: This took the place of my old cleanser and my weekly scrub. Skin feels polished daily instead of sandblasted once a week, which my reactive cheeks appreciate. Zero purging when I started, just gradually clearer skin over about six weeks.

It cleans well and the beads feel nice, but after two full tubes I can't say my skin looks meaningfully different than with my old salicylic wash at half the price. No irritation, no complaints, just not sure the premium is justified for me.

Keep one tube at home and one in the gym bag. Washes off sweat and sunscreen fast, never leaves that tight feeling, and the light exfoliation stopped the little bumps I used to get along my hairline from helmet straps.

By noon my forehead used to look like I'd dipped it in oil. A month of using this every morning and the difference is dramatic. The salicylic keeps pores clear while the niacinamide seems to have dialed down the oil production itself. My blotting papers are gathering dust.

Cycling to work year-round gave me a permanent crop of bumps along my hairline and jaw where the helmet straps sit. Washing with this right after I get in cleared it up within a month. I keep a second tube in my pannier.

Five stars for the cleanser itself. The flip cap earns none. Gel collects around the opening and crusts over if you aren't wiping it down every few days, and it is easy to squeeze out twice what you need. Skin looks clearer though, so I keep buying it.

Don't expect a foaming mountain, it's a gel that lathers modestly. Took me a week to trust it was actually cleaning, but my skin is balanced and clear so it clearly is. Slight medicinal scent that vanishes on rinsing.

The jojoba beads are finer than I expected, more like a texture whisper than a scrub. Still, my skin is noticeably smoother since switching. Taking one star off because the tube is hard to squeeze near the end and I know there's a week's worth trapped in there.

Combining beads with salicylic acid sounded like overkill but the beads are round and soft, nothing scratchy. Six weeks in, my breakouts are down to maybe one small spot around my period instead of a constant scatter across my chin.

r.t: Does the job twice a day
r.b: Twice a day, every day, and my T-zone has never looked better. The exfoliation is gentle enough that I can still use my retinol at night without irritation. One tube lasts me a solid three months.

Tiny clogged pores on my chin used to squeeze into nothing and refill within days. Three weeks of nightly use and they're basically gone. It's gentle enough for daily use, which is what separates it from every scrub I've tried before.

r.t: Great in summer, harsh in January
r.b: Love this from May through October when my skin runs oilier. Once the heaters come on I can only handle it at night, otherwise my cheeks flake around the nose. The beads are satisfying and it rinses clean. Four stars because I still need a gentler backup half the year.

Pairs really well ahead of my complexion pads, cleanser gets the surface, pads get the rest. My skin's the clearest it's been in years with that combo. On its own it's good but not quite enough for my oil levels, hence four stars.

Some gel cleansers leave that squeaky-tight feeling or a weird film. This rinses completely clean and my face feels washed, not stripped. Been through two tubes. Works up a decent lather with a little water.

Most scrubby cleansers tear my face up. This one uses smooth jojoba beads so I get the polish without redness, and the niacinamide seems to keep my cheeks calm. Pores along my nose look noticeably tighter after about a month of morning use.

Twice daily was too much for me by day ten, my cheeks started flaking. Scaled back to evenings only and now it's excellent. The salicylic is doing real work so treat it like an active, not just soap. Would be five stars with clearer usage guidance on the tube.

Foundation used to separate around my nose by mid-afternoon. Turns out the culprit was buildup and oil this cleanser handles easily. Two months in, my makeup lasts a full workday. Never thought a cleanser would be the fix.

Expected a proper scrub based on the description but the beads are sparse and the exfoliation is barely there. It cleans fine and smells pleasant, just nothing my drugstore salicylic wash wasn't already doing for a third of the price. Would work better for someone who wants very gentle.

Between the gentle jojoba beads and the salicylic acid this hits the exact balance my combination skin needed. Cheeks stay comfortable, t-zone stays clear. I use it nightly and a bead-free gentle cleanser in the morning.

Solid daily wash and the texture improvements are real, my makeup sits smoother now. I just have a hard time paying this much for something I rinse down the drain in thirty seconds. Waiting for restock sales and buying two at a time.

Been repurchasing this for over a year. A dime-sized squeeze foams just enough to move around the face, the beads give a mild scrub feel, and my chin stopped breaking out about three weeks after I started. Calgary winters normally wreck me and this one has never left my cheeks tight.

Forty minutes of extractions used to be standard at my monthly facial. Since adding this cleanser my esthetician barely finds anything to do. The salicylic just quietly keeps pores clear before anything can settle in. Stocked up during the last sale.

After years of angry hormonal breakouts along my jaw, this cleanser plus the ZO pads finally calmed things down. By week four the new spots slowed to almost nothing. It lathers lightly, the beads never feel sharp, and it removes sunscreen at night if I massage a full minute.

My ZO rep put me on this when my forehead was full of tiny clogged bumps. The gel carries little round jojoba beads that polish without scratching, and the salicylic acid keeps new congestion from forming. I use it every morning before vitamin C. Skin feels clean, never squeaky or stripped. Faint citrus scent that rinses off completely.

Started using the last bit of each squeeze on my chest and shoulders in the shower and the body breakouts cleared too. On my face it is the first cleanser that manages oil through a full workday. Citrusy but subtle, and a little goes far.

That slight tingle plus the beads makes my morning shower actually wake me up. Skin looks fresher after. Four stars because if I use it both morning and night my skin gets tight, so it's a once-a-day product for me.

A year of these. Started for stress breakouts during my thesis and never stopped. When I travel and skip a week the little bumps creep back, which is all the proof I need. Wish they sold a refill pouch honestly, the tubs pile up.

r.t: Gym twice a day, clear anyway
r.b: Training for a meet means two sweaty sessions daily and my skin used to pay for it. A pad after my evening shower keeps everything calm. Texas humidity hasn't beaten them yet.

Those little colorless bumps across my forehead that never turned into real pimples but never left either? Gone in about five weeks. One pad, whole face, every other night to start, then nightly once my skin adjusted.

Week before my period my chin used to erupt like clockwork. Swiping one of these every night from mid-cycle has cut those breakouts to maybe one small bump. The 2% salicylic with the mandelic keeps it from feeling brutal. Took about six weeks to trust it.

Swipe the smooth side across the whole face first, then use the textured side on stubborn spots. My esthetician taught me that and it made these even more effective. Chin and nose stay clear now, and the tub looks tidy on the counter instead of like a pharmacy item.

Post-Accutane maintenance was scarier than the treatment. My derm suggested a salicylic pad twice a week and these have kept me clear for eight months without drying out my already fragile skin. Two swipes weekly, that's the whole job.

Genuinely works faster on my whiteheads than the benzoyl gel my doctor gave me, and without bleaching my pillowcases. There is a medicinal smell on application that fades in about a minute. Would not use right after the exfoliating polish though, learned that the hard way.

Two weeks in, red and itchy along both cheekbones even at every-other-night. My skin's clearly not the audience for glycolic and salicylic stacked together. My brother uses the same tub with zero problems, so it's a fit issue, not a quality one.

Almost quit at day ten when things looked slightly worse. Glad I didn't, because week four onward my skin cleared steadily and it's held for two months. If you're impatient like me, take photos so you can actually see the trend.

Results are legit, my cheek congestion cleared in about a month. The witch hazel smell is very old-school pharmacy though, and it lingers a minute or two. I've learned to apply before brushing my teeth so I stop noticing. Would still repurchase.

Compared my December selfies to February and the difference across my cheeks is obvious, fewer bumps, less redness around each spot. I use them after the Gentle Cleanser, wait a minute, then moisturize. Boring routine, visible results.

Jumped in nightly and regretted it, my cheeks went tight and red for a week. Backed off to three nights a week and now they are perfect. Blemishes heal faster and the texture on my forehead smoothed out. Just respect the acids in these.

Each pad is soaked enough to do my forehead, nose, chin, and still have something left for my chest. Sixty of them lasts me two months. My pores look cleaner and makeup stopped sliding off my nose by lunch.

For surface stuff, small clogged pores, whiteheads, these work fine. My deep hormonal cysts ignored them completely, which I'd hoped 2% salicylic might at least discourage. Keeping them for maintenance but the big problems needed a prescription.

Adult acne is humiliating in a way teenage acne never was. These pads, every other night to start, then nightly, got my jawline under control by Christmas. Not overnight, not magic, just steady. First time in a decade I don't scan my face in every mirror.

Party season is in full swing and not one emergency pimple to hide. That's the pads. Nightly swipe, moisturizer after, done. My makeup artist cousin asked what changed, which is the highest compliment my face has ever received.

Annoyingly, the last dozen pads in the tub are always half dry no matter how tight I close the lid. I flip the tub upside down every few days now, which helps. Results are legit, clearer skin and smaller looking pores after six weeks, hence four stars anyway.

Helmet cage plus sweat used to mean a forehead full of bumps every season. One pad after showering at the rink and my forehead's stayed clear through fall league. Toss the used pad in my bag, done in ten seconds.

They work as advertised on my back and shoulders. Just know a tub goes fast when you're covering that much territory, roughly a month for me. Effective per pad, expensive per month. I rebuy anyway, grudgingly.

Use half a pad on my T-zone every morning and I stopped blotting by noon. The witch hazel gives it a proper astringent kick without leaving my skin flaky. A tub lasts me about two months cutting the pads in half.
These retired my toner, my spot treatment, and a scrub I was probably overusing. One swipe covers all of it. Shelf is emptier, skin is clearer, and I stopped debating what my face needs each night.

The pads themselves earn their keep, cleared my nose area in three weeks. The lid though, you have to really crank it shut or the tub loses moisture. I flipped mine upside down as insurance. Do that from day one.

Sunscreen plus sweat plus sand used to equal a clogged forehead all summer. These pads at night kept me clear through my entire beach volleyball season. I keep the tub sealed tight in a drawer so the top pads stay wet.

Fridays my skin is congested from long days in makeup. A pad each night over the weekend and Monday skin is smooth and calm again. The glycolic gives a slight glow beyond just breakout control, which I didn't expect from an acne product.

Pads cleared my breakouts, no complaints there. But the skin at the corners of my mouth gets papery if I'm careless, so I dab balm there first. A workaround I'm willing to keep doing, hence four stars instead of five.

Pulled five pads into a little zip bag for a two week trek and stayed clear the whole time, which never happens when I travel. No bottles to leak, no pumps to break. Only wish they came individually wrapped, the zip bag pads were half dry by day ten.

Smells like straight rubbing alcohol and stung every single use, even at twice a week. After ten days my cheeks were flaking around the corners of my mouth and I had to stop. Probably fine for resilient oily skin but my face wanted nothing to do with these.

Forehead like an oil slick by 10am, that was me. Couple weeks of nightly pads and I'm making it to mid-afternoon. Not a miracle mattifier but a real, measurable change. The glycolic in there is probably why my skin also looks brighter.

Strong. My skin can only handle these twice a week or I get flaking around my nostrils. On that slower schedule they do help with clogged pores, but progress is glacial. Probably better suited to oilier skin than mine.

First week I used them morning and night like an overeager rookie and peeled like a lizard. Night only now and it's excellent. Oil down, spots rare. The tingle on application is real but brief. Read the room, start slow.

Week one brought a small purge on my chin and I nearly quit. Glad I held on, because by week two everything started clearing and three months later I get maybe one spot a cycle. Sting is mild, smell is sharp but brief.

Getting a sixteen year old to do skincare is a hostage negotiation. A pad takes ten seconds so he actually does it, and his forehead has visibly cleared since April. Worth it for the compliance alone.

One swipe after cleansing at night and my breakouts have dropped off dramatically. The pads are soaked in a 2% salicylic solution with glycolic and mandelic in there too, so you feel a mild tingle for maybe thirty seconds. By week three my chin was the clearest it has been since high school.

Ordered these for my face but the real victory was my chest before wedding season. Swiped whatever was left on each pad across my décolletage and the little bumps cleared in six weeks. Dress photos, zero regrets.

Still wear a mask at work and the constant jaw breakouts were driving me crazy. These pads ended that within a month. I swipe every night after cleansing, let it dry a minute, then moisturizer. The pad itself is nicely quilted and holds plenty of solution.
Ingrowns and clogged pores along my beard edge drove me nuts for years. A pad over the whole area after trimming sorted it in a month. Slight sting on freshly shaved skin, worth it.

Grim winter skin, clogged and dull, and these turned it around in three weeks. I was careful, twice a week to start because of the acid combo, and never got the flaking people warn about. Now it's a Sunday and Wednesday ritual.

Nightly in summer, twice a week in a Minnesota winter, otherwise my cheeks flake. When dosed right these keep me almost completely clear. Wish they sold a bigger tub because the sixty count goes fast between my wife and me.

Deeply hydrating, and the tripeptide really does seem to smooth the surface over time. Two small gripes, the slanted tip gets messy once the tube is half empty, and you have to store it upright or product pools in the cap.
Three coffees deep and it's still there. That's my whole test, and almost everything fails it. Lips haven't felt tight in weeks.

Halfway through my first tube I ordered a second because running out felt like an actual risk. Nothing else has kept my lips comfortable through Edmonton winters. It sinks in within a couple of minutes and leaves a low sheen, not shine.

I sleep with my mouth open and wake up with lips like sandpaper, or I used to. This survives eight hours of that abuse better than anything I've tried. Not a full five because it took almost two weeks before the flaking fully stopped.

Between the dry cold outside and furnace air inside, my lips usually peel from November to March. This year they didn't crack once. I apply after brushing my teeth morning and night and reapply after coffee. That is the entire routine.

Wearing an N95 all shift used to shred my lips. This stays put under the mask for a full twelve hours, no reapplying in the car anymore. Nurses, this is the one. Pricey, yes, but a tube lasts me two months.

r.t: Peptides in a lip balm, sold
r.b: Skeptical about actives in a lip product but the difference from plain balms is real. Lips feel cushioned and look a touch fuller after a month. Four stars because the applicator tip got wobbly on my second tube. Formula itself deserves five.

Bought this for my post-filler appointments and now my husband uses it for his cracked lips from cycling. We're on tube number three. It has no scent at all, which he loves, and it doesn't leave a glossy finish. Ordering two at a time now.

My lipstick used to feather into the little lines around my mouth by lunch. Six weeks of using this twice daily and the border of my lips looks smoother and more defined. Didn't expect that from a lip product. Will keep buying.

Came for a basic balm, stayed because the fine lines around my mouth actually look softer. The tripeptide-38 must be pulling weight because plain butters never did this. It applies like a dense salve then disappears into a smooth base for lipstick.

The formula is quite stiff out of the tube and I have to press harder than I'd like on already sore lips. Once it warms up it spreads fine and the overnight repair is legit. Texture preference thing, but it matters to me.

Curiosity purchase after my injector mentioned it. Whatever the cupuacu butter is doing, my lips look fuller and the vertical lines above my mouth are softer after about six weeks. There's no tingle, no cinnamon burn, nothing gimmicky. Just steady improvement I can see in photos.

Did the math on cost per gram and winced, then repurchased anyway. My lips have never been this consistently smooth. It's the only balm that survives Texas AC plus outdoor heat swings. Just wish the tube were bigger.

Years of picking at dry flakes and this finally ended it because there's nothing left to pick. The peptide plumping is subtle but real. I use the applicator straight from the tube, one pass covers everything. Genuinely impressed.

Let's be honest, this costs more than any lip product should. And yet I've bought four tubes because nothing else keeps my lips this comfortable through heating season. Four stars only because my wallet files a complaint every time.

Took this to Breckenridge for a week of wind and altitude. My lips didn't crack once, which has literally never happened. Reapplied maybe three times a day under sunscreen balm. It's thick enough to shield but never waxy.

Right after my lip filler appointment my injector recommended this while everything was swollen and dry. It kept the flaking away during healing and I've used it daily since. The applicator tip lets you smooth it on without touching tender lips with your fingers.

Does the job about as well as balms costing a third as much, at least on my lips. Nice texture, no irritation, decent staying power. I just can't find the wow that justifies the price tag. Might finish the tube and go back to basics.

Every balm I've owned is gone by 2 am. This one is still there when my alarm goes off. It's thicker than a gloss but never gummy, and the shea butter feel doesn't migrate off the lip line. Bought a second tube for my desk.

At 61 my lips had gotten crepey and thin looking. After two months of morning and night use they hold moisture again and lipstick doesn't sink into every line. The hyaluronic acid plumps just enough to look natural, not done. My only note is the tube is small for the price, but a little goes far.

Honestly the slanted tip is what sold me. No fingers in a pot, no digging, just a clean swipe that spreads evenly. The formula itself is excellent too, my lips stopped peeling within days. A small thing done really well.

Tretinoin always wrecks the corners of my mouth. A thin layer of this at night and the cracking stopped within a week. No sting on broken skin either, which surprised me. Fifty-six years old and my lips finally look like they belong to the rest of my face.

Works as well as my old sleeping mask in a much more portable format. Wind off the harbour normally destroys my lips and this held up. One gripe, the formula is stiff when cold, so it drags a bit if the tube's been sitting in a chilly room.

Skincare routines come and go for me but this stayed. One swipe before bed, lips are smooth by morning, and the tube has lasted almost three months of nightly use. Zero taste, zero smell. Exactly how I like it.

r.t: Lovely but the tube is tiny
r.b: Honestly the nicest lip treatment I've used, glides on thick and my lips stopped peeling within days. Docking a star because the tube is small for the price and I go through one about every six weeks applying twice daily.

Replaced both my lanolin and my overnight lip mask with this one tube. It handles day and night duty without irritating my reactive skin. Knocking a star off for the size, I go through a tube in about six weeks with heavy use.

I've carried the same drugstore balm for a decade and this replaced it in a week. The texture is dense, almost like a salve, but it melts as soon as it hits my lips. Flaking along my lower lip stopped by day four. It's the tripeptide and shea combo I think. Reapplying twice a day instead of ten times is the real win.

Wanted to love this but it stung on application every single time, and my lips are admittedly cracked. Gave it two weeks hoping they'd heal enough to tolerate it, no luck. My partner uses it happily so it's clearly a me problem, but I can't recommend it for really raw lips.

Minus 35 with wind and my lips have stayed intact so far this winter. I keep one tube in my parka and one by the bed. It goes on thick and settles into a comfortable film. Nothing fancy about the packaging, everything fancy about the results.

Winter in Montreal usually means peeling lips by December. Not this year. I put a bead of this on after brushing my teeth and wake up with soft, comfortable lips. The applicator tip keeps everything hygienic too. Worth every dollar so far.

Treatment left my lips so dry they'd split when I smiled. My oncology nurse suggested something bland and rich, and this fit. No fragrance, no sting on cracked spots, and the shea and cupuacu butters keep everything sealed overnight. Small tube but it's the only thing that worked, so five stars.

At 61 my lipstick had started feathering into the little vertical lines around my mouth. Two months of this twice a day and the bleeding is far less noticeable. I dab it slightly past the lip border as instructed. Worth every penny for that alone.

Picked one up at my med spa on a whim and loved it enough to gift it to my mom and both sisters. Everyone comments on how it feels cushiony instead of sticky. My lips drink it in within twenty minutes and stay smooth for hours.

Solid product. Goes on rich, wears comfortably, and my flaking cleared up in under a week. I'd give five stars if the plumping effect was more noticeable, since that's half the pitch. As a repair balm though, it's the best I've used.

No cinnamon sting, no menthol tingle, just gradually fuller looking lips over about three weeks. The peptide approach takes patience but my lip lines are visibly softer now. I wear it overnight and under lipstick during the day.

Perfectly nice lip treatment that hydrates well and wears comfortably. For this price though I expected visible plumping and I'm not seeing it after two months. If you just want serious hydration, great. If you want fuller lips, temper your hopes.

Was worried it would look glossy but it settles into a natural finish within a few minutes. My chronically chapped lips healed in under a week and stay comfortable with one morning application. Even my barber asked what changed.
Thick layer before bed and I wake up with lips that feel brand new. It has a very faint sweetness, no real fragrance, and it doesn't migrate onto my pillow the way my old sleeping mask did.

Comfortable and moisturizing, but so is my twelve dollar drugstore treatment. I finished the whole tube waiting for the plumping and line-smoothing effects and honestly couldn't see a difference in photos. Not bad, just not worth the premium for my lips.

Every February my lips crack no matter how much balm I pile on. This actually repaired them instead of just coating them. The texture is a thick cushiony serum from a slant-tip tube, and the hyaluronic plus the shea and cupuacu butters keep them soft through a whole workday.

Took a solid six weeks before I noticed my lips looking fuller, so don't expect an instant plumper. What you get right away is deep comfort, the shea butter richness without any waxiness. Four stars for the wait, five for the feel.

Years of quitting every active because my skin would revolt. Eight weeks of Mystro seems to have raised my tolerance, and I'm back on a low retinoid twice a week with no drama. Whatever the adaptogens are doing, it's working for me.

Cold wind, hot yoga, a night of bad sleep, my face used to broadcast all of it. Three months into Mystro and my skin just absorbs the chaos. Texture is smoother too, though that felt like a bonus rather than the point.

A single half pump covers my entire face, so the bottle has lasted almost four months, which softens the sticker shock considerably. Skin feels sturdier and less reactive to cold wind. Just wish results went beyond calming into brightening.

Two weeks after a fraxel session my derm had me start this. The tight, shiny feeling resolved much faster than after my first treatment when I used nothing special. It has a slight peachy tint in the bottle from the astaxanthin but goes on invisible.

Before this serum I flared every few weeks, wind, wine, stress, didn't matter. Since starting it in January I've had two mild flares total. My dermatologist asked what changed. The pump is precise and one is plenty for my whole face.

You won't wake up transformed. What happens instead is your skin just stops having bad days. Fewer random spots, less tightness after cleansing, makeup sits better. Four stars only because the price demands obvious results and these are quiet ones.

Living at altitude with ski weekends means wind, sun, and dry air constantly. This serum under my moisturizer keeps the windburn redness from ever settling in. Absorbs in seconds, no residue, and one pump covers my whole face.

Didn't expect the serum itself to be that orangey color, that's the astaxanthin apparently, and no, it doesn't stain your face. What it does is keep my skin weirdly consistent. Same calm state whether I've slept four hours or nine.

Pink cheeks have been my baseline my whole adult life. After eight weeks of twice daily use the background redness is noticeably softer, enough that I skip color corrector most days. The niacinamide and adaptogens do slow, quiet work. No sting, no scent, no pilling.

Thesis year wrecked my sleep and my face broadcast it, dull, blotchy, reactive. This has been the steadying force. Skin tone looks even again and the random itchy patches are gone. Costs more than a grad student should spend, no regrets though.

I wanted to love this. Applied faithfully every day for two full bottles and saw no change in redness, texture, or the stress breakouts it supposedly targets. At this price point that is a painful experiment. Returning to my basic niacinamide serum.

Perfectly pleasant serum, silky, absorbs fast, never irritated me. But after two full bottles I can't identify a single concrete change in my skin. Maybe my skin was already balanced. Hard to justify a third bottle on maybes.

Performs exactly as promised for my reactive skin, calmer and more even within a month. The pump gives a consistent dose and the bottle lasted eleven weeks. I just wince at the reorder cost every single time, which keeps this at four stars.

Flying always trashes my skin for a week. Took this on a three week Europe trip, used it every morning and evening, and came home with the same skin I left with. The airless pump survived my carry-on and dispenses the exact right amount.

Went through a package of three microneedling sessions this spring and used this during every recovery window. Redness settled in about half the usual time and my skin never did that tight angry thing. Gentle enough for day two post-treatment.

Somehow this serum keeps the peace between my retinol nights and my acid mornings. Since adding it I've not had a single irritation flare. Hard to explain what it does until you skip it for a week and your skin reminds you.

Give it a full month before judging. Weeks one through three I saw nothing, then the background redness I've carried for years quietly dialed down. It's real but subtle, and slow, hence four stars instead of five.

Everything active used to burn my face, even the so-called sensitive formulas. This one goes on like a water-thin lotion with zero reaction, and after two months my skin tolerates my vitamin C again. My derm called it a barrier retrainer and that matches my experience.

Fifty three, and my skin had turned unpredictable, oily forehead, flaky cheeks, sudden red patches. This evened all of it out over about six weeks. I use two pumps in the morning under moisturizer and SPF. It has become the one product I refuse to run out of.

Went through a brutal work stretch and my face responded with redness, random dry patches, and breakouts all at once. Mystro settled everything down within a month. It is a silky, milky serum from a pump, sinks in fast, and layers under anything without pilling.

Effective little tube. My lip texture improved noticeably in about five weeks and gloss no longer settles into cracks. The warm vibrating tingle on application is polarizing though, I got used to it but my sister returned hers because of it.

It stays put. Every other lip treatment I have owned ends up on coffee cups and masks within the hour. This dries down to a thin film that keeps working underneath whatever else your day involves. Smoother, plumper looking lips by week four.

My injector suggested an antioxidant lip product to protect the results between appointments and this was her pick. Lips stay hydrated, the border looks crisp, and honestly the fine lines softened enough that I went longer between filler top-ups this year.

Real results, wrong wear time. Smoother lip surface and less peeling after a month, but I apply at ten and by two a.m. I'm reaching for something richer because it's worn off. I now layer a plain balm on top and the combo works.

r.t: Part of my nightly ritual now
r.b: Retinol for the face, this for the lips, both from my SkinCeuticals routine. The texture is a light gel that dries down semi-matte, so it never slides around overnight. My lip edges look more defined, and the dryness I blamed on age turned out to be fixable.

Feathering was ruining my lipstick, the vertical lines above my lip pulled color upward by mid-morning. A month of this every night and it has mostly stopped. It goes on glossy, settles to a comfortable film, and a tiny bead covers both lips.

Fair warning, the first few applications buzz like a mild pepper. It faded after week one and now I barely notice. What I do notice is that my lips haven't flaked since January despite the coastal wind, and my lip color goes on evenly for the first time in years.

My lips take abuse, hot coffee all day and a lakefront commute in January. This is the first treatment that kept them comfortable through an entire Toronto winter. Thin layer at night, done. The slight warmth on application stopped bothering me after week one.

Tretinoin migrates to my lip line no matter how careful I'm, and by December my mouth corners were cracked. Two weeks of this nightly repaired them, and staying on it has kept everything smooth since. The vitamin E and silymarin combo seems to do real repair work, not just coat.

Sixty seven years old and I had given up on the crepey texture around my mouth. Three months of this twice a day made a visible difference, my daughter noticed before I said anything. A rice grain amount covers both lips and the border.
You need a rice grain amount, so despite the small tube mine lasted a full season of daily use. Lips look smoother and the dry vertical creasing I usually get in winter never showed up this year.

r.t: Good stuff in a stingy tube
r.b: Works, but ten milliliters disappears fast when you apply it AM and PM. The precise applicator means nothing gets wasted at least. Lips are smoother, and the fine crinkling when I purse my mouth has eased up after two months.

Nurse here, constant dryness from hospital ventilation. One coat before a shift and my lips aren't peeling by hour ten anymore. It's more treatment than balm, slightly tingly at first, but the difference from regular chapstick is night and day.

At sixty-three my lips had gone thin and crinkled. Three months in, the texture is plumper and the creasing catches less light. It won't replace filler and doesn't claim to, but it's the most change I've gotten from anything topical. Applying it is now a nonnegotiable bedtime step.

For most people the sting apparently fades after a week. Mine never did, every application buzzed uncomfortably for a couple of minutes, and there is a faintly bitter taste if you talk too soon after applying. Results were decent, smoother texture, but the experience wore me down.

First few uses my lips buzzed for a good ten minutes and I nearly returned it. Dropped to every other night and worked up, and now it's fine and my lips are noticeably smoother. Fair warning for sensitive folks, ease in.

Two months before my wedding I started using it because every close-up photo showed peeling lips. By the big day they were smooth enough for the macro shots. It's not sticky and doesn't shine like gloss, just healthy looking. Groomsmen kept borrowing it, I pretended not to notice.

Understand what you are buying. This exfoliates and treats, it does not cushion like a balm, so I layer a plain balm on top at night. Doing that combo, my lips are smoother and the peeling is gone. On its own it can feel slightly drying at first.

Phoenix summers dehydrate everything and this kept my lips from shriveling. Knocking a star off because you really need a balm over it during the day, alone it feels a touch tight after a few hours in air conditioning.

No question it works, my lip edges look more defined and less crepey after six weeks. But there's a bitter medicinal taste if you talk too much right after applying, and I talk for a living. I've learned to apply it only at bedtime.

Quit smoking two years ago but the lines stuck around. Six months into this little tube used twice daily and even my wife commented they look shallower. The silymarin and vitamin E angle sold me, the mirror keeps me repurchasing.

Sure, it keeps my lips in good shape, but so did cheaper peptide balms I've used. The antioxidant story makes sense on paper and maybe I'm getting long-term protection I can't see, but at this price I wanted a visible wow and got a shrug.

Applied nightly along my lip border for three months and the vertical lines above my top lip have genuinely relaxed. It tingles the first minute, which the box warns about, then settles. Not a balm, more of a treatment serum with a satin finish.

r.t: Chinook winds could not crack them
r.b: Anyone from Calgary knows what the dry wind does to lips. First winter in years I didn't have a single split. I put it on before bed, let the tingle pass, and wake up sorted. Lasted me just over two months per tube.

Houston humidity destroys most moisturizers on my face by 10am. This one keeps its light, almost matte finish through the afternoon school run. The niacinamide seems to have calmed the redness around my nose as a bonus.

Close to ideal for combination skin in a hot climate. Absorbs fast, controls shine reasonably well, never breaks me out. The four stars is purely about price per ml, it goes quick when you use it twice a day.

Fourth bottle and counting. One pump in the morning, one at night, and a bottle lasts right around ten weeks. My hormonal chin breakouts quieted noticeably once I stopped using a heavier night cream and let this do both shifts.

Pores on my nose used to look inflamed and obvious by end of day. Two months with this and they've visibly settled down. It absorbs in seconds and doesn't smell like anything, which is exactly what I want.

Anything richer than a gel gives me closed comedones within a week. Three months on this and not a single new bump, while the dehydration lines around my eyes filled back in. It threads a needle I thought was impossible.
Zero pilling under my mineral sunscreen, which eliminated my last excuse for skipping moisturizer in the morning. Combination skin, mid forties, and my texture looks more even than it has in years.

From April to November this is all I need. Deep winter in Montreal demands something richer, so I switch to a heavier cream for January and February. The niacinamide keeps my tone even and it never pills under sunscreen. Just know its limits.

Really liked the product itself, kept my skin balanced through a Boston winter better than expected. But the pump on my second bottle started sputtering with maybe a fifth left and I had to cut it open to get the rest. Packaging quality control needs a look.

Every month like clockwork my chin would erupt the week before my period. Since switching to this in the fall, those breakouts have shrunk to maybe one small spot. I assume the salicylic acid is quietly doing prevention work. Genuinely grateful.

By 2pm my forehead used to glow like a lighthouse. A month into this and the oil production genuinely calmed down. I think the barrier repair angle with the ceramides is what did it. Light enough that I forget I am wearing anything.

Feels like applying nothing, which made me doubt it, yet my skin has stayed hydrated through gym sessions, patio season, and a head cold that involved a lot of nose blowing. The ceramide and NMF combination clearly pulls its weight.

Spent thirty years skipping moisturizer because everything felt like grease. This convinced me otherwise. Skin is less shiny now that it is properly hydrated, which sounds backwards but here we are. One pump does my whole face.

Really nice lightweight formula, and the niacinamide has faded some old acne marks along my chin. Docking a star because in January I needed to layer a heavier cream on top. It's not quite enough for a BC winter.

Bought this on an aesthetician's suggestion but my skin runs drier than I realized and this never felt like enough, even layered over a hyaluronic serum. Beautiful texture and no fragrance, just aimed at oilier faces than mine. My teenage son uses it now and likes it.

Whoever decided to put salicylic acid inside a ceramide moisturizer deserves a raise. My oily skin gets hydration and low-grade pore maintenance in one step, and I've had exactly one blemish since March. I used to get one a week.

Both times I tried to push through, my cheeks stung within a minute of applying and stayed pink for an hour. I suspect the salicylic acid is too much for my sensitive skin. Returned it, disappointed because the texture was lovely.

Makeup artists have twice asked what I prep with because foundation glides over this so well. It leaves a smooth, grippy-in-a-good-way canvas with zero residue. Been on it twice a day since spring and my skin has stayed balanced through everything.

For years my forehead shined while my cheeks flaked, and nothing addressed both. This does. Light enough for the oily zones, and the ceramides keep the dry parts comfortable. Took about three weeks to find the balance.

Nothing flashy happens. Skin just stays comfortable, balanced, and clear day after day, which after years of chasing dramatic actives feels like the actual goal. The airless pump dispenses a perfect dose right down to the last use.

Hydrates my cheeks without turning my T-zone into an oil slick by lunch. The texture is a light gel-cream that vanishes in about thirty seconds, and the whisper of salicylic in it keeps my pores from clogging. Airless pump means no scraping a jar with wet fingers.

Skeptical of the name, but six weeks in my skin genuinely behaves differently, less oil at the surface, no tight patches after cleansing, and my blotting papers are collecting dust. It layers cleanly over my AlphaRet at night with no pilling.

I'd accumulated a drawer of half used jars over the years. Gave them all away and just run this program morning and night. My texture is smoother, the vitamin C in the polish gives a nice glow, and I love that I don't have to think about layering order anymore.

r.t: My barber sells nothing this good
r.b: Grabbed this after my girlfriend got tired of me stealing her products. The steps take no thought, the scrub feels like proper equipment, and my face has stopped shining in photos. Two refills in and committed.

Maybe I did it wrong, but following the included schedule left my face red, tight, and stinging by day twelve. Customer service suggested spacing out the pads, which helped a little, but for this price I shouldn't need a recovery plan. Went back to my old cleanser and cream.

What sold me is how the steps build on each other. Salicylic in the cleanser, glycolic in the pads, then Daily Power Defense to settle everything down. I'd been mixing brands for years and always had one product fighting another. Ten weeks in, my skin tone looks even in daylight without filters.

Gave away half a drawer of products after a month on this program. The exfoliating cleanser handles daily oil, the vitamin C in the polish step gives a glow, and DPD under sunscreen has kept new sun spots away through spring. Repurchasing was automatic.
Skin's been glowing since week four and I've finally stopped shopping for new products.

I bought this after my facialist kept nagging me about consistency. The cleanser and polish handle mornings, the glycolic pads and Daily Power Defense do evenings, and my combination skin stopped throwing tantrums around week five. Texture on my forehead is noticeably smoother. It's not cheap but everything gets used, nothing sits in a drawer.

Sizing is my only real gripe. The cleanser and polish are generous but the Daily Power Defense, clearly the star of the box, runs out a month before everything else. Results were noticeable by week five, brighter skin and fewer clogged pores. Wish the ratios matched.

Flushed cheeks for the first two weeks, until I dropped the pads to every other night. After that adjustment it's been smooth sailing, literally, my texture is the best it's been in years. Sensitive folks should just know the acids announce themselves early.

It's less about any single hero product and more that I actually do all four steps now because they're sitting there in order. Skin looks polished, my esthetician asked what changed, and the Daily Power Defense layer keeps everything from feeling stripped. Wish the pads tub were a little bigger.

Counters keep trying to sell women my age fourteen different products. This box replaced them all and my skin is brighter and less crepey looking after three months. The polish step I do gently, twice weekly, and the Daily Power Defense feels like silk under my sunscreen.

Does what it promises, my texture improved and the routine takes five minutes. The upfront cost stings though, and when the DPD runs dry you realize the refill economics. Budget for the serum separately and the kit makes more sense as a starting point.

Nothing dramatic happened until week seven, and I almost quit at week five. Glad I didn't. Oil production is down, blackheads on my chin mostly gone. If you want overnight miracles look elsewhere, this one builds slowly and quietly.

My girlfriend set this up on my bathroom counter and honestly I just did what the box said. Two months later my skin's less greasy by noon and the bumps along my hairline are gone. The magnesium polish feels like it's doing something real. Never thought I'd reorder skincare.

Sadly the acids in the pads plus the polish were more than my skin could take, even spaced out. Three weeks of stinging and flaky patches around my nose before I gave up. My sister with oily skin took over the kit and loves it, so know your skin type before buying.

The serum in this kit is genuinely excellent, silky under sunscreen, and I'll rebuy it full size. Cleanser and polish are solid but not special. Four stars because replacing the individual pieces once the kit runs out costs a small fortune.

Second box. First one lasted me almost four months using the polish twice a week like the pamphlet suggests. Pores along my nose look half the size they did in spring and razor burn is basically history. Easy to follow even when I'm half asleep.

Left to my own devices I collect random serums and use none of them consistently. This kit forced a rhythm, wash, polish on Sundays and Wednesdays, protect with the DPD serum daily. Three months later my texture is smoother than it has been in a decade.

Worried the acids would be too much for minus thirty weather, but pairing the program with a heavier night cream worked perfectly. The polish keeps flaky winter buildup away, honestly the best part of the kit. Skin looked good in every holiday photo for once.

r.t: My dry skin waved the white flag
r.b: The pads plus the exfoliating cleanser was just too much acid for my dry skin, even at half frequency. Flaking around my nose by day ten. The Daily Power Defense is beautiful though, so I kept that and gifted the rest to my oily sister. She loves it, for what it's worth.

Never had a routine before forty and figured a kit was the safest entry point. The instructions are clear about what goes when, the polish is weirdly satisfying, and after two months colleagues started asking if I changed something. Nobody guesses it is just consistency.

r.t: Cleared up my dull gray look
r.b: For most of my thirties my skin looked tired and gray. Six weeks with this kit and coworkers started asking if I'd been on vacation. The pads sting for a second, that's it. Great intro to actual actives.

Using the magnesium polish daily like I first did is a mistake, my cheeks went red and stayed red. Twice a week is the sweet spot. With that adjustment the kit delivers, clearer pores, brighter tone, and the DPD layer makes my SPF apply smoother.

Ordered this instead of piecing together products and it simplified everything. Cleanser morning and night, the magnesium crystal polish twice a week, renewal pads in the evening, and Daily Power Defense every morning. Six weeks in my skin looks polished and even, and I actually stick to it because it is idiot proof.

r.t: Box did what my derm said
r.b: Dermatologist recommended ZO and this was the cheapest way to try several products at once. She was right. Three months in, breakouts are rare and my skin doesn't get shiny by lunch. Following the schedule card is the whole trick.

r.t: Week two was rough, worth it
r.b: Nobody warned me about the adjustment period. My skin felt tight and looked slightly flaky for the first two weeks while it got used to the glycolic and salicylic. Then everything settled and the payoff arrived, smooth, bright, even skin that makeup barely needs to help.

Dermatologist suggestion after a round of skin cancer screenings left my face raw from biopsies. Healing skin accepted it without a single complaint. A year later it is still what I reach for, and at 68 I have earned the right to be picky.

Counterintuitive but true. Once I stopped attacking my oil with harsh cleansers, my skin stopped overproducing to compensate. Two months of this mild gel and my midday shine has genuinely decreased. Should've listened to my esthetician years ago.

Post-workout my face is a salt lick, and this takes it all off without leaving me stripped for the walk home. It's the only cleanser that survives daily double washing without wrecking my cheeks. Ten months strong.

Stripped my routine to almost nothing while pregnant and this made the keep pile. My OB had no notes on the ingredients, my newly weird hormonal skin has no complaints, and I'm not thinking about my cleanser at all. Perfect.

When my derm bumped me to nightly tretinoin she told me to swap my foaming cleanser for something like this. Irritation dropped immediately. It removes the day without touching my barrier, and the bottle design lets you get every last bit out.

There's the faintest clean smell that disappears in seconds, which my migraine-prone self appreciates. Cleans well, rinses fast. Knocking a star because the gel is so light I sometimes use two squeezes when I'm wearing sunscreen.

Fifteen years of foam and I thought tight skin meant clean skin. Three washes with this and I realized my face had been thirsty the whole time. Rinses clean, feels like nothing, and my moisturizer use has literally halved.

It's gentle, no argument there, but one wash won't fully break down my mineral sunscreen. I end up going twice at night which burns through the bottle. Fine as a morning cleanser, incomplete as an evening one for me.

Perfectly fine cleanser that does nothing wrong, but for the price I expected some noticeable difference from my usual sensitive-skin drugstore wash. There is none that I can detect. If money is no object it is lovely. Mine is an object.

Didn't expect much from something this basic, but the thin gel works into a soft, low lather and rinses completely. My combination skin feels clean without that tight pull across the cheeks. I use it morning and night before my vitamin C and it's never once interfered. Boring in the best way.

Gentle, sure, but my nose blackheads didn't budge in two months, and I'd hoped for at least a little help. It cleans without irritation and that's the whole story. If you need actual exfoliation, this isn't your product.

My skin thinned in my sixties and foaming cleansers became the enemy. This washes everything away and leaves the little moisture I still make. Paired with my Renewal Creme, my face hasn't felt this comfortable in a decade.

Cleared by my clinic for use four days after microneedling, and it did not sting even then. The oat amino acid base is genuinely mild. Now it is my everyday cleanser, because anything that gentle that still gets sunscreen off deserves permanent counter space.

Bought this for my fifteen year old who was scrubbing her face raw with drugstore stuff. Her breakouts calmed once she stopped stripping her skin, and she actually uses it because it doesn't sting. Small parenting win.

Minus thirty outside, furnace air inside, and my face still isn't flaking. That's new. I've used it twice daily all winter with the glycerin clearly pulling its weight. First winter in years without a raw patch beside my nose.

The cleanser itself is great, mild and quick rinsing, but the bottle is rigid when it's full and cold, and you get a blob the size of a loonie whether you want it or not. Minor thing. Skin's happy, wallet's mostly happy.

r.t: One squeeze does my whole face
r.b: A single squeeze from the bottle works into a soft lather that takes off sunscreen without that squeaky stripped feeling. I use it morning and night and the bottle has lasted almost three months. Doesn't sting my eyes either, which my old foaming wash always did.
Solid everyday cleanser, gentle and quick. The flip cap traps a ring of dried gel that I have to pick out weekly which is mildly gross. Would still recommend, just keep a tissue nearby.
Works beautifully on my dry skin, no tightness, no flakes. I just have a hard time with the price for what is, at the end of the day, soap-adjacent. I'll rebuy, grumbling.

As a morning cleanser and post-workout wash it is faultless. At night it can't handle a full face on its own, I need a cleansing balm first or I wake up with mascara shadows. Fine once you accept it is step two, not a one-and-done.

Love the cleanser, hate refilling silicone travel bottles with a gel this runny. It gets everywhere. Buy the travel size or accept sticky hands, those are your options. Otherwise a genuinely reliable everyday wash.

Every cleanser used to leave my cheeks pink for an hour. This one doesn't. The oat amino acids must be doing something because I rinse and there's just quiet, normal skin. Eight months in and I won't switch.

Sensitive skin that punishes experimentation, that's mine. This gel is soft, rinses vite, and doesn't leave that burning I get from cleansers with perfume. Bought at my derm's office in the spring, already on bottle three. C'est simple et ça marche.

Reactive skin here, the kind that objects to water some days. This rinses off and leaves nothing behind, no heat, no itch, no tight forehead. There's green tea in it apparently, though all I notice is the absence of problems, which is exactly what I want.

My clinic said use only bland cleansers for a week after microneedling, and this was on their short list. Zero sting on freshly needled skin, which tells you everything about how mild it is. Kept using it after, no reason to change.
Wash with this, shave right after, way fewer razor bumps along my jaw. That's the whole review. Two minutes, softer stubble, calmer neck. My wife's the ZO person in the house but this one's mine now.

Cleans my face without stripping it. That is the whole review, and after trying half a dozen fancy cleansers that promised eight other things and irritated me while doing it, that is exactly why I keep buying this one.

r.t: Calm skin starts at the sink
r.b: Switching to this cleanser did more for my redness than two of the treatment serums I was using. Turns out I was aggravating my rosacea twice a day at the sink. Gentle lather, rinses fast, and the green tea in the formula appeals to me even if I can't prove it helps.

Everything else in my ZO lineup does the heavy lifting, the pads, the retinol, all of it. This is the step that keeps the rest tolerable. Skipped it for a week using hotel cleanser and my skin got cranky fast. Lesson learned.

Look, it cleans your face and gets out of the way. Nothing here treats anything, so don't expect miracles from the wash step. As a neutral first move before actual actives it's excellent. Four stars for doing its modest job well.

Using acne pads nightly meant my cleanser had to be a pacifist. This is that. Breakouts still clearing from the salicylic step, but no more flaky patches around my mouth since switching my wash. The combination finally works.
Maybe my hard water, maybe my very oily skin, but I never felt clean. There was a slippery layer after rinsing no matter how long I stood there. Gave it three weeks, went back to my old gel cleanser.

Everyone in this house uses this bottle. My wife takes off makeup with it and a cloth, I use it after shaving, and our teenager uses it around his retinoid routine. Nobody complains, which here is a miracle. It lasts about three months between the three of us.
Took me years to accept my oily skin doesn't need a harsh AM cleanser. This clears the overnight film and my sunscreen goes on smoother after. No squeak, no shine by ten. Settled the debate for me.

Figured a gentle cleanser would leave my oily face feeling half washed. Not this one. Skin is clean and comfortable, no residue, no squeak, and my usual afternoon shine has actually improved since I stopped over-stripping in the morning.
In our sticky summers one wash doesn't quite cut through the day's sweat and sunscreen, so I go twice and the bottle drains fast. Rest of the year it's fine. Seasonal three stars, I guess.
Great cleanser, awkward dispensing. I keep it upside down in the shower caddy so the gel reaches the cap. If ZO sold a pump version I'd buy two. Contents five stars, container three.

r.t: First cleanser my dry skin tolerates
r.b: Washing my face used to mean instant tightness and a race to the moisturizer. With this there is no countdown, my skin feels soft and normal even before I apply anything after. The glycerin must be doing the heavy lifting. Gel texture, minimal foam, no scent.
Started this in early February and it's May and there's still a third left, with twice daily use. The gel spreads far. Cost per wash is actually reasonable when you do the math, which surprised me.

I can wash right over my eyes with no burn, which almost nothing manages. My sensitive skin has been calm since February. It smells like almost nothing, rinses fast, and my redness hasn't flared once. Simple and kind.
After an oil cleanser at night this finishes the job with no residue left behind. My gripe is pace, I finish a bottle in under two months doing it this way. Wish there were a bigger size.
Our water is brutal and most cleansers turn it into a squeaky mess. This one still rinses soft. I don't understand the chemistry, I just know my forehead stopped feeling like a drum after washing.

Rosacea flares taught me to fear new cleansers. This one has never once made my face hot or tight. It is a soft gel that foams just a little, smells like almost nothing, and rinses completely. Boring in the best possible way.

Water alone used to make my face prickle, so an actual cleanser that causes zero reaction feels like a small miracle. Soft gel, barely any scent, rinses in seconds. I've stopped bracing myself at the sink.

r.t: The marine smell won me over
r.b: Nearly returned it after the first sniff, that oceany algae scent is unusual. Glad I didn't. Two months in, my perpetually thirsty sensitive skin stays comfortable through the whole day on one morning application. No stinging even during a flare, which almost never happens for me.

Calgary humidity swings used to leave my skin confused and itchy. Three weeks of this twice daily and the itch is gone. It smells like almost nothing, spreads easily, and a little goes a very long way. Repurchased already.

Does exactly what a rich moisturizer should, nothing more. No irritation on my rosacea-prone cheeks, plays fine with azelaic acid. Four stars because the tube gets hard to squeeze near the end and I know there is product left in there.

Applying this over my retinoid changed everything. No more morning tightness or peeling around my mouth. There's a faint botanical scent that vanishes fast, and my skin has never been calmer through an active-heavy routine.

Used it while healing from an IPL series on my clinic's advice. It never stung, which is more than I can say for anything else I tried that month. The texture is cushiony and the panthenol seemed to speed the flaky stage along. Still using it nightly.

For nighttime it's honestly quite good, my dehydrated cheeks drink it up. But any attempt to wear it under SPF in the morning ends in little rolling flakes, no matter how long I wait. Since I wanted a day and night cream, it's only doing half the job I bought it for.

Skating on the canal used to leave my face raw for days. A pea-size amount of this at night fixed that. Rich, almost balmy texture with panthenol that takes the redness down overnight. A tube lasts me three months.
Not a skincare person. My wife handed me this when my face started cracking in the cold and it just works. Doesn't leave me looking greasy at the office.

Windburn used to be the tax I paid for ski weekends. A solid layer of this before heading up the hill and my cheeks come home intact. It's rich without being sticky under a buff. Also lovely as a plain old night cream the rest of the week.

My esthetician kept nudging me toward this after a season of windburn and flaking. It is a thick cream, squeezes out of the tube like dense frosting, but it sinks in within a couple of minutes and my cheeks stopped peeling within a week. No sting even on freshly exfoliated skin. The faint botanical smell disappears fast.

r.t: Great at night, heavy for day
r.b: Absorbs slower than I would like under sunscreen, so it became my PM step only. In that role it is excellent, my retinol irritation basically vanished. Wish they made a lighter daytime sibling in the same tube format.

Thick creams usually leave a greasy layer that my pillow absorbs instead of my face. This one actually sinks in given fifteen minutes. Been using it nightly through a dry summer. Only reason for four stars is the tube feels small for the price and I finish one in about six weeks.

Bought this in winter and loved it, but come summer it just sits on my combination skin and I get shiny by mid-morning. Shelving it until the temperature drops. Also wish the tube opening were smaller, easy to squeeze out too much.

Even in Arizona AC dryness this keeps my skin comfortable without a slick film. I use it over the B5 gel at night. The marine extract blend sounds like marketing but whatever it is, my flaky forehead is smooth for the first time in years.

Lovely cream for my reactive skin, zero breakouts, and it buffers my tretinoin nights nicely. One star off because the price stings for what is essentially a very good basic moisturizer. The algae extract angle is nice but you are paying for the brand too.

At my age everything feels either greasy or useless. This is neither. I warm a small amount between my fingers and press it in after my serum, morning and evening. The tightness I used to feel by noon is gone. Mature skin, no fragrance issues, no milia.

Rough flaky patches on my cheeks show up every winter, and this year they surrendered within four days. It's a thick cream from the tube but spreads further than you'd expect. Northern winters are no joke and this held the line all season.
Nothing else has kept the eczema-adjacent patches on my jaw quiet through an Edmonton February. Thick, plain, dependable, and it never once made me break out.

Makeup artist here. I keep one in my kit for outdoor weddings because it primes the under eye, adds SPF, and stops concealer from creasing in heat. Clients keep asking what it is. On myself I wear it alone most days. Pricey to restock but it earns its place.

Summer after summer the melasma creeps toward my orbital bone, and regular SPF there makes my eyes water in the Florida heat. This mineral formula does not migrate. The Fair shade is a touch peachy but it doubles as color correction. Applying it feels like a tiny cold spoon.

A mile high, the sun is no joke and my under eyes were always the neglected zone. Trail runs, patio seasons, this has covered it all since January. Cooling applicator is a nice touch after a long run. Wish the tube were bigger but I'd still repurchase.

Hooded lids mean everything transfers to my crease by noon. This doesn't budge. I apply a thin layer, let it set for a minute, and it stays exactly where I put it through a full work day. Circles look less grey too, the peachy undertone does real work.

Court time at 7 am five days a week here. Sunscreen near the eyes always ended in burning halfway through a set. Not once with this one. I keep it in my racquet bag and swipe it on with the wand between matches. The tripeptides seem to be softening my squint lines too.

Eye cream, concealer, and SPF used to be separate steps. Now it's one wand and I'm out the door. The marine complex sounds like marketing but my under eyes hold moisture noticeably better through the day. Carry-on friendly size too, it came to Portugal with me.

Two hundred kilometres a week in the saddle and every sunscreen eventually ran into my eyes. This one has never stung, not once, even on humid climbs. The slight tint hides that I'm perpetually underslept from 5 am starts. My teammates mocked me until they borrowed it.

Hereditary dark circles since my twenties, and this is the first thing that visibly warms them up while the tripeptides do the slow work underneath. The cooling wand feels amazing at 6 am. One swipe under each eye, tap with the ring finger, done. Concealer is for special occasions now.

Pretty finish, tiny amount of product. If you apply it morning and midday like I do for hiking season, the wand empties in about six weeks. The tripeptide and mineral SPF combo is genuinely nice, I just wish the price per gram were less painful.

Solid product, gentle, nice subtle tint, wand feels great. My only hesitation is SPF 35 when the rest of my face wears 50. I top it with a mineral powder on high UV days. If they release a 50 version I'll upgrade in a heartbeat.

Four months of interrupted sleep shows up under my eyes first. My wife handed me her tube as a joke and now we each have our own. Takes thirty seconds, doesn't look like makeup on a guy, and the cold tip actually deflates the morning puff a bit.

Ski patrol for nine winters and the strip between my goggles and buff always burned. Nothing else stayed put at altitude without stinging my eyes when I sweat. This does, plus the tint hides how tired I look after avalanche control mornings. I've bought three tubes so far.

My circles are structural, deep set eyes with shadowing, and after four months of consistent use I can't say they look different. As a tinted eye sunscreen it does its job well and never irritated me. Just set expectations if your issue is anatomy rather than pigment.

Twelve hour hospital shifts wreck my under eyes and I'd resigned myself to looking exhausted forever. Rolled this on before school pickup one day and my kid asked if I'd finally slept. It brightens instantly and the puffiness relief from the cold tip is real. Small tube, but a little goes far.

Dark circles run in my family, so I was mostly buying this for the SPF and tint. Surprise: after about six weeks the actual darkness looks softer even before I apply it. Whether that is the peptides or just diligent sun protection, I will take it.

Beautiful brightening effect, but on my skin it settles into fine lines by mid afternoon unless I set it with a tiny bit of powder. Once I figured that out we've been fine. The SPF and the peptides make it worth the extra step for me.

Porcelain pale here, and most tinted products turn orange on me. The Fair shade of this blends invisibly. I wear it under glasses all day with no pilling where the frames sit. My esthetician commented on my under eye texture last visit, which has never happened before.
Swapped my concealer for this back in the fall and haven't looked back. It is makeup, skincare, and sunscreen in one pass, which is all my morning attention span can handle with two toddlers.

Adore the product, mildly annoyed by the packaging. There's no way to tell how much is left, so it dies without warning, always on a weekday morning. I now keep a backup, which I suppose says something about how much I like it. Brightens, protects, doesn't sting.

Does everything it claims. Circles brighter, no sting, SPF for my commute walk. My issue is purely economic, the tube lasted me nine weeks with daily use plus a lunchtime touch-up, and the price makes that repurchase cadence hurt. If money were no object this would be five stars.
