Used a full tube on my forehead over eleven weeks. Mild improvement, maybe, in certain lighting. My lines are deep and set, and I suspect this works better on early lines than established ones. It also balls up if I apply moisturizer too quickly afterward, so I have to stand around waiting.

It does soften expression lines, my crow's feet look better after two months of consistent use. But the tube is small for the price if you treat more than one area twice a day. I ration it to just my eye corners now.

Twelve weeks of twice-daily use on my nasolabial folds and the change is real. Not filler-level, but the lines catch less shadow and my foundation sits better. I layer it first, wait a minute, then moisturizer. The Argireline plus the layered hyaluronic acid seems to actually do something here.

Between Botox appointments my forehead lines used to creep back by month three. This keeps them at bay until at least month four now, and my injector actually commented. Not a needle replacement, but a genuine stretch of the results.

My injector suggested this to stretch the time between Botox visits, and it honestly does. The gel has a slight silicone slip, dries down invisible, and the crow's feet that usually reappear by month three stayed soft until month four and a half. Worth it for that alone.

r.t: Works until you wash it off
r.b: Plumping is real but strictly temporary for me. Lines look great all day, then I cleanse and everything's back by morning. After three months I expected some lasting change and there isn't any. It's rental smoothing, not ownership.

Deep horizontal forehead lines from years of squinting. Eight weeks in, the two worst ones look about half as deep in morning light. It never pilled under sunscreen either, which surprised me for something this concentrated.

Realistic expectations required. My deep elevens are maybe twenty percent improved after three months of religious use, which I'll take at 58, but this is no needle replacement. Nice under makeup though, almost like a blurring primer on the spots where you apply it.

Our photographer shoots at 8am and I'd cried the night before, obviously. This gel pulled the puffiness down while I did my hair and every closeup came out clean. It tightens as it dries, you can literally feel it working.

After my dad's funeral week I looked how you'd expect. This gel got me presentable for the services each morning. Strange product to be sentimental about, but it carried me through and I've kept it in rotation since.

Spring allergies wreck my under-eyes every year. This spring I used this gel every morning and the swelling was under control by the time I left the house. Cool, lightweight, sinks in clean under sunscreen. First eye product I have finished to the last pump.

Learned quickly that it has to go on bare skin first, before serum, before anything, or it just rolls into bits. Applied correctly it firms nicely for several hours. Just wish the instructions made the order clearer.

On no-makeup days this is fantastic, tight and smooth in minutes. Under concealer it needs a full five minute wait or things start pilling. Knock a star off for the choreography, but the de-puffing itself is the best I've used.

Coming off a string of nights in the ER, my eyes looked bruised. A colleague recommended this and I laughed, then borrowed hers. Bought my own the same week. It won't fix your dark circles but the swelling drops fast.

Instant is a strong word in skincare but this one earns it. I watch the skin under my eyes smooth out over ten minutes, like it has been gently pulled taut. Great before video calls. The airless pump dispenses a tidy amount, no waste, no scooping.
Morning results are impressive but by lunch the effect has mostly faded, and I'm not redoing my makeup to reapply it. Great for events and mornings that matter, less practical as an all-day fix.

However thin I applied it, once it dried the film would ball up into little white bits the second anything touched it, sunscreen, concealer, even my glasses. The tightening was real for the twenty minutes before the flaking started. Returned it.

Put this on at 6 a.m. before my sister's wedding, after crying through the rehearsal dinner the night before. By photos at nine, no bags. The silica gives a soft-focus finish that made concealer almost optional. It has become my day-of ritual for anything important.

Red-eye to Toronto, client meeting at ten, this thing in my carry-on. Dab it on in the airport bathroom and by the time I'm in the cab the puffiness is basically gone. The airless container survives being crushed in a bag too.

It smooths and de-puffs for a few hours, then everything returns exactly as it was. Nothing cumulative after two months, no change to my dark circles. Fine as a party trick, disappointing as a treatment.

The optical silica does not look powdery or obvious, it just quietly diffuses the shadow under my eyes. Paired with the de-puffing, my whole eye area reads fresher. Half a pump per eye is plenty. Bottle is lasting longer than I expected.

Boardroom at nine means this goes on at seven thirty. The caffeine and that algae complex genuinely flatten my under-eye bags within fifteen minutes, and the silica leaves a soft blur that reads as sleep I didn't actually get.

Skeptical of anything promising instant results, but you can feel a light tightening as it sets and the mirror agrees. Puffiness down, and the crepey texture under my eyes looks smoother for hours. Thin layer is the trick. Pile it on and it flakes.

Bags are visibly reduced every morning, no argument there. My hereditary dark circles didn't budge in three months, blur or no blur. If circles are your main issue, temper expectations. For swelling it is excellent.

Like a shot of espresso for my under eyes. I keep it in the fridge door next to the actual espresso and apply it cold, and the combination is unbeatable on humid Atlanta mornings when my face wakes up swollen.

One pump split between both eyes, tap it in, and within about five minutes the bags I wake up with have visibly tightened. There is a faint cooling feel as it sets. I keep it next to my toothbrush so I never skip it. Small pump but a little goes far.
Impressive lift within minutes, but by afternoon the skin under my eyes feels a touch tight and thirsty. I now layer a drop of eye cream on top once it sets and that solved it. Would still buy again.

You get maybe twenty seconds to pat it in and let it set before touching anything else, otherwise it crumbs up. Once I figured out the timing it works well, visible smoothing that lasts most of a workday.

Keep it in the fridge. Cold plus the caffeine is a one-two punch that flattens my morning puffiness in minutes. I'm 45 with hooded eyes and this is the only thing that makes them look more awake without makeup.

Two kids under three and I look human again by 7 a.m. The caffeine and whatever the algae complex is doing shrink the puff fast, and the slight blurring effect softens the dark circles enough that coworkers stopped commenting. Dries down in a minute or two if you keep the layer thin.

Every sunscreen I've owned collected in my beard line like grout. This absorbs before it can. I use a generous squeeze for face and neck before bike commuting and it holds up to drizzle and sweat. No cast even where the stubble is thickest. Small tube is the only knock.

Six hours in the garden means reapplying twice, and layer three of most minerals turns me into a mime. This stays invisible no matter how many coats. At 66 with thin sensitive skin I appreciate that it never dries me out. The tube lives in my potting basket.

No cast on my medium-deep skin, which is rare and appreciated. The finish leans dewy though, and by mid-afternoon my T-zone needs powder. If you are oily, plan for touch-ups. Otherwise this is the most cosmetically elegant mineral SPF I've tried.

Rushed mornings taught me this pills if I apply it within a couple of minutes of my hyaluronic serum. Given proper drying time it behaves perfectly and makeup goes over it like a primer. Four stars because my mornings don't always have proper drying time.

Ninety minutes of hot yoga and this stays out of my eyes, which I consider a miracle of engineering. Applied an hour before class, it just holds. Skin never feels suffocated afterward either. I've converted three people in my studio just by not crying through pigeon pose.

Reactive skin, rosacea prone, and most SPF makes me itch within an hour. Wore this daily for four months, including through a Florida vacation, with zero reactions. It leaves a soft natural finish, not greasy, not flat matte. Genuinely hard to find and worth the price to me.

Sunscreen shopping with rosacea is a minefield. This one has bisabolol and allantoin in it and my cheeks actually look less angry an hour after applying, which has never happened with an SPF before. Goes on white for about twenty seconds then vanishes completely. Third tube and counting.

My combination-oily skin reads this dewy finish as grease by 11 am. Blotting papers became a daily accessory, and powder on top defeated the natural look I bought it for. Dry-skinned friends adore theirs. Skin type match matters a lot here, and mine wasn't it.

Even mid-flare, when my cheeks are cracked and everything burns, I can put this on without wincing. That alone earned my loyalty. It's moisturizing enough that on calm skin days I skip a separate cream. Unscented, absorbs quick, plays fine under my tinted moisturizer.

Bought it for the no-cast claim, kept it for how soothing it is. Through an Ottawa winter my usual chapped red patches around my nose never showed up. I credit the allantoin. Goes on smooth even over flaky bits.

r.t: Face plus neck empties it fast
r.b: Applying properly, face, neck, and ears, I empty a tube in under five weeks. The formula is honestly the nicest mineral I've used, gentle on my reactive cheeks and invisible in a minute. I just wish it came in a bigger size. This sits in the birthday wishlist tier of skincare.

Pregnancy sent me hunting for mineral-only everything and most options felt like diaper cream. This feels like a decent moisturizer that happens to be SPF 50. No smell, which mattered a lot during first trimester nausea. Twenty weeks in and it's the one product I haven't rotated out.

First impressions were mixed, it looks chalky going on and I nearly returned it. Turns out it needs a proper sixty seconds of massaging, then it disappears entirely. Now that I know the trick it's my daily. One star off because that learning curve nearly cost them a customer.

Winter mornings in an old house, this tube gets firm enough that squeezing out a dose is a forearm workout. I've started storing it near the radiator. The sunscreen itself is excellent, no cast on my ruddy skin and no sting on the patch of eczema at my temple.

Performs beautifully, truly invisible, gentle on my reactive cheeks. But I go through a tube in six weeks using the proper amount for face and neck, and at this price that stings more than the sunscreen ever did.

A basal cell on my nose last year turned me into a daily sunscreen person overnight. Tried five brands in two months. This is the one I stuck with because there's no film, no smell, and no excuse not to wear it. My dermatologist sees me twice a year now and approves.

Breakout roulette is why I avoided sunscreen for years. Three months of daily wear, including gym days, and not a single new clogged pore I can blame on it. Lightweight, sinks in, done. It's become the boring reliable part of my routine, which is the highest compliment I can give.
Use it face and scalp daily. No shine dome effect, no residue on hats, no sting when I sweat on the seawall run. First zinc sunscreen I have finished a full tube of instead of abandoning in a drawer.

r.t: Desert hikes outlast the water resistance
r.b: For daily wear this is close to perfect. On long desert hikes with heavy sweat I find myself reapplying more often than the label's eighty minutes, my shoulders caught some color through it once. Face stayed protected though. It's now my everyday tube while a sport formula handles the trail.

Texture is closer to a good lotion than a sunscreen. I skip moisturizer on humid days and just use this. No white cast, no pilling under powder, no stinging eyes at the gym. Repurchased before the first tube ran out because I got nervous.

Skeptical is an understatement, every mineral SPF claiming no white cast has lied to me. This one rubbed into my medium-deep skin and just went away. My mum borrowed it, she's deeper than me, same result. We now split orders. Slight glow, not shine, and no stinging around the eyes.

Zero complaints about the sunscreen itself; it never irritates my skin and vanishes on application. My gripe is practical: the cap cracked in my beach bag two weeks in and the tube gets messy. Product five stars, packaging three.

On my very fair dry skin it applies well and feels soothing, but there is a persistent sheen that reads sweaty in photos rather than glowy. Fine for errands, not for events. I also wish the water resistance held up better through a hot yoga class.

Deep skin tone here and I have been burned, figuratively, by every so-called invisible mineral sunscreen on the market. This one actually disappears. Creamy out of the tube, spreads easily, and within a minute there is no trace. My reactive cheeks didn't flare once all summer.

Two big dogs, three walks a day, Tennessee humidity. Everything else I tried eventually ran into my eyes and burned like chlorine. Months of use and this hasn't stung once, even dripping sweat. Rubs in fast enough that the dogs don't lose patience. I buy two tubes at a time now.

Mineral sunscreens usually leave my olive complexion looking faintly grey, like a bad photo filter. Not this one. It disappears within a minute of rubbing it in and my skin just looks like skin, slightly smoother if anything. I've been through two tubes since spring and stopped shopping around.

Sits perfectly under foundation with no shifting or graying. One squeeze covers my face and neck, absorbs in under a minute, and my combination skin stays comfortable all day. My teenager with eczema-prone skin borrows it constantly, which says a lot.

Performs well, rubs in clear, no irritation on my sensitive skin. But comparing it honestly against the mineral SPF I buy at the pharmacy for a third of the price, I can't identify what the extra money bought me. If budget is no issue, lovely. Mine is an issue.

In person it looks natural, but on video calls and in flash photos there's a subtle gleam on my forehead. I work in sales with cameras on all day, so I add powder. Otherwise it's comfortable, unscented, and hasn't irritated the psoriasis patch near my ear. Solid four.

Been through maybe fifteen mineral sunscreens. This is the first with 10 percent zinc that my seborrheic-dermatitis-prone face tolerates every single day. Elegant texture, invisible finish, does not cling to dry patches. Only wish the tube were bigger.

Confession, I went most of my adult life bare faced because I hated how sunscreen felt. A friend squeezed some of this onto my hand at a picnic and I couldn't feel where it was after a minute. Bought my own that week. Ten months of daily wear says it stuck.

Post-IPL my derm said mineral only, nothing fragranced. This checks every box: unscented, zero sting even right after treatment, and it layers over my serums without balling up. The bisabolol seems to actually calm my cheeks rather than just not irritate them.

Prairie winter plus nightly retinol left my face flaky and reactive, and chemical sunscreens were burning on application. This goes over the flakiness without emphasizing it and never once tingled. The tremella extract seems to add a bit of hydration too. My derm nodded approvingly when I named it.

Feels like slightly thick water going on and disappears in about ten seconds. I press it into damp skin after cleansing and follow with moisturizer. Post-laser my clinic told me to keep using it and it never once stung on healing skin.

r.t: Even my under eyes tolerate it
r.b: Most hydrating serums sting near my eyes. This one doesn't, so I take it right up to the orbital bone before eye cream. Fine crinkles under my eyes look better hydrated and the whole thing takes fifteen seconds.

r.t: Bought for him, kept by me
r.b: Got this for my husband's dehydrated post-shave skin, then stole it because his results were annoyingly good. It's the rare product we can share since it's unscented and works on his oily skin and my combination skin equally. Now we just buy two.

Acne-prone but flaky, the worst of both worlds. This hydrates deeply with nothing that clogs. Eight weeks in, no new congestion and my skin stopped overproducing oil to compensate. The gel feels like nothing on the skin once it settles.

r.t: The step I didn't know was missing
r.b: Oily skin here, so I always skipped hydrators, then my esthetician explained dehydrated oily skin and it clicked. This gel gives water with none of the heaviness and my skin actually produces less oil now. Weird but true. A dropper of it under sunscreen every morning.

r.t: The unsung step in my routine
r.b: Every flashy serum I own gets rotated out eventually but this stays. It buffers both my morning vitamin C and my nighttime retinal so neither one stings. There's no scent, no color, no drama, and my skin drinks it. I go through a bottle about every three months.

Everything in my routine does two or three jobs except this, which only hydrates. It does that really well and never conflicts with actives, so it stays. Just wish there were a little niacinamide or something in there for the money.

Two drops on damp skin, then my moisturizer goes on top and nothing pills. I use it morning and night and my combination skin stopped doing that tight-but-shiny thing by the second week. It's fragrance free, sinks in fast, and plays nice with tretinoin. Wish the bottle were bigger for the price but I'm not stopping.

Used it after microneedling on my nurse's suggestion. Zero sting, immediate relief from the tight feeling, and my skin drank it up for days. It has stayed in my routine long after healing. Unscented and clean-feeling in the best way.
Post-shower at the gym, two drops, done. It absorbs before I've finished packing my bag and my face doesn't feel stripped from the locker room cleanser anymore.

Love the formula, terrified of the packaging. It's a slick glass bottle and my bathroom has tile floors. I decant into a pump now. The gel itself is soothing and my redness-prone skin has zero complaints after four months.

Started 0.5 retinol in December, which was a mistake in this climate, and my forehead went scaly. Three nights of this gel under a bland cream and the flaking settled. It feels like water, smells like nothing, and one bottle has lasted me since. Genuinely soothing.

No fragrance, no sting, no pilling under sunscreen. Just a light gel that makes every moisturizer I own work better. I have sensitive skin that protests most serums and this one has never caused a single problem in eight months.

Minus thirty outside, furnace air inside, and my face used to crack by January. Adding this gel morning and night was the single change this year and I haven't had one flaky patch. I keep a second bottle in my desk.

Oily skin that still dehydrates in Alberta winters is an annoying combination. This gel fixed it. Water-light, absorbs in seconds, and my moisturizer step became optional on milder days. A bottle lasts me four months.

Nothing in here to react to. My rosacea-prone face accepts it without a single flush, which I can't say for most serums, and the B5 seems to speed up healing when I do flare. Simple ingredient list, does what it says.

r.t: Teen daughter and I both use it
r.b: Her benzoyl peroxide was wrecking her barrier and my tretinoin was doing the same to mine. One bottle of this on the bathroom counter fixed both problems. Gentle enough for a fifteen-year-old, effective enough for a forty-five-year-old.
Absorbs nicely and adds a bit of plumpness, but honestly I cannot tell it apart from hyaluronic serums a third the price. If money were no object I'd keep it around. It isn't, so I'll not.

My dermatologist suggested a plain hyaluronic gel while I finished my course and this was the one the clinic stocked. Honestly it carried me through. No sting on flaky patches, the panthenol seems to calm things, and it never broke me out. One dropper's worth does my whole face.

CE Ferulic alone left my cheeks tight by noon. Two drops of this on top and the tightness is gone without adding any oil. They clearly designed it as a layering piece and it plays that role perfectly.

Underwhelmed, honestly. It hydrates lightly, absorbs quick, doesn't irritate. But friends talked this up like it transformed their skin and mine looks exactly the same after two months. Maybe my moisturizer was already doing the job. Not bad, just not necessary for me.

Does the hydration job well and never breaks me out. The tacky phase lasts a good sixty to ninety seconds on me though, and if I rush my sunscreen it drags. Minor thing, but at this price minor things count.

I fly four days a week and cabin air destroys my face. A few drops of this before boarding and again at the hotel keeps everything comfortable. It's the only serum I've used that doesn't ball up when I reapply over makeup residue. Third bottle.

As a pure hyaluronic gel it's excellent, and my skin holds onto moisture noticeably better when I use it. But it's water thin and I'm through the bottle in ten weeks. There are cheaper HA serums that get you eighty percent of the way. I keep repurchasing anyway, which tells you something.

In winter I layer it under Triple Lipid, in summer it replaces moisturizer entirely under SPF. Fine lines on my forehead look softer when my skin is this well hydrated. It has that faint tacky grip for a minute, which actually helps my next layer spread evenly.

No matter how long I waited, this gel balled up the second I applied sunscreen over it. Tried less product, tried pressing it in, same result. It hydrates fine alone at night but I bought it for daytime layering and it failed at that on my skin.

It hydrates, full stop. Don't expect brightening or line smoothing because that's not what a B5 gel is for. I apply it on damp skin after cleansing and my SPF spreads better over it. Four stars because the dropper drips down the neck of the bottle.

Moved from Houston humidity to Phoenix dry heat and this was the only skincare that made the trip without issues. In the desert I layer a cream over it, back home I wore it alone. Lightweight either way and my pores never clog.

Rarely repurchase anything, but this earned it. Light gel, sinks in fast, plays under everything, and my skin has looked quietly healthier since February. Nothing dramatic to report and that is exactly the point.

r.t: Nice, but you need a sealant
r.b: Hyaluronic acid pulls water in but doesn't hold it, so if you don't put a cream over this you can end up drier. Learned that the hard way in week one. Used correctly it's lovely and my fine dehydration lines look softer by afternoon.

r.t: One dropper, whole face and neck
r.b: A little spreads a long way when your skin is damp. I'm sixty-one, my skin is thin and easily upset, and this has been gentle from day one. Lines around my mouth look less etched when I'm consistent with it.

Nightly under my cream and I wake up with that bounce dehydrated skin forgets it can have. The panthenol seems to keep my face calm through acid nights too. Dropper is easy to control, three drops covers everything.

Been using it for half a year. Skin stays comfortable, makeup applies smoother, nothing has gone wrong. It's the beige sedan of serums and sometimes that's exactly what you want. Knock a star off for the price of what's essentially fancy water done well.

Fifty-six and my skin changed almost overnight last year. This gel under my usual cream got the tight, itchy feeling under control within a week. I've since added it to my neck and chest too. The dropper gives exactly the right amount.

Genuinely nice hydrator that livened up my dull winter skin within a couple of weeks. Four stars because 30 ml of what is mostly hyaluronic acid and B5 is priced like a specialty treatment. Cheaper dupes exist; this one is just more elegant.

Three drops pressed onto damp skin between my retinol and moisturizer stopped the flaking within a week. It is a clear gel, no scent, slightly tacky for a minute, then gone. Simple product done extremely well.

r.t: Just okay for truly dry skin
r.b: If your skin is dehydrated this will help, but mine is properly dry and it wasn't enough on its own. In a Winnipeg February I still needed a heavy cream over it, and at that point I'm not sure the gel added much. Nice texture though, absorbs in seconds.

Swapped my retinol for this during pregnancy with my derm's okay and honestly might not go back. Skin stays glowy and smooth, zero sting, and it doesn't pill under sunscreen. The pump gives exactly the right amount, no dropper mess.

My cheeks have had rough dry patches for years that scrubs only aggravated. Six weeks of this twice a day and I keep touching my face because the texture change is that noticeable. It works without any acid sting, which still confuses me, but I'll allow it.

To be clear, it won't erase pitted scars, but the shallow ones on my cheeks catch less light now and makeup doesn't sink into them the same way. That took about ten weeks. It also never once irritated the eczema patch near my jaw, which is unheard of.

Sides of my nose flaked year round and concealer made it worse. Two weeks of this nightly and the area is finally smooth. Kept going and now my whole face has that fresh look you get after a facial. Unscented, absorbs cleanly, pump is precise.

Very good with one caveat: if I use it the same night as my prescription tretinoin my face gets tight and flaky, so it lives on my off nights. On that schedule it keeps the glow up between retinoid nights with no drama.

Ring lights are cruel to bumpy skin. After two months my forehead reads smooth on camera, no filter needed. It plays fine with my salicylic cleanser and doesn't add shine, which for oily skin is half the battle.

The bumpy texture on my forehead that no scrub could fix has mostly leveled out after a month. This is sneaky exfoliation, it feels like a hydrating serum going on but resurfaces like an acid. Fragrance-free, plays fine under moisturizer.

r.t: Radiance back after a dull decade
r.b: Post-fifty my skin went flat and powdery looking no matter what I fed it. Two pumps of this every night brought back an actual light-catching finish by week five. My daughter noticed before I said anything. No burn, no peeling, just steady change.

Texture improvement is legit, my forehead bumps are mostly gone after seven weeks. The promised radiance is subtler, my tone looks about the same. Pairs well under a vitamin C in the morning though, and two pumps covers the whole face.

Maybe my expectations were off, but after a full bottle over three months I see only a mild improvement in texture. Nothing negative happened, it just underwhelmed. If you have real texture issues, an actual acid or retinoid will move faster.

Acids of every kind have lit my face up like a sunburn. This uses a hydroxyethyl urea complex instead and my skin genuinely cannot tell it's being exfoliated. Flaky patches around my nose resolved in two weeks and my redness never budged upward. Small miracle for reactive skin.

Quarterly facials instead of every six weeks, that's my result. My esthetician does light peels and even she admitted my skin needed less work lately. This serum is the only change. It nudges dead skin off without the post-peel redness so I stay glowy between visits.

Can't tolerate retinoids at all, and this has become my texture treatment instead. Pores look cleaner, the little closed comedones are gone, and my skin has an even, polished look by morning. Also layers beautifully with the B5 gel when winter hits.

Those tiny closed comedones on my chin that never became pimples but never left? Gone after about five weeks. I press two pumps in at night after cleansing. It feels more like a hydrating serum than an exfoliant, which makes the results feel a bit like a magic trick.

Nearly seven weeks passed before my texture changed enough to notice, which is a long time to keep faith at this price. Results are real now, smoother cheeks and smaller-looking pores, but pack patience with your purchase.

I use tretinoin three nights a week and this on the off nights. Texture has improved faster than tret alone ever managed and there's no flaking. Docked a star because the pump sputters when the bottle gets low and you lose product.

Nothing obvious for two weeks, then people started asking if I had been on vacation. It smooths and brightens gradually while hydrating, no flakes, no peeling phase. I use two pumps at night and my vitamin C in the morning.

Resurfacing-wise it delivers, my skin looks brighter and feels sanded smooth in a good way. The hydration claims are oversold for my dry skin though; I still need a proper serum and cream on top or I feel tight by midnight.

r.t: Strong results, silly price per ml
r.b: Does it resurface? Yes, gently and reliably, and I've repurchased once. But I go through a bottle in nine weeks at two pumps a night and the cost adds up fast. If it were thirty dollars cheaper this would be a forever product.

The results are decent, my texture is maybe fifteen percent smoother after two months, but the finish is slightly tacky and my moisturizer drags over it. In humid weather I skip it entirely. If the feel doesn't bother you, the formula clearly functions.

Sixty-three years of weather on this face. Three months of this every night and my wife says my skin finally feels like skin again. No irritation whatsoever, which at my age and with my patience is the whole battle.

Consistent soft radiance since week three, and no purging or peeling at any point. Withholding the fifth star only because the pump started sputtering and spitting product once the bottle got half empty.

Coming from glycolic this took longer to show, about twice as long honestly, but I also haven't had a single day of irritation since switching. That trade is worth it for my thin, easily annoyed skin. Wish they sold a bigger size.

r.t: Tried it on my arms too
r.b: Face results were great, smoother in about a month, so I started using the last bit of each pump on the rough bumps on my upper arms. Softer there too. It's hydrating enough that neither spot ever felt stripped. Buying my third bottle.

Acids make my face angry, so a resurfacing serum with zero sting felt too good to be true. Six weeks of nightly use and my cheeks are smoother than any glycolic ever got them, minus the redness. Watery texture from the pump, sinks in instantly.

Foundation used to cling to the dry patches around my nose by 2 p.m. A month of this at night and those patches are gone, so my base applies like a filter. Feels like water, smells like nothing, works like an acid without acting like one.

After two bottles over five months I honestly can't point to a change. My skin was in decent shape to start, so maybe there wasn't much to fix. It never irritated and layered fine, but I can't justify a third bottle on faith.

Here is the thing: nothing flashy happens, your skin just steadily looks more rested, firmer, and smoother until one day an old photo shocks you. Ten months and two bottles in. Unscented, absorbs in under a minute, works for my combination skin even in summer.

r.t: Cut my routine by two steps
r.b: One pump covers face and neck, so I dropped my separate neck cream and my old moisturizer. Simplified my whole routine and my skin looks better than when I used four products. The airless pump gets every last bit out too.

At 58 my jawline was starting to blur and my neck looked older than my face. Five months of this, morning and night, and photos from my daughter's wedding actually surprised me. The peptides are doing something real here.

Using it morning and night on face, neck, and chest since January. By month two the crepey texture on my neck looked tighter, and by month four even my skeptical hairdresser commented. It is a substantial cream that somehow absorbs without residue. The airless pump is hygienic and precise.

r.t: Great for face, meh for neck
r.b: My face loves it, smoother texture and a bit of bounce within weeks. My neck, which is why I bought it, has improved much less. Maybe neck skin is just stubborn. Still a good cream, just uneven results for me.

Working from home means staring at my own sagging chin on video calls all day. Three months of this cream and I've stopped angling the camera up. Firmer along the jaw, and zero irritation even next to my retinol nights.

Four months of consistent use, morning and night, and I can't honestly say my jawline looks different. Skin feels nicer, sure, hydrated and smooth, but at this price I wanted lift and I'm not seeing it.

Always thought expensive creams were pure marketing. My wife's bottle changed my mind when my perpetually dry neck stopped flaking inside two weeks and the lines from looking down at my phone softened by month three. I bought my own so we stop fighting over hers.

Most firming creams make my neck itch within days. This one has been completely calm on me since February, and the skin below my jaw feels denser somehow. Pricey, but I stretched one bottle over four months using a single pump.

Menopause turned my skin to paper, and this cream gives it substance again. Plumper cheeks by week three, firmer feel along the jaw by month two. The SYN-AKE peptide sounds like a gimmick but something in here is pulling real weight.

Not much happened for the first eight weeks and I nearly quit. Around month three the lines on my neck started looking softer and now I get it. Four stars because that wait is real and the price makes waiting painful.

Committed for twelve weeks before I could honestly say my neck looked different. It does now, slightly lifted and less crepey, but anyone expecting a one month miracle at this price will be disappointed. Texture and pump are faultless.

Silky, cushiony, spreads over face and throat with one and a half pumps. My makeup applies better over it than over my old primer. Six weeks in, the fine lines across my neck catch less light. This is the first neck product I have actually finished.

Honestly didn't believe the SYN-AKE claims, sounded like snake oil, pun intended. But the horizontal lines across my throat are visibly shallower after about ten weeks. It's a rich cream that sinks in fully before I button my collar.

The results on my neck are real and the texture is the nicest I've used. But twice-daily use on face, neck, and chest empties the pump in about seven weeks and the repurchase hurts every time. I now save it for neck only.
Still impressed half a year later, which never happens with me and skincare. Texture on my neck is smoother, the crepey look under my chin has eased, and it layers under makeup without any slip.

Peptides over promises: my jawline looks firmer and the skin on my neck bounces back when pinched, something I tested weekly like a nerd. Four months in. No fragrance issues, no breakouts, and the airless pump keeps everything fresh to the last dose.

r.t: Broke me out along the jaw
r.b: Beautiful texture, but within ten days I had clusters of small bumps along my jawline and neck exactly where I applied it, and they cleared when I stopped. Tried reintroducing twice with the same result. My skin is normally not fussy, so this one stung at this price.

Rich enough for my dry skin in a Quebec winter yet it never leaves that greasy film on my pillow. I'd give five stars if the results were as impressive as the texture. They're good, but modest so far.

Twenty years at a desk gave me rings around my neck. This has visibly softened the two shallow ones since March; the deep one is a longer project. The cream feels luxurious without being heavy and never pills over my morning antioxidant serum.

Those necklace rings I've had since my forties are softer now. Not gone, but softer enough that I noticed in the mirror before I remembered I was using anything. Takes a couple of months, so be patient with it.

Simplified my whole routine. Rich enough for my dry 60-year-old face, absorbs fast enough that I can dress right after doing my neck. The horizontal necklace lines are softer after three months. Expensive, yes, but it replaced two products.

From spring to fall it is perfect on its own. In a Winnipeg February my dry cheeks needed an oil on top or I felt tight by evening. The firming effects are gradual but honest. Four stars as a moisturizer, five as a treatment.

Colorado sun at elevation is unforgiving and I used to burn through lesser sunscreens on a single hike. Two summers of fourteeners with this and not one burn. It is water resistant for real, still working after creek crossings and heavy sweat.

Working outdoor day camp means sunscreen is basically my uniform. This size survives a whole session where the regular tubes died in ten days. The waterproof claim holds through canoe tipping practice, tested more times than I'd like. No breakouts despite reapplying over sweat for weeks.

Applied it on my toddler and myself all through June. Rubs in fast, leaves a light sheen rather than a white film, and has no perfume smell, just a faint clean scent that fades. The 226 gram bottle is genuinely economical compared to buying multiple small tubes.

Sand, sweat, and ocean dips every Sunday and I stopped coming home pink. Reapply once mid-session and it truly lasts. Light sheen on the skin but no grease slick, and it has never broken out my chest or back.

Protection is flawless, no burns all year including a Mexico trip in January. Docked a star because it leaves a noticeable shine that shows up in photos, and the big bottle is awkward to pack for carry-on travel.

Performs exactly as promised through runs and open water swims. Getting the last fifth out of the large bottle takes patience and shaking. Also a touch shiny on the face for daily office wear; I keep it strictly for sport days.

With three kids in summer soccer, sunscreen negotiations happen every weekend. This goes on smoothly, doesn't sting when they sweat it into their eyes, and one coat lasts a tournament morning. The large size stretched from June to late August, which no other bottle has managed.

Swim, bike, run, sweat: this stays put through all of it. I apply once before long Saturday rides and my cyclist tan lines have basically stopped getting worse. No greasy hands on the handlebars after applying, which matters more than people think.

The math works out way cheaper per gram than the small tube and we go through a lot between ball tournaments and the lake. Only knock is the big tube doesn't fit any beach bag pocket and it's heavy for day hikes. We decant into a travel bottle now. No burns all August.

Lives in my golf bag from May through September. Goes on my arms, legs, neck, and face before every round, never greasy on the grip, never stings my eyes on hot days. A single big bottle covered the entire season with some left over.

Both my daughters react to most drugstore sunscreens with bumps and redness. Zero reactions with this one all summer, and the zinc-based formula gives me peace of mind. It spreads easier than the pure mineral ones we tried, so nobody hides when the bottle comes out.

We bought the big 226 gram size for our Muskoka week and it handled two adults and three kids for the entire trip. Nobody burned, nobody complained about stinging eyes, and it rubbed in without the ghost-white look. Refilling the beach bag with one bottle instead of four little tubes is the dream.

r.t: Finally a size that matches usage
r.b: Small tubes disappear in a week when you reapply properly, so the 226 gram size just makes sense. Kept it by the cottage door all July for swims and tubing, and it's still going. Same trusted formula, rubs in clean, no sting when lake water hits your face.

On the water four days a week all season. Salt spray, sweat, sun off the waves, and this held for full mornings between reapplications. Vitamin E or not, what sold me is that my forearms stopped peeling for the first summer in years.

Great on arms and shoulders, no burns hiking. On my face it slid into my eyes during a hard run around mile four and stung for a solid ten minutes, which is the one thing a sport sunscreen should never do to me. Body only from now on.

Nothing sets my face off like a new moisturizer, so I patch tested this for a week first. Total non-event, in the best way. No sting, no bumps, just calm cushioned skin, and I suspect the oat kernel extract deserves the credit. It gets me through every flare now.

It took a good month before I saw more than basic moisturizing. Around week five my skin started looking bouncier, so the TriHex stuff may be real, just not fast. Nice that it is unscented. Knocking a star for the pace and the price.

r.t: Love it, wish it lasted longer
r.b: Beautiful cream, truly. Rich, calming, sinks in clean, and my flaky forehead stayed smooth for the first winter in years. But I go through a pump in six weeks using it twice daily, and the repurchase price makes me wince every time. Four stars from my wallet, five from my face.

Airless pump means the last bit is as fresh as the first, which matters when a cream costs this much. One pump does my whole face. My skin drinks it in overnight and I wake up without that tight morning feeling I've had for years.

Sadly my combination skin couldn't handle it. Cheeks loved the richness but I got clogged pores along my chin and jaw within two weeks. Stopped, cleared, tried again, same result. If your skin is truly dry this is probably lovely. Mine just isn't dry enough.

Dry patches used to camp on my cheeks from November through March. Since switching my night cream to this, none. Thick in the hand but it spreads further than you'd expect, so one pump handles face and neck. Unexpected bonus, my skin feels slightly bouncier, maybe the peptides.

Sandwich method saved my retinol routine and this is the bread. Thick, almost balm-like out of the airless pump, but it melts down and doesn't sit greasy. Zero flaking since I started, even on 0.05 tret nights. A little goes far.

Bought it for post-shave irritation and dry Manitoba winters. Works for both. Now my wife uses it over her retinol nights so we are going through it twice as fast. Would appreciate a bigger size option.

Calgary chinooks destroy my skin every January and this is the first moisturizer that kept the windburn redness off my cheeks. I layer it over the Restorative Skin Complex at night. Two pumps covers face and neck. A jar this rich would feel like petroleum, somehow this doesn't.

December here is a skin destroyer and this held the line. I use it as my last step at night and wake up with comfortable, plump skin instead of that tight morning feeling. Heavier than my summer cream but never suffocating. The pump keeps it hygienic too.

Cream itself is lovely, my flaking around the eyebrows stopped in about ten days. The pump started sputtering with maybe a fifth left and I had to bang it on the counter to get product out. For this price the packaging should work to the last gram.

Sent home from my clinic with this after a Halo treatment and it kept the tight, sandpapery feeling away for the whole recovery week. Thick cream out of the airless pump but it melts in without sitting greasy. Now I use it every winter night. Zero sting even on freshly resurfaced skin.

Used this twice a day for a week after microneedling on my derm's instructions. Redness settled faster than my previous session where I just used a drugstore cream, and nothing stung going on. The TriHex peptides are supposedly working underneath but honestly I bought it again for the texture alone.

Right after my IPL session my skin felt like shrink wrap. Two nights of this and the tightness was gone, with no peeling at all this round. My derm said it supports the TriHex serum I already use, and the pair really does seem to work faster together. Pricey, worth it.

r.t: Wonderful at night, heavy for day
r.b: Too rich to sit under sunscreen and makeup for me, it takes a long time to fully settle. As a night cream though it is lovely, and my skin looks calmer in the morning. Four stars because I wanted a do-everything cream and this is strictly PM in my routine.

r.t: Heavy for July, perfect for February
r.b: Half the year this is perfect. Once the humidity rises it's too much for me, I get shiny by noon if I use it in the morning. Night use only in warm months solved it. Texture and calming effect are excellent, just know it's a genuinely rich cream.

No fragrance, no essential oils, no drama. I react to almost every rich cream and this one gave me nothing but comfort. By week two the flaky patches around my nose were gone. It is expensive, but I stopped needing a separate barrier balm, so it evens out.

Whipped, dense, a little goes far. The tremella and shea combo reads heavy on paper but it absorbs before I hit the pillow. Three weeks in, the crepey feel on my cheeks softened noticeably. My esthetician noticed before I said anything.

Finding a cream this rich that doesn't leave a slick has taken me years. The shea gives it real cushion but it settles almost powdery after a few minutes. My dry patches around the nose disappeared inside two weeks. No fragrance that my sensitive nose can detect.

Pilled under my mineral SPF almost every morning and felt like a film by afternoon on my oilier T-zone. My dry cheeks liked it fine. If your whole face is dry this probably deserves five stars, mine isn't, lesson learned.

Genuinely rich texture, almost balm-like, yet twenty minutes later my face just feels cushioned, not coated. The oat kernel extract seems to be doing something because the itchy patches along my jaw stopped within days. Pump is airless so nothing oxidizes or gets gunky.

r.t: Weirdly effective for something so simple
r.b: Skeptical because the ingredient list is basically two things, but the 120 ppm hypochlorous concentration seems to matter. Post-shave bumps on my neck are way down. I use it after cleansing, let it dry, then serum. Bottle lasted me about two months of daily use.

Retired my old astringent toner for this and my 58-year-old skin thanked me immediately. No sting, no tightness, just calm. It layers under everything without any residue. A bottle lasts me about seven weeks at two uses a day.

Hard to justify the cost when the ingredients read like fancy water, and yet my dermatitis patches flare less when I use it consistently. I ration it to twice a day. Wish the bottle were bigger for the price, hence four stars.

The routine is stupidly simple and that's why it sticks. I mist, give it a minute, then seal with my cream. My reactive cheeks have been calmer these past three months than in years. One tip, don't let it fully evaporate before moisturizing or you'll feel tight.

First spray had me worried, it genuinely smells like a pool for a few seconds. Then it's gone and so is the irritation I've fought along my hairline for years. Docking a star for the scent surprise, keeping it in my routine regardless.

Post IPL my face was hot, tight, and blotchy, and this was the only thing my clinic allowed for 48 hours. It kept me comfortable enough to skip the ice packs. Healing looked ahead of schedule at my follow-up. Full bottle used, replacement ordered.

Read the ingredient list and laughed, then my dermatologist told me to try it anyway after a laser session. My face healed faster than the previous round and the itchy phase basically didn't happen. Now I use it after every workout too. I get it now.

Impulse bought it at my clinic before a peel. It kept everything comfortable during the flaky week and I've since used it on bug bites and razor burn. Only complaint is the sprayer occasionally spits instead of misting when the bottle gets low.

Rosacea flares used to take days to settle. A few mists of this morning and night and the heat comes down by evening. Nothing else in my routine changed, so I am crediting this little spray. No residue, no film, my moisturizer goes right over it.

When my rosacea flares I mist this and the stinging calms down within the hour. Nothing else I own works that fast. It smells faintly of swimming pool for about thirty seconds, then nothing. I keep one in the bathroom and one in my bag.

Love the calm it gives my skin after retinol nights, but I empty a bottle in about a month misting twice daily. The cost adds up. Effective and gentle, absolutely, I just wish there were a bigger size.

Used the entire bottle over two months, misting twice a day like directed. My skin is maybe slightly calmer. For pennies' worth of ingredients this needs to deliver more than maybe. People with truly reactive skin will probably get more out of it than I did.

My skin reacts to practically everything, including water some days. This is one of maybe three products that cause zero response. I mist after cleansing and my usual background redness has dialed way down over a couple of months. Boring in the best possible way.

Does calm my skin down, no question. The catch is it evaporates quickly and if I don't follow with moisturizer within a minute my face feels tighter than before. Fine once you learn the rhythm. Four stars for the extra step it demands.

Hockey mom who plays herself twice a week. Misting under and after the helmet cleared up the forehead bumps I have fought for two seasons. Takes two seconds, dries in maybe thirty. My teenager started stealing it, which says everything.

Brought the bottle to my appointment expecting to get scolded about gimmicks. Instead she said hypochlorous acid is legit and to keep going. Six months in, fewer random irritated patches and my post-shave redness settles fast. That endorsement plus results is enough for me.

Finished the whole bottle over six weeks on normal skin with no procedures in between and noticed very little beyond a nice cooling feel. I suspect this shines post-treatment or on reactive skin. On boring healthy skin it was a pleasant shrug.

r.t: Nothing to feel, plenty to see
r.b: It's odd reviewing a product you can't feel working. There's no texture, no scent after a moment, no sensation. But my flush settles faster and my skin barrier survived winter, so something's happening. Four stars because the price for what it is stings a little.

r.t: Left my face tighter than before
r.b: Every mist evaporated into a tight, squeaky feeling no matter how fast I moisturized after. My dry skin fought this for three weeks before I quit. It clearly works for my sister's reactive skin so I passed the bottle along, but for very dry types like me, be careful.

Picked it up for my wife's post-microneedling care and ended up misting my fresh forearm tattoo with it. Healed clean, no crusting drama, artist was impressed. We now fight over the bottle. Buying two next time.

Keep it in my gym bag and mist after every workout before I can shower. The chin breakouts I blamed on sweat basically stopped within a month. It is just hypochlorous acid and electrolyzed water, but the concentration and the nozzle are better than the cheap ones I tried.

Helpful for calming things down after my clinic treatments, less impressive for everyday use. On normal weeks I honestly can't tell if it's doing anything. I'll repurchase around procedures only. It's fine, it's just not the daily transformation some reviews promised me.

Barber suggested hypochlorous acid for the irritation under my beard and this was the one my clinic stocked. Two sprays after washing, morning and night. The bumps along my jaw cleared in about five days and haven't returned in two months.

r.t: Bought for procedures, kept for daily
r.b: Originally got it for after my wife's microneedling appointments, then read up on hypochlorous and started misting my own face post-run. Ingrown hairs and random chin spots both improved. It is the least fussy product on our shelf.

Nothing hormonal ever fully goes away, but misting this twice a day has cut my chin breakouts roughly in half since June. It doesn't dry me out like my old toner did either. Spray nozzle gives a genuinely fine mist, not a squirt.

Training outside in Tennessee summer meant constant clogged pores until I started misting this right after sessions. Breakouts are down noticeably over the last two months. Not a miracle, my bad diet weeks still show up on my face, but it removed one whole category of problem.

Grabbed this off my shelf in desperation after a patio sunburn and the relief was almost instant. The heat and tightness settled within minutes. I already loved it for post-facial redness but now it's earned year-round status. Fine even mist, no sputtering.

Spritzed this every few hours after microneedling and had noticeably less crusting and tightness than my first session without it. The mist is ultra fine, no sting at all on raw skin. Smells faintly like a swimming pool for about ten seconds, then nothing.

Long-haul flights used to leave my face wrecked. Misted this every couple of hours from Edmonton to Frankfurt and landed with completely calm skin. Security-friendly size too. It's water with a job, and it does the job.

r.t: My reactive skin's new best friend
r.b: Every toner I've tried in five years stung. This doesn't, at all. It has quietly replaced that step for me morning and night. Redness after cleansing settles in minutes instead of an hour. Buying a backup before I run out.

Respirator all day at the shop used to mean a broken-out chin by Friday. Now I spray this at every break and the difference is night and day. Took maybe two weeks to see it fully. Simple stuff, electrolyzed water and hypochlorous acid, but it delivers.

There is a definite chlorine whiff when you spray, which nobody warns you about with hypochlorous. It fades fast and the results are real, my post-waxing redness settles in half the time. Just do not expect a spa smell.

Cat scratches, razor nicks, a picked-at blemish, this quietly speeds all of it along. Started as post-procedure care after microneedling and became the household first response spray. The faint chlorine note vanishes in seconds. Genuinely useful thing to own.

After my laser appointment the nurse misted this on and the cooling relief was instant, so I bought a bottle at the front desk. Been using it post-treatment and honestly just on hot days. The spray pattern is even and never spits.

Finished my first bottle, saw enough change in my forehead to stock up. It sinks in fast enough for my morning rush and never makes my oily skin shine worse. If you're on the fence, take weekly selfies, that's what convinced me.

Foundation glides over it and stops creasing into my laugh lines by afternoon, which was happening daily before. That was worth it alone, and then around week seven the lines themselves started looking softer bare-faced. Genuinely impressive double duty.

Read up on the peptide studies before buying, went in with modest expectations, and still got more than I hoped. My forehead moves fine but rests smoother, if that makes sense. Half a dropper covers the whole upper face. No fragrance issues, no purging.

Not saying it replaces injections for everyone, but my lines are early enough that this held them over. My forehead moves normally and still looks smoother than it did in January. The 5% niacinamide keeps my tone even as a bonus.

Skeptical by default, I read up on hexapeptide-8 and SYN-AKE before buying because I don't trust marketing. Real ingredients, sensible concentrations, and after ten weeks my forehead looks smoother in my clinic's before and after photos. My aesthetician takes them quarterly, so this isn't wishful thinking.

Within two weeks the 5% niacinamide had my skin looking brighter and more even. The expression line payoff came slower, around week eight for me, mostly on the forehead. It layers cleanly under sunscreen with zero pilling, which vitamin serums don't always get right.

The vertical lines between my brows have been my obsession for years. Eight weeks of this every morning under sunscreen and they're softer in photos. Not gone, softer. The peptides need time so don't judge it at week two. Texture is silky and layers well.

r.t: Stretches my appointments to five months
r.b: Confession: I used to book tox every three months. With this serum morning and night I comfortably go four to five now, and my injector confirmed I needed fewer units last visit. It has paid for itself twice over.

Recommended by my injector to maintain results, and I can actually tell when I skip a week because my elevens start creeping back. Light texture, sinks in fast, no sting despite the 5% PHA. Plays fine under retinol nights too.

r.t: The PHA does quiet extra work
r.b: Bought it for expression lines, stayed for the glow. The 5% PHA gives a mild resurfacing effect my oily skin loves, no irritation, just smoother texture. The lines themselves are moving more slowly, real change but subtle at month two, hence four stars.

Two months in, my deeper elevens are maybe ten percent softer while the fine lines around my eyes improved more. If you expect frozen-face results you will be disappointed. As a supporting act between tox visits it earns its keep, barely, at this price.

Everyone says forehead but for me the line between my brows responded fastest, about five weeks. It layers under moisturizer without pilling and doesn't sting even after retinol nights. My only note is the dropper glugs if you tip it too fast.

My goal isn't erasing anything, it's slowing the slide, and this does that visibly. Expression lines look softened rather than gone and my skin texture is more refined from the PHA. One bottle lasts me about eleven weeks using it twice a day.

I stare at my own face on calls all day and the horizontal forehead lines were bugging me. Two months of this and the difference on camera is real. Nobody's asked if I got work done, they just say I look less tired. I'll take it.

Went in for my regular appointment and she said my lines had held better than usual. Only new thing in my routine was this serum. Texture is like a light lotion, dries down satiny, faint clean scent. A bottle lasts me about ten weeks using it once a day.

Sixty-one year old guy, deep forehead grooves from decades outdoors. This softened the shallower lines around my eyes nicely but barely dented the big ones. Still, it's the first serum my wife bought me that I finished and reordered.

Product itself is quietly effective, my forehead texture is smoother and lines less etched after two months. The glass dropper though pulls up more than you need and it runs down the neck of the bottle. A pump would suit this texture far better.

Prairie sun means I've squinted my whole life. Three months in, the fan of lines at my eye corners is finer and my makeup doesn't settle into them by noon. I use two drops morning and night. It has a slight slip that makes it easy to spread.

Six weeks of nightly use and the horizontal lines on my forehead catch less light. I get tox twice a year and this stretches the smooth window between appointments. The milky serum spreads easily from the dropper and the niacinamide gives a nice glow on top.

On a whim I started dragging the leftover drops down my neck, and the horizontal creases there look better than they have in years. On the face it's doing steady work on my smile lines. Absorbs in under a minute, no tackiness on my skin despite what others report.

Results showed up around week six for me, mostly around my crow's feet. It's real but it's a subscription, because the day you stop, the lines drift back. Factor that into the price math before you commit.

Retinol wrecks me, so a peptide route was my only option for the lines around my mouth. Three months in they look softened, not erased, and my redness never flared once. The PHA exfoliates so gently I forgot it was in there.

r.t: Patience ran out at month three
r.b: Used it faithfully twice a day, finished the whole bottle, and I'd call the change marginal. My skin felt nice and looked hydrated but the frown lines look the same to me. Maybe my lines are too set. Younger users may fare better.

r.t: Broke me out along my hairline
r.b: Gave it six weeks and kept getting small clogged bumps along my forehead where I applied it. Once I stopped, they cleared. Frustrating because I could see the start of line softening. My acne-prone skin just wouldn't cooperate with something in the formula.

Not ready for injections, so I gave this three months. The frown line between my brows is shallower in photos and my makeup no longer creases into it by noon. The peptides plus PHA combo also smoothed the texture across my forehead. Worth every penny for a needle skeptic.

What it does is blur and relax the look of my expression lines, but if you're expecting a filler effect, temper that. At sixty-three I see maybe thirty percent improvement, which honestly is more than any cream before it. Elegant texture, no scent I can detect.

The serum stays slightly tacky for about five minutes, which drives me crazy when I am rushing in the morning. Results are legit though, my bunny lines and forehead look smoother after seven weeks. Moved it to evenings and we get along fine now.

Faithfully applied it every single morning for three months and photographed my crow's feet at the start and end. I genuinely cannot see a difference. Skin felt nice and hydrated, tone slightly brighter, but for this money I needed the lines to budge. Returned my second bottle.

Peptides plus PHA sounded risky for my reactive skin but there's been no sting, no redness, nothing. It's the first anti-aging serum I've tolerated at full twice-daily use. Lines at my brow are subtly relaxed after two months and my skin feels bouncier.

r.t: Smile lines softened by month two
r.b: One dropper every morning before moisturizer was my whole protocol. First month, nothing but nice hydration. Somewhere in month two the crow's feet at the corners of my eyes stopped being the first thing I saw in mirrors. Patience required, results delivered.

For six weeks nothing happened and I nearly quit. Somewhere in month two my eleven lines stopped looking angry. It's now month four and the improvement is steady but gradual. Four stars for the timeline, not the result.

r.t: Too much for my sensitive skin
r.b: Between the acid pads and the scrub my barrier waved a white flag around week three, red and tight along my cheeks. Dropped the pads to twice weekly and things settled, but at that pace the kit isn't doing what it promises. Better suited to resilient, oilier skin than mine.

r.t: Worth it for the pads alone
r.b: Those complexion renewal pads are the best chemical exfoliant I've used, and I have used many. The whole kit lasted me almost four months, which softens the sticker shock. Skin is clearer, smoother, and my ingrowns after shaving are way down.

My derm called this the prep work and she wasn't kidding. Two months in, my skin took to tretinoin with barely any flaking because the texture groundwork was already done. Even on its own it gave me smoother, brighter skin. Great value next to buying the three pieces separately.

Fair warning, the pads sting for real at first. I had to start every other night for two weeks before my skin adjusted. Once it did, clearer and brighter skin, no argument. The polish is great but do not press hard, let the crystals do the work.

First two weeks my cheeks felt tender if I did pads and polish on the same day, so now I alternate and it's been smooth since. Skin is brighter and my makeup applies evenly. Four stars because the instructions could flag the adjustment period better.

My skin coach insisted on getting skin ready before starting Wrinkle and Texture Repair, and she was right. Six weeks of the kit and my skin handled the retinol with barely a flake. The pads tingle for a few seconds, that is it.

Bought this before committing to the pricier serums and it earned my trust in about a month. Cleanser is mild, the polish leaves my skin insanely smooth, and the pads keep my oily zones clear. My esthetician noticed the difference before I told her anything.

Nurse here, still masked all shift. The pads at night keep my chin and jaw clear for the first time in years, and the cleanser gets the day off without stripping. Polish stays at twice a week or my sensitive spots complain. Kit number two already ordered.

Got this for my sister's birthday, borrowed her pads for a weekend, and ordered my own kit that Monday. The glycolic pads are the star but the magnesium polish is a close second. Skin looks polished, not scrubbed raw. Six months later we're both on our second box.

Wash, polish on weekends, wipe with a pad at night. Even I can follow that. Two months later my girlfriend asked if I got a facial. Oil control through the workday is the biggest win, my forehead used to be a mirror by 2 pm.

Pads and cleanser earn five stars from me. The polish felt too aggressive for anything more than once a week on my skin, even with a light hand. If your skin runs thick and oily you will probably tolerate it more often. Solid starting point overall.

The cleanser was lovely but the pads plus polish combo left my dry skin feeling stripped no matter how I spaced them out. My oily teenager took over the kit and his skin looks great, so it's not bad, just badly matched to dry types like me.

r.t: Skeptic to subscriber in six weeks
r.b: Figured a kit this simple couldn't move the needle. Six weeks later my texture is smoother, the bumps along my hairline are gone, and my skin tolerates the pads nightly now. Buying the components separately when these run out.

Honestly the exfoliating polish is the star for me, those magnesium crystals scrub without shredding, and the glycolic pads keep things clear in between. Blackheads on my nose that survived a decade of pore strips are visibly reduced at week five.

Three products, zero confusion, and by week five the congestion on my nose and chin had mostly cleared, I use the polish twice a week and the pads nightly and honestly it's the first routine I've finished instead of abandoning in a drawer.

Dull, rough, thirty-something skin going in. By the third week the pads had smoothed the little bumps on my chin, and the polish leaves that fresh, slightly pink glow every Sunday. The gentle cleanser is unremarkable in the best way, no tightness after.

Love the system, hate the math. Using the cleanser twice daily means it empties weeks before the polish and pads. ZO should size these to finish together. Results wise, smoother texture and fewer clogged pores by week four, no complaints there.

Started ZO with this three months ago. Cleanser morning and night, polish twice a week, pads every evening. My texture changed noticeably inside a month, pores around my nose look tighter and the afternoon shine is gone. Simple enough that I actually kept the routine.

Adding this to an existing retinoid routine proved too much, my cheeks got flaky and irritated by week two even alternating nights. On its own it is a fine, gentle exfoliating serum. If you already use a strong retinol, think hard about whether you need both.

Picked it up for the acids, then read about the 1% taurine and phytic acid combo. Whatever the mechanism, my skin recovers overnight in a way it hasn't since my twenties. Makeup-free days went from rare to routine in about two months.

r.t: Pores read smaller by month one
r.b: Nobody promised me pores and yet here we are, the ones on my nose look tighter and my whole face reflects light better. Seven drops at night, no sting past the first week. It's become the serum I'd rescue in a fire.

r.t: Event skin on a random Tuesday
r.b: You know that lit-from-within thing you only get before special occasions when you've prepped for weeks? This delivers it constantly. Five to seven drops nightly, moisturizer on top, and by morning my skin looks freshly exfoliated without a single flake. Two months in and strangers ask about my routine.

Apply at night, wake up smoother. It sounds like ad copy and I am as surprised as anyone. Six weeks in, the rough patch on my chin from years of surfing sun is nearly gone. Tingles the first few nights, then your skin stops noticing.

For the first two weeks this stung more than I expected around my nostrils, enough that I nearly quit. Glad I pushed through because the glow at week four is real. Start slow if you are sensitive. Also the dropper drips if you move too fast.

r.t: Good results, dropper drives me nuts
r.b: The serum itself is doing everything right, smoother texture by week four and a brightness people comment on. But the dropper is stiff and either gives you nothing or floods your palm. Minor problem, real annoyance at this price.

I used to do an at-home glycolic peel every Sunday. This nightly serum gives the same smoothness with none of the downtime or flaking. The 7.7% acid blend sounds intense but it is remarkably civilized. Makeup sits better, pores look cleaner.

At fifty-eight my cell turnover clearly needed the nudge. Within a month the dull grey cast lifted and rough patches on my cheekbones smoothed out. I alternate it with a retinol night and the two together have my skin the best it's been this decade.

Little bumps across my forehead that no cleanser ever touched are basically gone after two months of nightly use. It plays fine with my retinol on alternate nights. Slight tingle on nights after shaving, otherwise drama free.

r.t: Plays nice with my rosacea meds
r.b: Cleared it with my derm first since I'm on azelaic acid. No conflict, no flare, and the multi-acid blend at 7.7% is somehow gentler than the 5% glycolic toner I used to fear. Skin looks polished and the dry patches at my temples are gone.

Acids usually leave my face hot and angry. This one goes on like water from the dropper, tingles faintly for a minute, and that is the whole event. Three weeks in my skin looks polished, like I exfoliated without the aftermath. The taurine buffering seems to be more than marketing.

August left me blotchy and rough. Six weeks of this at night and the mottled look has faded into something even and glowy. I was considering microdermabrasion and no longer feel the need. Layered under moisturizer it never once burned.

Melasma-adjacent dullness had me looking tired constantly. Within three weeks on this my overall tone looked lit from within, and by week six two small dark patches near my temple had faded noticeably. It layers beautifully, thin and watery, then gone.

Results are genuinely good, smoother texture and a brighter look within a month. But a bottle at nightly use goes fast, and at this price that stings more than the acids do. Waiting for sales to repurchase, which tells you my exact level of devotion.

Three months in and the changes are subtle enough that I question them. My texture might be a touch smoother. For a resurfacing serum I expected my oily, thick skin to respond more. People with delicate skin probably see the value faster than I did.

At 54 my cheeks had that crosshatched dry texture. A month of this every evening under moisturizer and it has visibly softened. No flaking, no purge, just steady renewal. The dropper bottle looks small yet three months later I still have product left.

Straight glycolic serums made me flake at the corners of my nose. This multi-acid blend with phytic acid gives the same Saturday-morning glow without a single flake. I even use it the night before events now. Nearly weightless texture, absorbs before I count to ten.

The renewal part works, my skin tone is fresher and more uniform after six weeks. But it leans drying on my skin despite the gentle marketing, and I had to add a richer night cream to stay comfortable. Worth it with that adjustment.

All the reviews had me expecting a resurfacing miracle. What I got after eight weeks was a mild, pleasant glow I could probably get from a good lactic acid at a third of the price. Zero irritation to its credit. Just underwhelmed relative to the cost.

r.t: My C E Ferulic works harder now
r.b: Using this at night and my vitamin C in the morning turned my dull winter skin around in under a month. Texture on my forehead is smoother and the serum itself vanishes in seconds, no residue, no smell to speak of.

r.t: The last step my barrier needed
r.b: Overdid the acids last spring and my barrier was a mess, tight, shiny, stinging at everything. Two weeks of a gentle cleanser plus this cream and I was back. It feels rich going on and then just becomes comfortable skin. Keeping it in the rotation permanently.

r.t: Takes a minute to sink in
r.b: Be prepared to stand there patting for a good minute or two, it's a dense cream that doesn't rush. Once absorbed it's excellent, my dry patches surrendered within a week. Just not a product for people who sprint through their routine.

Prone to eczema flares on my cheekbones every spring. This is the first moisturizer rich enough to prevent them without triggering the little bumps I get from heavy occlusives. I wake up plump and calm. My derm approved it without hesitation when I showed her.

I was slugging with petroleum jelly every night just to survive Minneapolis winters. This replaced that entire ritual, no more greasy pillowcases. Squalane and cholesterol apparently beat vaseline, who knew. One airless pump lasts surprisingly long too.

Beautiful cream on bare skin at night, but it pilled over my vitamin C serum and under sunscreen no matter how long I waited. My combination skin also felt smothered by day three of daily use. One for truly dry faces, not mine.

Sixty-one year old skin is thin, dry, and picky. This cream leaves it comfortable for a full day and my foundation stopped catching in the dry creases beside my mouth. The airless pump delivers the same dose every time, no digging in a jar.

Chinook winds leave my cheeks shredded every February. Started this on a Monday and by Friday the flaky patches around my mouth were simply gone. It's thick and takes some warming between the fingers, but nothing else has worked this fast.

Great everywhere except the crease of my nose, where I got small clogged pores after about three weeks of nightly use. Now I avoid that zone and it's fine, but a moisturizer this expensive shouldn't need a map.

Sandwiching my prescription tretinoin between layers of this saved my winter routine. Zero flaking since November. It is unscented, dense, and one pump genuinely covers my whole face. A jar would tempt me to overuse it, so the airless packaging is probably saving me money.

Hypothyroidism makes my skin desert dry no matter what I do. The urea plus ceramide combination in this actually keeps moisture in overnight instead of evaporating by 2am. I wake up with comfortable skin for the first time in a decade.

Takes a solid few minutes to fully sink in, and if I apply anything on top too soon it balls up. Learned to make it my true last step at night and now we get along. Deeply moisturizing, my flaky chin surrendered within a week.

Ingredient nerds, this is the one. Urea and sodium PCA pull water in, ceramides and cholesterol seal it, squalane keeps it comfortable. My heels know urea well but my face had never met it. Dry patches along my jaw gone in ten days.

Evenings only for me. Under makeup it's too much and I look glazed by 11am. As a night treatment though it's terrific, I wake up genuinely soft. Normal skin types should probably reserve it for the cold months.

Yes it costs a lot. It also ended my flaky forehead within days, works over any serum without pilling, and one pump does face and neck. I bought it in August ahead of the cold and ended up using it year round at night.

Months after finishing accutane my face still felt like paper. Two pumps of this at night changed everything within a week, no sting on the raw corners of my mouth, no clogged pores despite the richness. It has that thick cream feel without any greasy shine.

October through April this cream is unbeatable on my dry skin. Come summer humidity it feels like too much, so into the drawer it goes. Four stars because the price hurts when it only earns its keep seven months a year.
Evenings after hockey the rink air leaves my face raw, and one pump of this dense, fragrance free cream has everything smooth and settled by morning.

Sixty-four years old, skin thinned by the years and a blood pressure medication. This cream gives it back some cushion. I apply it at night after a hyaluronic serum and by morning my face feels padded again, not papery.

Winnipeg in February is a skin destroyer and this cream held my face together all season. Rich, almost buttery, but it absorbs by the time I finish brushing my teeth. Not a single flake this winter, first time in years I can say that.

Wanted this to work so badly. The brightening was starting to show around week three, but so were small closed comedones along my jaw and hairline, and by week five I had to stop. My oily skin apparently reads this as too rich. Fine texture, wrong face.

No matter how long I waited, this balled up the second I applied my mineral sunscreen over it. Tried five different SPFs from my drawer, same story with four of them. Brightening seemed promising in week one but I can't build a morning routine around a product this fussy.

Fragrance-free is non-negotiable for me and this delivers there. Skin is brighter, softer, and my age spots have faded a shade over three months. I keep a stronger serum for nighttime because at 66 my skin wants more, but as a daytime C step this is lovely.

Packing one pump bottle instead of a serum, a moisturizer, and prayers that my dropper does not leak in the suitcase. Skin stayed bright and hydrated through two weeks in dry mountain air. It has quietly become the anchor of my morning routine at home too.

Vitamin C always meant tingling and eventual flaky patches for me. This behaves like a comfortable moisturizer that happens to brighten. My dark spots from last summer are visibly lighter and my dry cheeks stopped drinking foundation. Very easy product to love.

Airless pump means the vitamin C actually stays potent, no browning, no waste, and it dispenses to the end. Results are solid, brighter overall tone within a month or so. Just not seeing much movement on my two darker sun spots yet, hence four stars.

Grey winter face is my usual baseline by February. About four weeks into this and coworkers started asking if I'd been somewhere sunny. It's a medium-weight cream, absorbs in a minute or so, and the pump gives the same dose every time.

From May to October this is all my skin wants in the morning. Once furnace season hit I had to layer a heavier cream over it, which defeats some of the one-step appeal. Brightening is gradual and real. Just know its hydration ceiling if you run dry.

Primer-level smoothness from a skincare step. Foundation glides over it and lasts longer through the day, which I didn't expect from a vitamin C product. Skin tone looks fresher after about six weeks too. The pump is sturdy and dispenses cleanly.
