Picked this up to deal with sun spots from a careless summer. Two months of morning use and the two on my cheekbone are noticeably lighter in photos. The kakadu plum and green tea give it a fresh feel and the hydration is enough that I skip serum entirely.

Swapped out a serum that cost nearly double and honestly see no downgrade. Brightness held, hydration improved, one less step. Altitude dryness usually forces me into heavier creams by December but this plus sunscreen has been enough.

r.t: Five star cream, one star cap
r.b: Five stars for the product, my dull skin looks alive again after six weeks of morning use. Zero for the packaging, the cap popped off twice in my bag and the pump dispensed all over everything. Decant carefully if you travel with it.
Coworkers keep asking if I changed my makeup, but it is just five weeks of this light, cushiony vitamin C cream every morning under sunscreen.

Light enough that my T-zone doesn't revolt, rich enough for my cheeks in fall. Tone has evened out nicely since September. Four stars because in humid summer weather it was borderline too much for me, I'll switch to something lighter come July.

Regular vitamin C serums light my face on fire. This one, nothing, not even warmth. Three months in and the blotchiness across my cheeks has faded noticeably while my moisture barrier stayed happy. Finally get to have the brightening everyone else talks about.

L-ascorbic serums always burned my face. This cream version with THD ascorbate gives me the brightening without any of the drama. Light lotion texture from the pump, absorbs quickly, sits perfectly under mineral SPF. My post-blemish marks faded faster over six weeks.

Chemistry matters, apparently. Every ascorbic acid product I owned stung and quit working within weeks as it browned in the bottle. This stable form stays cream-colored to the last pump and my skin has steadily brightened over the summer. Convinced convert here.

Surprised how calming this is for a vitamin C product. My usual pink cheeks look settled and my skin has that healthy, rested look by week three. A single pump covers everything. My teenage daughter keeps borrowing it, which is its own five star review.

r.t: Wanted more oomph for the price
r.b: Nice moisturizer, mild brightening, and that's about the whole story after two months of daily use. My old serum plus a cheap moisturizer did more for less money. If your skin hates strong actives this makes sense. Mine doesn't, so I'm moving on.

r.t: Brightening that shows on deeper skin
r.b: Plenty of vitamin C products claim brightening and deliver ash. This one evened out the hyperpigmentation around my beard line within about seven weeks with no grey cast and no clogging. Pump bottle keeps the C stable too, my last dropper serum went orange in a month.

Stopped editing the redness out of my selfies around month two. Tone looks more uniform, especially the old acne marks along my chin. Sits well under makeup with no pilling for me. The green tea and kakadu plum give it a faint natural scent that disappears fast.

Tried a dozen morning moisturizers that balled up under my zinc SPF. This one dries down clean in under a minute and the sunscreen glides over it. Bonus that my skin tone looks fresher, and the sodium hyaluronate keeps things plump through office air conditioning.

Give it eight weeks, not two. I almost gave up at the one month mark, then my post-shave dark marks started fading and the overall tone caught up. Nice light cream, no scent worth mentioning. Four stars for the patience required at this price point.

r.t: Vitamin C and moisturizer in one go
r.b: Ditched my separate vitamin C serum and moisturizer for this and my mornings got five minutes shorter. THD ascorbate is the gentle kind, no sting, none of that hot dog water smell some C serums have. Tone looks brighter and more even after about a month.

Cut my five-step morning down to cleanse, this, sunscreen. Done in three minutes and my skin looks better than when I was layering a separate vitamin C serum. The THD ascorbate doesn't sting or oxidize orange like my old ascorbic acid bottles did.

r.t: One pump, no fuss, clear skin
r.b: Simple routine guy here. Cleanser, this, moisturizer, sleep. Clear skin in about eight weeks with zero flaking, unlike the adapalene I tried before. Bottle lasted eleven weeks. Wish everything in life worked this well.

Foundation used to cling to the rough patches on my cheeks and now it just glides. Pores around my nose look tighter too. My single complaint is the opaque airless pump, since I never know how much is left until it sputters. Otherwise a quiet workhorse I reorder without thinking.

Results didn't plateau, which was my fear. Half a year of nightly use, skin stays clear, texture keeps improving, and the redness from old breakouts is nearly gone. I've stopped wearing foundation to work. It travels well too since the pump can't leak or spill in a bag.

My dermatologist suggested this after tretinoin left me raw and peeling. The difference is night and day. Same smoothing effect over about ten weeks, none of the irritation, and the built-in salicylic keeps the small bumps on my chin from surfacing. Worth every penny for skin that hates harsh actives.

r.t: Hormonal spots and fine lines, handled
r.b: Forty two with teenage breakouts and forty two year old lines, which felt unfair. This covers both. Breakouts calmed within a month, the lines around my mouth softened by month three. It never left me red or peeling the way tret did. Genuinely worth the price for doing two jobs.

Thirty six years old and still breaking out until this serum. The retinoid plus salicylic combo cleared my chin in about seven weeks with only mild flaking at the start. A pump at night, moisturizer over top, done. My skin also looks smoother in a way spot treatments never managed.

Miss two nights and I can tell by the weekend. When I'm consistent it's excellent, clear skin and smaller pores. When work travel throws me off, small breakouts creep back within days. That fragility keeps it at four stars. Also the pump occasionally spits a double dose.

Surface level congestion improved, I'll give it that. The deep painful ones along my chin still show up on schedule and this doesn't touch them. For the price I hoped for more than a decent exfoliating serum. My derm says cystic acne usually needs more than topicals, so partly on me.

Fair warning, I purged for about two weeks before things turned around. By month two my skin was smoother and clearer than baseline, so it earned its spot, but that early stretch was rough enough that I nearly quit. Start with two nights a week.

Skeptical of pore claims but here we are. Nose and cheek pores are visibly tighter after two months, and the blackheads that used to refill weekly just don't. Goes on smooth, dries down fast, never pilled under my night moisturizer.

r.t: Week three was rough, worth it
r.b: Fair warning, my skin got worse before better. Week three brought a cluster of small whiteheads that took ten days to clear. After that, smooth sailing and genuinely clearer skin than I've had since college. Knock a star off for the scare, the end result earns the rest.

Like clockwork I'd get three deep spots every month. Since November I've had one, singular. I use it two nights on, one night off, and buffer with a ceramide cream. There was a mild purge around week two, nothing scary. The airless pump keeps it from degrading, smart packaging.

r.t: Perfect bridge between acne and aging
r.b: Products for breakouts always ignored my crow's feet and vice versa. This is the first thing that respects that I'm 47 with occasional spots. Clear and smoother in the same bottle. It does make my skin a touch dry in winter so I've added a richer night cream on top.
One pump, once a night, and my skin looks better at 41 than it did at 35. That is the whole review.

Normally I'd be back at the derm every winter for my usual flare. This year it never came. I credit nightly AlphaRet Clearing plus better sleep. The retinoid is gentle enough that I never had the ugly adjustment phase, and my post spot marks faded quicker than they ever have.

r.t: Does what it claims, costs plenty
r.b: Texture is noticeably smoother after two months and breakouts are down maybe seventy percent. My only gripe is sticker shock at repurchase time. I'll buy it again, but only when it goes on sale.

r.t: Zinc PCA keeps the shine down
r.b: Midday oil slick used to be my signature. Three months of this at night and my forehead stays matte until late afternoon. Clearer too, only the odd small spot around my period. It stings for a second on freshly exfoliated skin so I space it away from acid nights.

Six weeks in and the dark marks from old breakouts are fading faster than with anything else I have tried. I apply it every other night under a plain moisturizer, no sting, no dryness. The zinc PCA seems to keep my midday shine in check too.

Great on my oily zones, harsh on the dry parts. My cheeks flake if I use it more than every other night, even sandwiched between moisturizer layers. Breakouts are way down though, and the texture change on my forehead is real. Combination skin folks, start slow and buffer.

Bumpy forehead texture I'd had for years is basically gone. Took about six weeks of nightly use. It's a silky lotion serum, absorbs quick, no smell I can detect. Zinc PCA seems to keep my oil in check too because I'm blotting way less by lunch.

Breakouts are smaller and heal faster now that the salicylic acid rides along with the retinoid. Docking a star because the bottle emptied in about seven weeks at one pump a night, and at this price that hurts.

Hormonal breakouts along my jaw have calmed way down since I started this in June. It goes on like a thin lotion, absorbs in under a minute, and I wake up without that greasy film other night serums leave. Around week five the texture on my forehead smoothed out as a bonus.

When my face cleared around month two I started using the last bit of each pump on my shoulders. Bacne improved noticeably within a few weeks. It's expensive real estate to use on a back, but hey, it works. Face is clear, marks fading, no complaints on the formula.

Powerful stuff for something marketed as gentle. My sensitive skin tolerated it only once I committed to a thick ceramide cream on top every night. With that system it's been great, clearer and brighter by week nine. Without it, tight and pink by morning. Plan accordingly.

Fine on plain skin but burns if I've used my glycolic toner within a day or two. Took me a month to figure out the pattern. Now that they're separated it's okay, mild improvement in texture, small drop in breakouts. Just wish the guidance on mixing actives was clearer on the box.

Flaking has ruined every retinol I tried before this one. Three months in and nothing, no peeling, but the change is real. My cheeks are smoother and the clogged pores along my jaw are mostly gone. The airless pump doles out the same amount every night, which I appreciate.

r.t: More than my skin can handle
r.b: I wanted to love this but even twice a week it left my cheeks tight and pink by morning. The pump is nice and it never pilled, it is simply too strong for my reactive skin. It now handles the breakouts on my back instead, so not a total loss.

r.t: Replaced two products in my routine
r.b: This took over my alternating retinol and BHA nights and does the job of both in one pump. Fewer steps, fewer clogged pores, and my skin stopped getting confused by the back and forth. No scent to speak of, and it layers cleanly under a ceramide cream.

r.t: Handles breakouts and lines at once
r.b: Adult acne plus early fine lines is an annoying combination and this actually addresses both. One pump at night after cleansing, no purge, and by week four my chin was noticeably clearer. The light lotion texture sinks in fast and has never pilled under my moisturizer.

Really nice mild gel that melts off makeup residue without stripping. My only annoyance is that the pump dispenses more than I need, so I share the extra with my neck. Skin has looked a little brighter since week three, which I credit to the gentle botanical acids.

Recommended by my clinic for the flaky week after chemical peels, and it was gentle enough for even day two skin. Now it's my everyday cleanser because at 57 anything harsher leaves me tight. A bottle lasts about three months with nightly use.

Even mid-flare, when almost everything burns, this doesn't. The panthenol seems to take the edge off the redness, and there is no perfumey scent to aggravate things. Been through two bottles and my cheeks stay calm through cleansing now.

Deep-clean feeling with none of the tightness, which I didn't think was possible for my combination skin. Breakouts along my hairline quieted down within a month, probably because I stopped over-cleansing to compensate. The amber tint is just the fulvic acid, don't let it scare you.

r.t: Second cleanse hero in dry climate
r.b: Living at altitude, most cleansers leave me tight within minutes. This one takes off the last traces of mineral sunscreen as my second cleanse and my face stays comfortable while I wait to apply toner. The pump gives exactly the right amount in one press.

Between the mild fulvic acid and the gentle exfoliating complex, my retinol and vitamin C both seem to penetrate better since I switched. Skin stays comfortable through winter. Four stars because it struggles with waterproof mascara, I still need a separate remover for eyes.

r.t: The prep step I was missing
r.b: Started this when I began a stronger vitamin C and the difference in how it applies is obvious, way less tingle and no blotchiness after. The gel is silky rather than foamy, and one pump covers my whole face. Two months in, my skin tone looks more even overall.

r.t: Fancy cleanser that backs it up
r.b: Skeptical of any cleanser over twenty bucks, but this one changed my mind mostly. Skin feels prepped and smooth, no dryness even in radiator season. Still not fully convinced a rinse-off product justifies this price, hence the missing star, but I've repurchased once already.
Zero residue after rinsing, and my retinol stopped stinging on application within the first week of using this. Didn't expect the cleanser to be the fix.
After about six weeks there is a mild glow I attribute to the botanical AHA blend, nothing dramatic but real. Wish the bottle were bigger, because two pumps per wash empties it in under two months.

Noticed within the first week that everything I apply after cleansing absorbs quicker and works better. The gentle botanical AHA complex preps without any scrubby nonsense. It lathers lightly, rinses completely, and one pump covers my whole face and neck.

Honestly hard to rave about a cleanser, but my serums do seem to absorb quicker since switching, which I assume is the whole prep-the-skin point. Rinses completely clean. Four stars because I'm not fully convinced a cheaper gentle cleanser couldn't do most of this.

Lovely texture, but by evening my T-zone needs more degreasing than this can offer on its own. I ended up double cleansing anyway, which defeats the purpose at this price. Now it is my morning cleanser only, where it is fine.

An aesthetician sent me home with this after microneedling and it did not sting even on freshly treated skin. It is a low-lather gel with a faint earthy smell from the fulvic acid, and my face felt clean but cushioned afterward. Still using it months later.

Pleasant to use, rinses clean, smells like almost nothing. But my oily skin needs more grunt and by afternoon I'm shiny like always. My dry-skinned mom loves the bottle I passed her, so it's clearly a skin type match issue. Just not mine.

Skin feels soft and prepped, my retinol no longer tingles going on, and the light botanical scent disappears on rinsing. But fifty-plus dollars for a cleanser is a stretch, so it loses a star on value alone.

Double cleansing always left my face stripped until this. It removes sunscreen and light makeup in one go and my skin feels cushioned after, not squeaky. The panthenol must be doing the heavy lifting. Four months in and my barrier has never been calmer.

r.t: Held up through a Winnipeg February
r.b: Calgary winters usually leave my face flaky no matter how gentle the cleanser. Not this year. Between the panthenol and whatever else is in here, I got through February without a single dry patch, and my hyaluronic serum layers on smoother afterward.

Do not be alarmed by the tea-colored gel, that is apparently the fulvic acid. Barely any foam, yet it takes off everything, and my sixty-year-old skin never feels tight after. My vitamin C sinks in noticeably faster on skin washed with this.

r.t: Wish it came in a twin pack
r.b: Handy little cleanser that lasted me about three weeks of nightly use. Does what the big one does. Selling these in pairs would make more sense for anyone who travels monthly.

Nice gentle gel, cleans well without drying my oily skin, and the green tea formula leaves no residue. My only gripe is the cap, it's small and fiddly to flip open with wet hands, I fumbled it into the sink more than once. Contents get five stars, packaging loses one.
Fourteen days through Portugal and my face never once freaked out. That is all I ask of a travel cleanser.

Went through security at Trudeau without a second look and lasted my entire twelve-day trip to France with washes morning and night. No fragrance sting, no tightness, even with hard hotel water. My combination skin stayed completely predictable the whole trip.

Lives in my equipment bag now. Post-game face wash in an arena bathroom isn't glamorous but this cuts through sweat and doesn't leave my skin tight for the drive home. Small enough that I don't care if it rattles around with my gear.

Most gel cleansers leave my forehead squeaky and then twice as greasy by noon. This one cleans without triggering that rebound shine, which surprised me from such a gentle formula. The travel size convinced me, and the full pump bottle is on my counter now.

Packed one bottle for a ten day trip and my husband, a bar soap loyalist since forever, borrowed it once and never gave it back. It's mild, has basically no scent, and doesn't strip. We now buy two travel sizes for every trip plus the big one at home. That's the whole review, it won over a man who thought moisturizer was a scam.

Threw it in my bag for a ski weekend expecting the usual windburned tight face at night. Washed with this and my skin actually felt comfortable enough to skip my heavier night cream. It is now permanently packed.

The flip cap popped open somewhere over the Atlantic and half the tube ended up coating my dopp kit. What survived was a perfectly nice gentle cleanser, but between the leak and the price for such a small amount, I'll decant the full size into a proper travel bottle next time.

Same reliable cleanser as the full size, and it slid right into my carry-on liquids bag. Per millilitre though, you pay a real premium for the small format. Buy it to trial the formula, not to save money.

Nice and mild, but the light lather means I need a second pass to fully remove mineral sunscreen at night. For morning washes it is exactly right. Green tea in the ingredients, no scent that I can detect.

Smart way to trial the formula before dropping money on the big bottle. Two weeks of twice-daily use told me everything, gentle, rinses clean, no breakouts. Full size ordered before this one was even empty.

Hotel tap water usually wrecks my face by day three of any trip. Used this through a week in Vegas and my skin stayed calm and soft, no flaking around my nose at all. The glycerin must be doing overtime.

Most cleansers light my face up within days. This one, with the oat amino acids, has been calm sailing through two full trips including a week of skiing. No tightness, no red patches, rinses clean without squeaking. Bought the full size the day I got home.

Perfect size for post-spin face washes. The gel lathers just enough, rinses fast in a busy locker room, and the oat amino acids keep my face from feeling stripped before I head back to the office. This little tube earns its keep.

Traveling usually means my skin rebels. This small tube kept things boring, in the best way, across four hotels in one week. No perfume, a soft gel texture, and my cheeks never got that hot tight feeling after washing.

My forehead used to be a mirror by noon. A month and a half of using this at night and I'm blotting maybe once a day instead of four times. Texture on my nose is smoother too. Smells faintly acidic, nothing offensive. Just don't get greedy with the drops, I learned that the hard way with a red flaky week.

Alternating this with my retinol turned out to be the combination my skin was waiting for. Texture on my cheeks smoothed out within the first month and I get fewer of those deep, slow-healing spots. No pilling, no residue, just a barely-there liquid with a slight tingle.
Cheek pores I have stared at in the mirror for a decade are visibly tighter after eight weeks. Enough said, reordering.

Effective serum that demands respect. I jumped in nightly and got a stinging red mess by day four. Backed off to twice a week, built up over a month, and now my skin's clearer and smoother than it's been in years. Four stars because the learning curve is real and the label undersells it.

At my age the breakouts were supposed to stop, and they never did. This is the first serum that respects that I also have wrinkles to think about. Breakouts down to almost nothing since January, and the glycolic keeps my skin tone bright. It stings a touch on application, worth it.

Such a thin fluid that a little covers everything. I'm 47 with oily skin that still breaks out and this hits both problems, the glycolic smooths my texture while the salicylic and LHA keep pores clear. Empty bottle number two just went in the recycling.

r.t: Plays nice with my retinol nights
r.b: So thin and watery that it disappears into skin instantly, which makes layering effortless. I follow with a peptide serum and cream and nothing pills. Two months in, my skin looks polished, pores smaller, the odd hormonal spot gone within days instead of a week.

Everyone's skin is different so take this as one data point. Weeks one through three were rough, more breakouts than I started with. It did eventually calm down and my texture now is better than baseline, but I'm not sure the trade was worth it. Three stars, cautiously.

Started on my face, then began sweeping a few drops across my shoulders after workouts. Cleared both zones within six weeks. It's oil free so it never feels like another layer sitting on me. Bottle goes fast when you use it on body too, that's my only note.
Resurfaces without wrecking my barrier, twice a week alongside my retinol nights, and my texture hasn't looked this polished in a decade.

Word of warning, the liquid is thin as water and races down your fingers if you hesitate. Dispense onto your palm quickly. Results are legit, clearer skin by week five and a smoother jawline, but the price and the messy dropper keep it at four stars.

Blackheads on and around my nose have thinned out dramatically since mid-September. I use three or four drops at night, moisturizer on top, done. It is basically water in texture so it spreads everywhere fast. Glad I ignored the price and bought it.

Full marks for the serum itself, my blackheads have thinned out noticeably since September. The dropper earns none. It dispenses unevenly, sometimes a flood, sometimes nothing, and with a liquid this thin I've dribbled plenty onto the counter. Great skin, messy vanity.

Only every third night works for my skin, so progress has been gradual, noticeable smoothing around week six rather than week three. It does sting for thirty seconds going on. If your skin is tougher than mine you will probably get there faster.

Miami humidity turns my face into an oil slick by mid-morning most of the year. A month of this every night and the shine is legitimately reduced through the afternoon, plus the rough patches on my forehead are gone. Dioic acid is apparently the unsung hero. The dropper makes dosing simple.

Leftover marks from my mask wearing years were just sitting there refusing to fade. Eight weeks of this every other night and they're visibly lighter, plus no new breakouts on my chin. The 2% dioic acid was the ingredient my derm specifically pointed at. It stings a little on freshly cleansed skin, so I wait ten minutes after washing.

Expect a minute of tingling when it goes on and a slightly medicinal, alcohol-ish scent. Push through, because by week four my texture was visibly smoother and the little clogged pores on my chin had mostly cleared. Not one for the scent-sensitive.

r.t: Way too strong for my skin
r.b: Even once a week over moisturizer this left my cheeks flaking and hot. I'm in my fifties with dry skin and the occasional breakout, and I thought the aging plus blemish angle made it perfect for me. It wasn't. My daughter with oily skin took it off my hands and she loves it, so there's that.

Used nightly, this flaked me out around the mouth and nose within two weeks, and my skin is only moderately dry to begin with. Scaling back to twice a week fixed the flaking, but at that frequency results crawl. Probably brilliant for oily skin, just not mine.

r.t: Jaw bumps gone by week five
r.b: Those stubborn under the skin bumps along my jaw are gone. Took about five weeks of nightly use, three drops over my whole face. It's watery and absorbs in seconds. Mild prickle at first that faded after week one. My skin hasn't been this clear since college.

Nose and inner cheek pores were the first thing I saw in every mirror. Two months of nightly drops and they've visibly tightened up. No purge for me, just steadily smoother skin. I follow with a plain moisturizer and that's the whole evening routine now.

Every month like clockwork my chin would erupt, and since starting this in February those flare-ups have shrunk to maybe one small spot. Skin looks glowier too, which I didn't expect from an acid serum. I apply it after cleansing at night, wait a few minutes, then moisturize.

Nothing else in my routine treats both problems at once. The watery serum takes seconds to absorb, and within three weeks the bumps along my chin flattened while the fine lines near my mouth looked softer. Four drops does my whole face. There is a faint clinical smell that vanishes quickly.

r.t: Six weeks, modest change so far
r.b: Early days I know, but six weeks felt like enough time to report something. Slight brightening, maybe. The crinkles are unchanged. No irritation at least, which is why I'm continuing. Will update if the second half of the tube performs better than the first.

r.t: Slow and steady, emphasis on slow
r.b: Solid product, but temper expectations on speed. It took a full twelve weeks before I saw a convincing difference in my crow's feet, and at this price I wanted faster. No irritation at all in dry Colorado air, which counts for something.

r.t: My before and after shocked me
r.b: Took a photo in December on a whim and compared it last week. The difference in the crepe under my eyes is honestly startling. I'm 63 and assumed that texture was permanent. Nightly use, never skipped more than a night or two. My daughter just ordered her own tube.

Comfortable cream, nicely moisturizing, never irritated my dry skin. As for the actual retinoid results, I'm at month four and my lines look the same in every light I check. Maybe my expectations were inflated by the reviews. It's a pleasant eye moisturizer at a treatment price.

r.t: Astaxanthin sold me, results kept me
r.b: Bought it for the antioxidant angle after reading about astaxanthin. Stayed because my under eyes look smoother and less crepey than they have in five years. Nightly, tiny amount, tapped in with my ring finger. It layers fine under my morning eye SPF with no pilling. Zero irritation across eight months.

r.t: Better than my last three eye creams
r.b: Compared to the peptide and caffeine creams I've cycled through, this actually changed the skin instead of temporarily plumping it. Downside is cost per gram, this is jewelry pricing. But at 58 my under eyes look better in photos than they did at 55, so the math sort of works.

r.t: Under eye lines softened by spring
r.b: Started in January, rice sized amount patted under each eye at night. By April the fan of lines under my eyes had visibly relaxed. No sting, no redness, and it didn't migrate into my eyes even when I got sloppy. The tube is small but four months in it's still going.

Around week seven I noticed my concealer was sitting smoothly instead of collecting in the lines under my eyes. That was the moment I became a repeat customer. Small dab, once nightly, no irritation ever.

Measured expectations going in since eye creams have burned me before, financially speaking. This one delivered around the ten week mark. Crow's feet are softer, especially the deep one on my right side. A pea covers both eyes with some left for the brow bone. No stinging, no milia, no scent.

It works, my undereye texture is smoother and concealer no longer settles into every crease. The tube is tiny though, and the cost per gram is genuinely hard to justify. Four stars for the wallet, five for the skin.

r.t: Retinoid for eyes, minus the drama
r.b: Regular retinol near my eyes always ended in flaky red crescents. This AlphaRet version has been completely calm from night one. Three months in, the crinkling when I smile is finer and my concealer doesn't settle as much. It's pricey but a tube lasts ages if you use the right amount.

r.t: Gentle enough for nightly use eventually
r.b: Directions say build up slowly and they mean it. Twice a week for the first month, then alternating nights, now nightly with no issues. Rushing it early gave me one flaky patch that resolved fast. Results at four months are good, finer lines and brighter skin, just not dramatic yet.

Repurchased without hesitation. First tube took about five months using it five nights a week. Sensitive skin, contact lens wearer, not one day of stinging or watering. Lines at the outer corners are visibly finer and the skin doesn't look as thin. It earns the price tag slowly but surely.

r.t: A little goes a very long way
r.b: Half a rice grain per eye is truly enough, my first tube lasted four months. The cream has a soft peach tone that disappears on application and plays fine under my morning eye SPF. Lines from squinting at screens all day are fainter, and no dryness even in January.

r.t: Works where tret was too harsh
r.b: Prescription tretinoin wrecked my eye area twice before I gave up. This has the retinoid benefits at a pace my skin accepts. Six months in, the etched line under my left eye is shallower and the skin looks thicker somehow. Patience needed, but it's the tortoise that wins.

Texture and fine lines improved by month three, no question. My hereditary dark circles didn't budge, though to be fair nothing topical has ever touched them. If your issue is crepiness and crinkles, buy it. If it's shadows, manage expectations. Lovely rich cream either way, a little goes far.

Sensitive eyes here, the kind that water at strong creams. Not a single night of stinging in four months, and the crepiness under my eyes has plumped up noticeably. I keep it on my nightstand and apply it last, after my face retinol has dried down.

Patience required. Months one and two were just nice hydration, then somewhere in month three the lines at my eye corners started looking softer and shallower. The peptide and retinoid combination apparently needed time to compound. Now on tube number two.

Ten hours a day at a monitor gave me squint lines by 35. Four months of this every night and they've backed off noticeably. The cream is rich but never greasy, and the astaxanthin gives it a slight warm tint that disappears on skin. Genuinely impressed.
No fireworks, just steadily better skin around my eyes every week since late July. Sometimes that is exactly what you want.

r.t: Eye area finally matches my face
r.b: Years of retinol had my cheeks looking great while my eye area lagged behind, lined and thin. Eight months of EyeMax evened the score. The hexapeptide plus retinoid combo actually firmed the skin under my eyes, not just moisturized it. Wish I'd started sooner instead of hoarding my face products.

r.t: First eye retinoid I could tolerate
r.b: Regular retinol eye creams always left me red and crepey before they helped anything. This one never irritated once, even applied close to the lash line on the orbital bone, and after about two months the etched-in lines under my eyes are shallower. Genuinely impressed.

Three weeks in, tiny milia-like bumps appeared under both eyes and didn't clear until I stopped using it. Frustrating, because the texture is lovely and my lines were starting to look better. My esthetician thinks the formula is just too rich for my skin. Yours may fare better.

Under-eye crepiness had me avoiding close-up mirrors at 58. Five months of this every night and the skin looks thicker and smoother. I even pat a little on my upper lids without trouble. A tube lasts me about three months using a tiny amount.

Ten weeks of nightly use and the fan of lines at the corners of my eyes has genuinely softened. The cream is rich with a slight peachy tint from the astaxanthin, but it absorbs clear and never migrates into my eyes. A rice grain per side is plenty.

r.t: Started weekly, now every other night
r.b: Slow ramp worked perfectly for me. No purging, no bumps, just gradual smoothing. At the five month mark my wife asked if I'd been sleeping better. Only gripe is the tube dispenses more than needed if you squeeze carelessly, and at this price overdispensing hurts.

Thick enough to feel like it is doing something, yet it sinks in fully before I hit the pillow, no smeared residue on the pillowcase. Through an Edmonton winter my undereyes stayed hydrated and the fine dryness lines vanished within the first month.
Store it in the fridge, apply it cold, and thank me later. My dry skin loves the slight richness the vitamin E gives it, and the tightness I used to feel by noon has been gone since around week two.

Came out of ski season with a ridiculous goggle line. My girlfriend handed me her bottle and by mid May the demarcation had blended out. Now I've bought my own and use it daily under SPF. Altitude sun is brutal here and this is the first thing that keeps my skin looking even.

Bought this after my wife's dermatologist appointment turned into a household conversion. At 62 my skin was flat and sallow. Four months of daily use and there's actual radiance again, plus the deep crease in my forehead looks shallower in bright light. We now go through two bottles at a time.

First serious skincare purchase of my life and the learning curve was zero. Cleanse, four drops, moisturizer, sunscreen. By week three the dry dull patches on my cheeks looked alive again. I get why this has been around for two decades.

Living in Phoenix means UV is a daily battle. I layer this under SPF 50 every single morning and my skin has stopped looking leathery. The ferulic acid supposedly stabilizes the vitamin C and I believe it, my bottle stayed pale yellow to the end. Pricey, absolutely, but cheaper than laser.

Skipped highlighter entirely at my cousin's wedding because my actual skin was doing the work, two months in, applied to clean skin every morning, and honestly I keep catching my reflection. On my deeper skin tone some vitamin C serums leave a weird cast, this one disappears completely. The scent is odd for about ten seconds. Buying forever.

Let's be honest about what's happening here, I'm paying more per millilitre than I've paid for anything I put on my face, and it works well enough that I keep doing it. Brighter, smoother, spots fading slowly. Four stars because my wallet gets a vote and it votes no.

Bottle number two just arrived and I opened it the way other people open sneakers. The first one erased most of a stubborn patch of dullness on my forehead and made my pores look tighter, probably just from the evened-out tone.

Genuinely shocked. Fifteen percent vitamin C should have set my reactive cheeks on fire but the formula is gentler than the number suggests. Started twice a week, worked up to daily over a month. Brightness is up, background redness maybe slightly down. My derm approved it and I understand why.

r.t: Splitting a bottle with my mom
r.b: My mom and I split a bottle to test it before committing, and we both caved and bought our own within a month. Three drops each morning, wait a minute, then sunscreen. My combination skin looks lit from within by lunch and her sun spots have visibly softened. The savoury smell is real but gone in seconds.

The dropper is my enemy. It dribbles down the bottle neck and I have wasted a noticeable amount of an extremely expensive serum. Results are good, my age spots are lighter after four months, but the packaging needs a redesign.

Interesting timeline for me. Around week three my skin felt noticeably smoother, almost polished, but the brightening took closer to two months to show. Now at month four both are obvious. I apply it to dry skin, wait, then do the rest. One drop less than recommended stopped the slight stickiness.

Finished the entire bottle over three months and I'd describe the change as modest. Slightly brighter, sure. The two dark spots I wanted gone are still there, just softer at the edges. For this money I wanted more. It might work better for others, my skin seems stubborn.

Cleanse, three drops, sunscreen, done. I'm not a routine guy and this survived where everything else got abandoned. Six months in, the sun damage on my temples has faded and colleagues keep saying I look well rested. It tingles the first couple weeks, then your skin gets used to it.

Two months in and the difference shows up mostly in photos, less gray, more even, like a subtle filter. I use three drops, let it dry while I make coffee, then sunscreen. Zero pilling under anything I layer on top.

Six months of daily use and the difference is documented, my wife took monthly photos. The deep crease between my brows is unchanged, fair enough, but the overall tone, the spots, the texture around my eyes, all measurably better.

Years of ingrown marks along my beard line and nothing touched them until this. The 15 percent L-ascorbic acid tingles a little going on but by week six the dark marks were noticeably lighter. I use four drops after shaving, then moisturizer. Wish the bottle was bigger for the price.

Hype is real and I say that as someone who returns most expensive skincare. The 15 percent ascorbic acid with ferulic is the original recipe everyone copies for a reason. Six weeks to visible brightness, three months to fading spots.

Picked it up in November when my skin looked like porridge and the difference by January was significant. Come spring the improvements plateaued, so now I think of it as maintenance rather than a miracle. Four stars, it does what it says, just don't expect it to keep escalating forever.

r.t: The only vitamin C worth it
r.b: Bought this after a pharmacist friend called it the only vitamin C worth the money. The ferulic acid supposedly stabilizes the whole formula and I believe it, my bottle stayed pale yellow to the last drop. Skin is brighter and old razor marks on my jaw faded.

r.t: Four drops covers face and neck
r.b: People complain about the price but nobody mentions how little you need. Four drops, pressed in with palms, does my face and neck. My bottle lasted eleven weeks. Skin looks brighter and the fine lines by my eyes have softened since December. The dropper takes practice, go slow.

Freckles I wanted to keep stayed, sun damage I wanted gone faded, which felt like luck but apparently is just consistent use. Only gripe is the dropper picks up serum on the outside of the stem and gets slippery.

Last year I developed two new sun spots by August. This year, using C E Ferulic every morning since March, none. That's the whole review really. The antioxidant protection claim seemed like marketing until I watched it play out on my own face.

Didn't buy it for this but the redness I get after shaving calms way faster on mornings I use it. The main event is real too, brighter skin and the acne marks on my jaw have faded since November. A bottle lasts me about ten weeks using three drops.

Retinol at night, this in the morning, sunscreen always. That trio simplified my skincare and improved my skin more in six months than the drawer of products I used to rotate through. The ferulic acid keeps this stable to the last drop.

Careful application near my eye area was the surprise win. The whole zone looks less shadowed and my concealer usage has dropped by half. I've been through two bottles now, applied to damp skin every morning before moisturizer. It stings on windburned days, fair warning for Maritime winters.

You can feel that it is a serious formula the moment it goes on, slightly watery, a faint metallic smell, absorbed in under a minute. Ten weeks in and the dullness I blamed on commuting and bad sleep is gone.

Winter here destroys my skin every year, and this was the first one my face stayed bright instead of gray and patchy. I layered it under a heavy ceramide cream every morning and the two never pilled once.

Layered under my moisturizer it causes zero irritation, which shocked me given my history with actives. A gentle tingle the first week, then nothing. Four months later the redness marks from old breakouts have faded and my skin barely reacts to weather swings anymore.

The serum earns its reputation. My complaint is entirely about the amber glass bottle, which I've nearly dropped in the sink a dozen times with wet hands, and the dropper that dispenses unevenly. Put this formula in an airless pump and I'd give six stars. Skin looks great though.

After my third bottle I can say this is not placebo. The hyperpigmentation from an old acne phase is maybe 70 percent gone. I keep it in a dark cabinet and finish each bottle within three months so it never oxidizes on me.

Thirty five years of recess duty gave me a lot of sun damage. My dermatologist suggested this and after four months the mottled patches on my cheeks are dramatically lighter. I ration it carefully, three drops, and a bottle lasts me a full three months. At 68 I didn't expect this much change.

Took a chance despite my reactive skin and mostly won. A mild sting the first ten days, then calm. Tone is more even and a red patch on my chin has quieted. Four stars because sensitive folks should know the adjustment period is real.

Three weeks was all it took for coworkers to ask if I had been on vacation. It is watery, slightly slick from the vitamin E, and settles fast. I keep the amber bottle in a drawer away from light and it stayed the same pale champagne color throughout.

Ordered during a sale and now I understand why people pay full price. The dropper gives exact control, four drops covers my face and neck, and the brightness kicked in around week four. My bottle never turned dark.

A summer of golf left my forehead two shades darker than the rest of my face. Eight weeks of this every morning and the line is basically gone. Genuinely didn't expect that speed. The vitamin E in it seems to keep my skin from drying out too. Solid buy.

Yellow tint to the serum transferred a faint tinge to my white pillowcase the one night I applied it before bed, so keep it to mornings. Otherwise it earns the hype, brighter skin, softer lines, no irritation whatsoever.

For oily skin I expected this to feel heavy, but three drops disappear in seconds and my midday shine is actually less aggressive than before. Old acne marks on my chin faded by around week five. The savory smell is a fair trade.

Smells like hot dog water, I said what everyone thinks. You forgive it quickly because the glow is real and my skin texture is the smoothest it has been in years. Docking a star because a bottle this small should not cost this much.

Results are honestly excellent, my whole face looks more even and awake after two months. The reason for four stars is the finish. It sits slightly oily for a good hour, so I've learned to apply it right when I wake up and do my makeup last. Worth the scheduling dance.

Expensive habit that I keep questioning. My skin is brighter, no argument, but at over two hundred dollars a bottle I expected the deeper lines to budge too, and after eight months they haven't. Buying it again is a coin flip every time.

Four drops every morning under sunscreen, that is my entire routine, and people have started commenting on my skin. It layers beautifully, never pills, and one bottle lasted me just over three months.

By late morning my skin used to look grey and tired no matter how much sleep I got. Since adding this in September there's a steadiness to my skin, it just looks alive all day. Layers fine under my moisturizer and SPF. The smell is like a savoury broth but honestly you stop noticing.

Half a bottle in, my skin tone is noticeably more uniform and the little lines by my eyes catch less light. The texture is almost thinner than water, spreads easily, dries down clean. The savory scent is gone within a minute.

Post-IPL my clinic recommended adding this to protect the investment, and the results have held beautifully for eight months. Pigment has not crept back the way it did after my first round of treatments years ago.

Slight sting on application and a smell I can only call meaty, neither of which stopped me finishing the bottle because the results are legit. Softer lines across my forehead, brighter overall. Just wish the experience matched the price.

There's a distinct sting for the first thirty seconds every morning, and with my sensitive skin I nearly quit in week one. Glad I didn't. Tone is more uniform and the dullness is gone. I buffer with moisturizer on rough days. If your barrier is compromised, patch test first.

At 52 I have tried a lot of antioxidant serums and this is the one that made my esthetician ask what changed. Fine lines around my eyes look softer and the sun damage on my forehead has faded meaningfully since spring.

This replaced three other products in my morning routine. A few drops from the dropper, press it in, done. The vitamin E adds just enough slip that my dry cheeks do not feel stripped, and the glow by week three was noticeable in photos.

Everyone raves so maybe my expectations were unfair. After a full bottle my skin is slightly brighter but the acne marks I bought it for are only marginally better. The smell never stopped bothering me either. It's fine, it works a bit, I just won't repurchase at this price.

Compared it side by side with a cheaper dupe for two months, this on the left cheek, the dupe on the right. Left side won on brightness and the fading of one stubborn spot. Placebo is impossible when your own face is the control.

Pricey, yes, and on my oily T-zone the finish reads slightly greasy until it fully sets. Still, my acne marks faded faster than with anything else I've used and my skin tolerates it with zero irritation. Would love a mattifying version.

Fluorescent office lighting used to expose every bit of unevenness on my skin. Ten weeks of this each morning and even under those awful lights my tone looks consistent. No grey cast, which I've had with other vitamin C serums on deeper skin. It absorbs clean and plays fine with sunscreen.

Can't do the smell, I really tried. It hits like broth every morning and lingered on my skin for close to an hour, and on top of that I got small itchy bumps along my jaw in week two. Returned what was left. Clearly works for others, not for me.

On my fifth bottle. The consistency between batches is perfect, always the same pale yellow, same quick-absorbing feel. Sunspots along my hairline have lightened and my barber noticed. A grown man doesn't expect compliments at the barber.

First bottle turned amber by week eight because I left it on a sunny counter, total rookie mistake. Second bottle lives in a drawer and stayed fresh. The glow is legit and my skin tone is more even, but you have to babysit this stuff. Knocking a star for how finicky it is.

The smell is genuinely strange, like hot dog water, and it took me two weeks to stop noticing it. Results are real though. Redness around my nose calmed down and my tone looked more even by week six. Four stars only because of the scent and the price.

Genuinely brighter skin in under a month, and I'm the least consistent person alive with skincare. Even applying it maybe five mornings a week the change was obvious enough that my roommate asked what I switched.

It stings for about thirty seconds every single morning, even after three months. My skin does look brighter and a little firmer, but with sensitive skin I have to skip days after retinol nights, which slows everything down. Good product, tricky fit for me.

Received a sample from my derm after a consult and finished it in ten days, then bought the full amber bottle. Two months later the sun damage on my left cheek, the driving side, has faded noticeably.

There is a reason every dermatologist I have ever seen name-drops this serum. The L-ascorbic acid concentration is at the top of what skin can actually use and it shows, brighter within a month, an old sunspot on my temple half gone by month three.

Flying leaves my face dull and dehydrated, and UV exposure through cockpit windows is no joke. This has been my morning constant for five months. Skin looks healthier than it has in years and the captain I fly with just ordered his own bottle. Absorbs fast, no residue under sunscreen.

Not going to lie, the price stung more than the serum. But my melasma patch is lighter, my makeup sits better, and I stopped using a separate brightening product. Wish the bottle were bigger for what it costs.

Okay so nobody warned me about the two week purge. Small breakouts along my cheeks, then they cleared and took some of my older marks with them. Now at month three my skin looks better than before, but brace yourself early on.

r.t: The one my clinic insisted on
r.b: Between appointments at my clinic this is the one product they insisted I keep using at home. Brightness holds steady, the fine lines on my forehead look softer, and one bottle carries me about three months using four drops a day.

Three days in and my chin erupted in clogged pores that took two weeks to settle. I know this formula is beloved but the base is too rich for my oily skin. Tried it twice more with the same result. The Silymarin version might've been the smarter pick for me. Returned it.

Melasma across my upper lip had resisted everything short of lasers. Six months of this every morning under a mineral SPF and it is faint enough that I skip concealer most days. Nothing else changed in my routine, so the credit goes here.

Turned orange on me within six weeks, even stored in a cool dark drawer with the cap tight. At this price oxidation that fast is unacceptable. The two weeks it was fresh my skin did look brighter, which somehow makes it more frustrating.

My dermatologist pushed me toward this for two years before I caved. She was right. The 15 percent L-ascorbic acid is no joke, my forehead lines look softer and my overall tone is brighter. The amber glass bottle also keeps it stable longer than the cheaper serums I tried.
Wish I could give it four and a half. Brightness, check. Softer lines on my forehead, check. But the bottle lasted me barely ten weeks using the recommended drops, and at this price that math hurts.

Honestly it took almost two months before I noticed anything, so patience is required. Now at month four my post-blemish marks fade way faster than they used to. Slightly tacky finish for the first few minutes, which bugs me under makeup.

Age spots on my cheekbones had been multiplying for a decade. Ten months of this every morning and two of them are gone completely while the rest have softened. My only regret isn't starting at 40 instead of 61.

A little goes a long way, so despite the sticker shock a bottle lasts me a full season. Glow is real by week three. It does leave the faintest tacky feel that my bangs stick to at the gym, hence four stars.

r.t: Asked if I had work done
r.b: I was skeptical that any serum could justify this price. Then a colleague asked if I had something done. Three months of daily use, five drops each morning, and the crepiness on my cheeks has genuinely improved. Refilling forever.

Works, but so does my old drugstore vitamin C at a fifth of the price, at least on my skin. The finish is a touch oily for me and I didn't see a dramatic difference by bottle end. Maybe my expectations were inflated by the hype.

Everyone talks about the smell and yes, it is odd for a few seconds, but nobody warned me how fast the results come. Brighter by week two, smoother by week five. I store it in its box away from light and the formula stayed stable all winter.

Ran out for two weeks between bottles and watched my skin slowly go back to dull, which is the most convincing review I can give. Four stars only because the price forces those gaps in the first place.

Took this on vacation and the dropper cap leaked in my toiletry bag, lost probably a week's worth. At home it's fine as long as it stays upright. The serum itself deserves the hype, my dry skin looks luminous and the fine lines around my mouth are less obvious. Just pack it carefully.

Sun damage from thirty years in Arizona is no small thing, and this is the first product that visibly lightened the mottled patches on my cheeks. My derm confirmed the improvement at my annual check. I apply it religiously before SPF 50.

r.t: Worth every penny, four months in
r.b: Been using this every morning for four months now. Four drops after cleansing, wait a minute, then moisturizer and SPF. The watery texture sinks in fast and my sun spots from last summer have visibly faded. Yes it smells odd, sort of salty, but that disappears in seconds.

Never thought a serum could make me look forward to mornings. Four drops, a minute to sink in, then SPF. The hyperpigmentation on my cheekbones from years of skipped sunscreen has faded to almost nothing since I started in early spring.
Under makeup this behaves perfectly, no pilling, no balling up with primer, and by week four my foundation looked better because the skin under it looked better.

Gifted a bottle by my sister who works at a medspa, and I finished it convinced. My combination skin drank it up with no pilling under SPF, and by the end my chin was clear of the lingering marks from winter breakouts.

First impressions matter and this delivered in week one, the persistent dry patch on my left cheek that laughed at everything else simply faded. The texture is dense but spreads thin and even. I follow with nothing at night, it is enough on its own. Already planning the repurchase.

Perimenopause turned my formerly normal skin unpredictable, dry one week and reactive the next. This has been the steadying force for eight months. Whatever my hormones are doing, one pump at night keeps my face even and calm. The cholesterol-heavy ratio apparently suits older skin and mine agrees completely.

For mature skin this is close to perfect. The cholesterol-heavy formula makes sense for skin like mine that lost its bounce, and after roughly eight weeks my face feels padded again instead of papery. My only note is to warm it between fingers first, it spreads much easier that way.

Swim four mornings a week and chlorine strips my face raw. This is the only moisturizer that rebuilds it by the next day. Applied after every post-pool shower and again at night. Six months in, no more tight burning feeling after practice. My teammates have started asking what changed.

r.t: Worth it, barely, but worth it
r.b: Pricey but I keep coming back because nothing at half the cost performs like this. It smoothed the dehydration lines on my forehead in about three weeks and sits perfectly under my tinted SPF. I dock a star because the bottle is small and I resent how quickly I fall in love with expensive things.

r.t: Give it ten minutes before makeup
r.b: Beautiful cream with one workflow issue, it needs a solid ten minutes to fully settle before foundation or things get patchy. On weekends when I'm bare faced it's flawless, my dry patches are gone and my cheeks look plush. Weekday mornings require planning. Still repurchasing, just noting it.

Took about a month before I saw anything beyond basic moisture, and I nearly gave up at week two. Glad I stuck it out. The crepiness on my cheeks softened noticeably by week five and my skin stopped drinking three layers of serum to feel normal. Slow starter, strong finisher.

Retinol users, this is the buffer you want. I apply it fifteen minutes after tretinoin and my usual week two peel simply didn't happen this cycle. The scent is faint to me, more plant than perfume. My derm confirmed it will not interfere with the retinoid. Excellent.

Three weeks in I noticed little white bumps under my eyes and along my cheekbones that I've never had before. Stopped using it and they took over a month to clear. My esthetician said rich creams do this to some people. Clearly gorgeous formula for the right skin, mine wasn't it.

r.t: Sceptic to loyalist in one bottle
r.b: Skeptical at first because the marketing around lipid ratios sounded like nonsense to me. Six weeks later the persistent rough patch on my jawline that survived three other creams is gone. It goes on thick, warms into the skin, and my face feels cushioned rather than coated. I stand corrected.

Too much cream for my daytime routine even in a dry January, it sat heavy under sunscreen. As a night cream though it's excellent, especially over retinol, my skin wakes up calm and cushioned. Half a pump is all I need. Four stars for being a specialist rather than an all-rounder.

r.t: The brand earned my trust again
r.b: Been using SkinCeuticals vitamin C for years but their moisturizers never tempted me until this one. It fixed the rough patches by my ears that I assumed were permanent, took maybe three weeks. Dense texture, spreads easily, faint botanical smell that vanishes. Now the two products bookend my whole routine.

Started using it after my dermatologist mentioned the lipid ratio research behind it. Results are real, less tightness, fewer flakes, smoother texture by week four. The caveat is that in summer it feels like too much for me, so it becomes a winter-only product, which makes the price harder to justify year round.

At 63 my skin drinks whatever I give it and stays thirsty. Not with this. One pump at bedtime and I wake up with skin that feels padded, for lack of a better word. Fine lines on my cheeks are less etched after three months. The scent is odd for thirty seconds, then gone.

Three bottles in and I have zero interest in trying anything else. My cheeks used to feel tight an hour after cleansing, now they stay comfortable all day. I pair it with C E Ferulic in the morning and the two together made my skin look genuinely healthy for the first time in years.

Halifax winters are a damp cold that gets into your bones and apparently your face. This cream kept my skin comfortable through the whole season, no chapped patches along my jaw for the first time in years. It goes on thick, absorbs in a minute, and one bottle took me from December to March.

r.t: Only thing that calmed the itch
r.b: Nothing else calmed the itchy tight feeling I get every February, and I tried five different barrier creams this year, this one did it in four nights flat.

Minus forty walks to work all winter and my face didn't crack once. That's never happened. The 2:4:2 lipid ratio sounded like marketing until I lived through a Yukon February with intact skin. A little melts in fast and doesn't sit greasy under a balaclava. Expensive and completely justified.

Works, but be warned the pump gets airy in the last fifth of the bottle and you end up shaking it like ketchup. Formula-wise it is the best barrier cream I've used, cracked winter skin healed in about a week and stayed healed. I just wish the last 10 ml were easier to extract.

Expensive, yes, and I hesitate every time I reorder. But nothing else keeps my skin comfortable through an Edmonton February, and a little truly does go far, one pump does my whole face and neck. If it were 20 dollars cheaper I'd buy it without thinking. Four stars for the wallet damage only.

Our furnace runs six months a year and my skin usually pays the price by January. This year my face stayed comfortable straight through. I'm 58 with dry skin and this replaced both my day cream and my sleeping mask. The pump gets sluggish near the end, tip it upside down overnight.

Second winter with this cream and it remains the only thing standing between my face and the parking lot wind tunnel at work. Absorbs fully before I leave the bathroom, never pills under sunscreen, and the slight herbal smell has honestly grown on me. Buy it when it goes on promo and stock up.

My dermatologist recommended this during my accutane course when everything else stung or just disappeared into the desert of my face. It's the first cream that actually held moisture in overnight. Thick but spreads easily, no fragrance issues, and the pump keeps it hygienic. Cost hurts on a student budget but nothing else worked.

Winter in Calgary destroys my face, the dry wind cracks the skin around my mouth every year. Not this year. Two pumps at night, one in the morning under SPF, and by early December the usual rough patches never showed up. It smells a bit like lavender and something fatty, which I don't love, but the results shut me up.

Decent but I expected fireworks at this price and got a reliable candle. It moisturizes well, no irritation, no pilling, but after three months I can't point to a single dramatic change beyond soft skin, which cheaper creams also give me. If money is no object, sure. Mine is an object.

r.t: Repurchased twice, that says it all
r.b: Repurchased twice now, and I am ruthless about cutting products that coast. My barometer is how my skin handles a week of skiing, and this year I came home without the usual windburn peel. Goes on like a rich balm, finishes like a normal cream. The airless pump uses up cleanly to the last week.

Spend most winter weekends on the lake and used to come home with a scorched red face. A layer of this before heading out and another at night changed everything this season. It's thick enough to actually protect but doesn't feel like grease. My brother borrowed it once and never gave it back.

Love that it comes in an airless pump instead of a jar, I refuse to buy jar moisturizers anymore after learning how fast actives degrade. The cream itself is a rich, faintly herbal-smelling cushion that fixed my winter cheek flaking in ten days. Minnesota winters are no joke and neither is this.
Rich without being greasy, absorbs in about ninety seconds, and kept my face comfortable through minus 30 windchill walks to work, second bottle already.

If your skin is truly dry, this is the one. If you are oily, walk away, it will be far too much. I'm firmly in camp desert and it erased the ashy look I'd get by mid-afternoon. Only gripe is the pump gets stubborn near the end and I know there is product left in there I can't reach.

Smells like a herbalist's shop for the first thirty seconds, that is my one real complaint. The performance is hard to argue with, my dehydration lines plumped up within two weeks and it never once pilled under my vitamin C in the morning. By now I barely notice the scent, but it is there.

r.t: Finally got through winter without flaking
r.b: My derm recommended this after I complained about constant flaking around my nose every January. It is a thick cream but it sinks in within a minute or two, no greasy film. By week three the flaking was gone and my foundation stopped catching on dry patches. The airless pump dispenses exactly the right amount. Worth the splurge for me.

Consultant life, four flights a week, and my cheeks used to be flaky by Thursday. One pump morning and night fixed what three cheaper creams couldn't. It has a faint corn-like smell that vanishes in a minute. The airless pump survives being thrown in a carry-on, which matters more than you'd think.

You need barely a pea-sized pump for the whole face, so don't be put off by the small bottle. Mine lasted three and a half months of nightly use. Skin feels rebuilt rather than coated, and the rough texture on my chin resolved by the one month mark. Genuinely impressive formula.

Every fall I start this up again like clockwork, usually mid-October when the furnace comes on. Within a week my skin transitions without the usual angry tight phase. I have recommended it to three coworkers and all of them repurchased. The pump design keeps it fresh to the last drop.

Great under makeup, which shocked me for something this rich. I let it sink in for five minutes, then foundation glides on and does not cling to the dry spots by my nose anymore. My mother borrowed it for a wedding weekend and immediately bought her own bottle.

Fine, I admit it, my daughter was right about this one. She put me onto it after my usual cream stopped coping with my thyroid-related dryness. Six weeks of nightly use and my face no longer feels stretched over my cheekbones by morning. The pump is tidy, the cream is rich, the results are real.

Menopause wrecked my skin barrier almost overnight, everything itched and burned. The 2 percent ceramides and 4 percent cholesterol ratio in this actually rebuilt things. It took a solid month, not overnight, but the itching stopped first, then the rough texture, then the dullness. Pricey and worth every dollar in my case.

Recovery from microneedling used to mean three red, tight days. With this, barely one. My clinic suggested it and now it's my everyday night cream between treatments. Melts in within a minute, one pump covers face and neck. Boring in the best possible way, my skin just stays calm.

Genuinely surprised. I'm 63 and have tried every department store cream since the eighties. This is the first one where strangers commented, a pharmacist asked what I use. Skin looks padded and calm, the deep lines are still there but everything around them looks healthier. Two pumps nightly, one every morning.

A little goes a long way, which softens the price per use math considerably. One pump covers my face and neck with a bit left for the backs of my hands. Four months on the same bottle. Skin is calmer, smoother, and my winter eczema patches beside my nose never returned this year.

Prone to eczema flare-ups on my cheeks every autumn, like clockwork. First year in a decade it didn't happen, and the only change was adding this in September. My GP was pleasantly surprised. It's rich without being occlusive and never stings even on freshly irritated skin. Genuine barrier repair.

At 58, my skin just stopped holding moisture on its own. This cream changed the texture of my whole face in about a month, softer, less crosshatching on my cheeks. I use it morning and night, and one bottle lasts me around ten weeks. The airless pump means no scooping cream out of a jar with fingers, hallelujah.

It melts in on contact, which I didn't expect from something that looks like frosting coming out of the pump. No residue on my pillow, no shine at my hairline. My fine lines around the eyes look softer after two months. The 48 ml lasts longer than the size suggests.

Six weeks in and the crosshatch texture on my cheeks has visibly relaxed. I take a photo of my face monthly, same light and angle, and the difference between March and May was obvious even to my husband. Two pumps at night is my sweet spot. Nothing pilled over it, ever.

r.t: Better than expected, scent is odd
r.b: Honestly wasn't expecting much beyond a fancy price tag, but my barrier was wrecked from overdoing acids and this fixed it in about two weeks. The smell is the only drawback, sort of herbal and waxy at the same time. It dissipates quickly but I notice it every single application.

r.t: Face and neck in one pump
r.b: One pump covers my face and neck if I warm it in my palms first. My neck was the real test, crepey and always irritated by fragranced creams, and this smoothed it without any reaction. Eight weeks in the improvement is obvious in photos. Buying a second bottle just for my mother.

The pump sputters and spits half doses about a third of the time, which drives me nuts at this price point. The cream itself is genuinely nice, my skin felt smoother within a couple of weeks, but I fight with the dispenser every morning. Three stars until they fix the hardware.

Used it nightly for two months before writing this. Fine lines around my mouth are softer, the crepey texture on my cheeks is smoother, and I haven't had a single dry patch since starting. It plays nicely over serums and never pills, even when I'm impatient and layer too fast.

Cannot get behind the smell, full stop. It reads medicinal and fatty to me and it lingers just long enough to bother me every night. I also developed two tiny milia under my eyes by week three. Texture and moisture were genuinely good, but between the scent and the bumps I gave it away.

The 2:4:2 ratio sounded like marketing until I read the research my derm sent me. Whatever the mechanism, my skin is measurably less flaky and the fine lines around my mouth have softened over two months. It absorbs faster than creams half as rich. Genuine science in a pump bottle.

r.t: Slow burn but it convinced me
r.b: On the fence for the first three weeks because at altitude my skin is a special kind of parched and this seemed merely fine. Around week four something shifted, smoother forehead, no more flaking eyebrows. I still think the pump wastes a little product when it sputters, but the cream earned its fourth star.

Bought this after a facialist raved about the 2:4:2 lipid ratio. It does what it promises, my cheeks stopped feeling tight by the second week, and it layers beautifully under sunscreen. Knocking a star because the price for 48 ml stings and I go through a pump and a half per use in winter.

Owned this for a full year now so here's the honest seasonal report. October through April it's unbeatable, my face survived an Edmonton winter genuinely comfortable. May onward it's too much, I switch to a gel and save this pump for after-sun evenings. Buy it in fall, thank me later.

r.t: Too heavy for my combo skin
r.b: Not for me at all. My cheeks liked it but my T-zone revolted, clogged pores across my forehead within two weeks even using a single pump at night only. I get that it is designed for dry, mature skin, but I wish I had known how occlusive it feels before spending this much. Returned what was left.

Post-menopausal skin in a desert climate is a brutal combination and this handles it. I apply on damp skin after a hyaluronic serum and stay comfortable through 40 degree days in air conditioning. Texture improvement showed around week five. My aesthetician spotted the change before I said anything.

Heavy. Too heavy for anyone with functioning oil glands, in my opinion. I bought it for winter and even then it left me shiny by noon. My mother has classic dry mature skin and it looks incredible on her, so I handed it over. Know your skin type before spending this much.

After my Fraxel session my derm told me to use something bland and lipid-heavy while healing. This was gentler than the plain drugstore cream I tried first, no sting on raw skin, and the tight shiny feeling eased within days. I kept using it after healing because my skin has honestly never looked better.

r.t: Fixed my patches, mind the amount
r.b: Dry patches around my nostrils and between my brows disappeared within two weeks, which no ceramide cream from the drugstore ever managed. Word of caution, more isn't better. When I got generous with three pumps I woke up with a slightly congested chin. One pump, thin layer, perfection.

This cream saved my face after I got greedy with glycolic acid and burned my barrier. Everything stung, even water. Two weeks of this morning and night, nothing else except sunscreen, and my skin calmed completely. It has earned a permanent spot even now that things are healed.

r.t: Like a lipid smoothie for your face
r.b: The texture reminds me of softened butter that melts on contact, thick out of the pump but it spreads thin and disappears. I sandwich it around tretinoin nights and my peeling stopped almost completely within ten days. My esthetician noticed the difference before I told her I switched.

Since starting tretinoin last fall my skin was in open rebellion until this arrived. I do a thin layer before and after on heavy nights. Peeling stopped, redness faded, and I kept every bit of the retinoid progress. The fatty acids and cholesterol do the repair work while the tret does the renovation.

I broke out along my chin the first two weeks, small closed comedones that I never get normally. Backed off to every other night and it settled, and to be fair my skin does feel less tight now. I want to love it given what I paid, but I am watching my chin like a hawk.

r.t: Works great, smells like a health store
r.b: There is a scent, and nobody warned me. Kind of herbal, kind of like plant oils, definitely noticeable for the first minute. Past that, the cream itself is outstanding, my flaky chin cleared up in under two weeks and makeup sits better. If you are scent-sensitive, sample first.

Was gifted a sample at a medspa appointment and used it for five nights. That was enough. Bought the full size before the sample ran out. My cheeks stopped looking gray and tired, and blush sits on smooth skin now instead of catching on dry bits. No irritation whatsoever on my reactive skin.

Ran a two month split-face test against a drugstore ceramide moisturizer because I'm that person. Honestly, the difference was smaller than the price gap suggests. This side felt slightly more supple, looked marginally smoother. If money's no object, sure. Mine has objections.

r.t: The one my skin waits for
r.b: This is the first moisturizer that actually repaired my barrier instead of just sitting on top of it. I use one pump at night over my retinol and the stinging I used to get is gone. Skin looks plumper, less crepey around my jaw after about six weeks. The scent is herbal and takes getting used to, but it fades fast.

Used my wife's stash for a week when my face was peeling after a beach trip and got caught because my skin suddenly looked better than hers. Now we each have a pump on the counter. It settles in fast for something this rich and doesn't smell like a candle store, which I appreciate.

r.t: Calmed my reactive skin right down
r.b: I have rosacea-prone skin and most rich creams make me flush. This one is loaded with ceramides and cholesterol instead of fragrance-heavy fillers, and my redness actually settled after a couple of weeks of nightly use. No stinging, no clogged pores. The pump keeps everything hygienic, which I appreciate.

Layered over my retinol as the last step, this stopped the dryness and irritation that made me quit retinoids twice before. It is thick enough to buffer but never blocks the active from working, my texture kept improving. Two months in, the corners of my mouth no longer crack in the morning.

r.t: Cheeks love it, T-zone tolerates it
r.b: Combination skin here, so I use it on cheeks and jaw only and skip my nose and forehead. Used that way it is excellent, no more flaky cheekbones and my redness is down. Applied all over it was too rich and I got a couple of small bumps. Zone application is the trick.

Started this last spring and my photos from back then are startling now. The horizontal lines on my forehead are half as deep, and my skin bounces back when I press it, which it didn't do at 61. I stay religious about sunscreen over it since even low-dose retinol deserves respect.

Seventy this year and still vain, thankfully. This serum has given my cheeks back some spring and faded the blotchiness that crept in over the last decade. My daughter applies it for me on days my hands are stiff, and even she noticed the change. We call it my expensive habit.

Nothing for seven weeks, then suddenly a coworker asked if I'd changed my makeup, then my mom, then a barista. Something turns a corner around the two month mark. Firmer, more even, kind of lit up. One pump twice daily, layered before moisturizer. Trust the process on this one.

Very good serum, real results on the fine lines around my mouth after about ten weeks. My only complaints are the price, which stings at renewal, and that the last few pumps sputter and spray unevenly. I'll repurchase, probably during a sale.

Works, genuinely. Cheeks firmer, tone brighter, fine lines quieter after three months. But at two pumps twice daily the bottle empties in about six weeks, and the cost per month is hard to swallow. I have scaled back to one pump at night and the results are holding.

Turned fifty this spring and two separate people guessed forty three, which has literally never happened before this serum. Eight months of use, morning and night under moisturizer. The texture is a smooth gel with a slight tack that disappears once the next layer goes on. Buying it forever, quietly.
One pump covers my face and neck if I move fast, and after three months of firmer, brighter skin it has become the single product I'd never cut from the budget.

Everything firming I tried before triggered a flush. This hasn't, not once in five months. My cheeks are noticeably tighter and the burning feeling I get from most actives simply never happened. I apply it to fully dry skin and wait a minute before moisturizer, as my derm suggested.

r.t: Third product I tried, last one
r.b: Went through a peptide serum and a pricier growth factor brand before this one. Neither did what this has done for the crepiness on my cheeks in five months. The SYN-AKE peptide sounds gimmicky, snake venom mimic, sure, but my skin doesn't care about marketing and it's visibly firmer at 60.

Perfectly pleasant serum that did perfectly average things for my skin. Slightly smoother texture after two months, maybe a touch brighter. For this money I wanted more than maybe. The quick-drying gel and the precise pump are the best parts.

Compared honestly against a growth factor serum costing nearly double, this held its own and then some. Skin is firmer at the cheekbones, tone is more even, and the metered pump wastes nothing. I apply it after my vitamin C in the morning with no conflict.

Week twelve is where I finally saw it, the parentheses around my mouth looking softer in my car mirror of all places. It's a light gel, one pump morning and night, dries down in a couple minutes. There's low-dose retinol in it but I've had zero irritation. Slow and steady product.

Through an Edmonton February this needed a rich cream over top or my skin felt stripped by morning. Spring and fall it is perfect alone under SPF. The firming earned it a permanent spot regardless. Just know what it is, a treatment step, despite a price that suggests it should do everything.
